papers.title: Inflammaging and Cellular Senescence in Postmenopausal Depression: Linking Estrogen Deficiency, Immune Dysregulation, and Brain Aging.
papers.abstract: Postmenopausal depression is clinically heterogeneous and cannot be explained by estrogen deficiency alone. We propose a conceptual, testable neuroimmune-aging model in which endocrine decline may interact with inflammaging, cellular senescence, and brain vulnerability in a subset of women. The evidentiary base is uneven: direct studies of senescence in well-phenotyped postmenopausal depression are lacking; clinical endocrine data come mainly from perimenopausal depression; molecular-senescence findings come from late-life depression or general major depressive disorder; and most cellular and brain mechanisms are supported by aging or preclinical models. Reduced estrogen signaling may weaken immune homeostasis, whereas peripheral cytokines or senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors could influence vascular and neural interfaces, glia, neurotransmitter metabolism, stress signaling, mitochondrial function, and neuroplasticity. These pathways are candidate mediators, not established causal mechanisms. Clinically established care remains diagnosis-based antidepressant treatment, evidence-based management of vasomotor and sleep symptoms, and individualized menopausal hormone therapy for appropriate candidates. Anti-inflammatory, microbiome-based, and senescence-targeted strategies remain investigational; no senolytic or senomorphic is approved for depression or menopause-related mood symptoms. Prospective studies integrating menopausal staging, prespecified confounders, senescence biomarkers, neuroimaging, and mood outcomes are needed to test this model.

papers.title: Atrial Flutter in Adolescence Due to Invasive Cardiac Lipoma: A Rare Presentation.
papers.abstract: Primary cardiac tumors are rare, with lipomas comprising ∼10% of benign cases. Although typically asymptomatic, invasive variants may infiltrate myocardium and generate significant arrhythmogenic substrate. A 14-year-old previously healthy male patient presented with atrial flutter and was found to have a large, infiltrative lipomatous mass involving the right atrium, right ventricle, and tricuspid valve. Biopsy and partial debulking confirmed invasive cardiac lipoma, but complete excision was precluded by extensive myocardial infiltration. Despite antiarrhythmic therapy, he developed recurrent atrial flutter and ventricular dysfunction. Electrophysiology study identified a cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent flutter that was successfully ablated; however, a second tumor-associated circuit was not amenable to ablation because of anatomical barriers. Sinus rhythm was restored with cardioversion and amiodarone with subsequent recovery of ventricular function. Invasive cardiac lipomas present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, often requiring multimodal imaging, multidisciplinary management, aggressive rhythm control, and consideration of cardiac transplantation in select patients.

papers.title: Neurocosmetics Under Scrutiny: A Critical Appraisal of the Evidence Base and a Measurement Framework for Substantiating Skin-Brain Claims.
papers.abstract: The skin is a peripheral neuroimmunoendocrine organ that communicates bidirectionally with the central nervous system, providing a plausible biological basis for topical products intended to influence cutaneous sensation, physiological stress responses, or emotional well-being. However, evidence supporting neurocosmetic claims remains heterogeneous, and biological mechanisms, peripheral physiological changes, and central or subjective outcomes are frequently conflated. Although previous reviews have described neurocosmetic ingredients, mechanisms, products, and neurophysiological assessment methods, an operational framework linking each claim type to its corresponding burden of proof remains lacking. This review critically evaluates the available evidence and proposes a unified, claim-centred framework that organises neurocosmetic claims into three tiers-local cutaneous, peripheral physiological, and central or emotional-and aligns each tier with the evidence level required for substantiation. It also identifies suitable study designs and objective endpoints, mapping psychophysiological and neurophysiological methods-including salivary cortisol, heart-rate variability, electrodermal activity, facial electromyography, EEG, fMRI, and MEG-to the specific types of claims they best support. Selected studies are then evaluated according to the correspondence between the claim, study design, comparator, and endpoint. Within the context of European cosmetic regulation, we argue that stronger claims require correspondingly stronger and more specific evidence. Current evidence most clearly supports local cutaneous effects, whereas many peripheral physiological and central or emotional effects require better-controlled and adequately powered human studies. The proposed framework is intended to support more transparent, falsifiable, and proportionate substantiation of skin-brain claims.

papers.title: Predicting Motor Recovery in the Subacute Phase of Stroke: The Role of Passive Motor Task and Electroencephalogram Brain Networks.
papers.abstract: In stroke rehabilitation, the identification of reliable prognostic factors remains a challenge for effective rehabilitation strategies. This study investigates which motor task has the most predictive utility based on electroencephalogram (EEG) characteristics during the subacute phase of stroke. Data were collected from 10 subacute stroke patients performed different motor tasks (passive, robotic movement; active, voluntary execution; motor imagery [MI]) and a nonmotor task (No-Go) at two time points: T1, approximately 3 weeks after stroke onset, and T2, 2 months after T1. EEG power and network characteristics were extracted for each task, and prognostic models were constructed with nested leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation (CV) to avoid information leakage. Our findings show that the passive task model produced the strongest internal predictive performance across all task conditions (root-mean-square error 5.94; nested LOSO CV-R2, 0.91), with ipsilesional/contralesional motor area event-related desynchronization, characteristic path length, and clustering coefficient emerging as consistent prognostic features. The passive task also showed less overactivation and hyperconnectivity in the early subacute phase relative to the active and MI tasks. This performance advantage was replicated across six analytic procedures (2 feature-selection × 3 regression strategies), supporting the robustness of the task comparison within the present dataset. These findings suggest that EEG features obtained during a robot-assisted passive task may provide exploratory prognostic utility for motor recovery prediction in the early subacute phase of stroke.Impact StatementThe passive task may offer a practical approach for assessing neurophysiological markers of recovery potential, supporting the development of more personalized rehabilitation strategies and earlier prognostic evaluation in stroke patients.

papers.title: Prevalence and Association of Undiagnosed Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Perioperative Neurocognitive Disorders, and Quality of Life After Brain Surgery.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is increasingly seen in neurosurgical patients and can impact patient outcomes. There is a paucity of literature regarding the OSA burden in the neurosurgical population and its link with perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) and quality of life (QoL). Our primary objective was to evaluate the OSA prevalence in patients undergoing brain surgery and, secondarily, to assess its association with postoperative complications of emergence delirium (ED), postoperative delirium (POD), and delayed neurocognitive recovery, sleep, respiratory events, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, hospital stay, 28-day QoL, and functional recovery. This secondary analysis of a primary study was conducted among adults undergoing elective brain surgery over a 14-month period. Patients were screened preoperatively for undiagnosed OSA using the STOP-BANG questionnaire. ED was evaluated using the Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale, POD using the Confusion Assessment Method and PND using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Sleep, Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE) scores and QoL were also assessed. The prevalence of OSA was 31.5% (117/371). OSA was not associated with PND, except at baseline (P = 0.039). Similarly, OSA was not associated with sleep disturbances, respiratory complications, or ICU admission. Higher STOP-BANG scores correlated with longer hospital stays (P = 0.042), lower GOSE scores (P = 0.006), and worse cumulative QoL scores (P = 0.018). Approximately one-third of patients undergoing brain surgery had undiagnosed OSA. Higher STOP-BANG scores were associated with preoperative cognitive impairment. Although OSA was not associated with sleep disturbances or PND, higher STOP-BANG scores were associated with unfavorable functional recovery and poorer QoL 28 days after surgery.

papers.title: Cortical Network Alterations and Treatment-Induced Reorganization in Panic Disorder: A Longitudinal High-Density EEG Study.
papers.abstract: Although neuroimaging has identified network abnormalities in panic disorder (PD), the rapid and transient nature of panic symptoms highlights the need for methods with high temporal resolution. This study used high-density electroencephalography (EEG) to investigate cortical network alterations in PD and explore their potential as translational biomarkers. This longitudinal study enrolled 52 drug-naïve PD patients and 43 healthy controls. High-density (128-channel) resting-state EEG was collected from both groups at baseline, with repeat assessments performed in PD patients after 6 weeks of venlafaxine treatment. Source-level functional connectivity and network topology were analyzed to characterize cortical network features. Support vector machine (SVM) was used to evaluate the discriminative potential of baseline network features. At baseline, PD patients showed frequency-specific network disruptions, with enhanced connectivity within and between the default mode network, frontoparietal network, and dorsal attention network in the α band, but reduced connectivity across multiple networks in the θ and δ bands. Graph theory analysis revealed decreased global efficiency and increased characteristic path length in the α and δ bands. The SVM classifier achieved 86.32% accuracy in distinguishing PD patients from controls. Following treatment, clinical improvement was accompanied by network reorganization, including increased global efficiency and small-worldness in the α band, and enhanced fronto-temporal connectivity in the δ band. Exploratory brain-behavior associations did not survive FDR correction. PD is characterized by frequency-specific cortical network disruptions that show dynamic reorganization following treatment. These findings highlight the potential of EEG-derived network features as candidate markers for PD identification and treatment monitoring.

GluN3 Subunits of NMDA Receptors are Functionally Expressed in Neurons of the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus of Mice.
papers.abstract: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is the principal circadian clock in the mammalian brain. This structure is synchronized to the light-dark cycle through the retinohypothalamic tract (RHT), which releases glutamate onto the ventral SCN. Glutamate activates N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) and α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA)/kainate receptors, increasing intracellular calcium levels and activating signaling pathways required for light-induced phase shifts. NMDA receptors are composed of different subunits: GluN1, GluN2 (A-D), and GluN3 (A-B). However, it remains unknown whether GluN3-containing NMDA receptors are present in SCN neurons and, if so, whether these subunits are functional and contribute to glutamatergic signaling in the ventral SCN. To address these questions, we used immunohistochemistry to assess GluN3 expression in the ventral and dorsal SCN and whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in the ventral SCN to monitor stimulus-evoked asynchronous excitatory postsynaptic currents (aEPSCs) following repetitive electrical stimulation of the RHT. Analyses of GluN3A and GluN3B expression disclosed higher levels of both subunits, as well as higher numbers of immunopositive particles during daytime vs nighttime in the ventral SCN. In contrast, the dorsal SCN showed a reversed pattern, with higher GluN3A expression during the night. Electrophysiological experiments showed that CGP-78608, an antagonist of the GluN1 glycine-binding site and a positive allosteric modulator of GluN3A-mediated responses, reduced the frequency and amplitude of aEPSCs during daytime, but not during nighttime. Moreover, bath application of glycine, which activates the GluN3 subunit, increased the frequency and amplitude of aEPSCs during the day, but not during the night. Finally, the antagonist 5,7-Dichlorokynurenic acid (DCKA) completely abolished the remaining aEPSCs at both times analyzed, further supporting the contribution of GluN3-containing NMDA receptors to these responses. Our findings support that GluN3 subunits are expressed in both ventral and dorsal SCN neurons and that GluN3-containing receptors are functionally involved in the glutamatergic signaling of the ventral SCN, depending on the circadian time (day vs night, at least).

papers.title: Quantitative proteomics uncovers a role for REVEILLE8-like clock genes in osmotic and salt stress response in Arabidopsis.
papers.abstract: The plant circadian clock governs the precise regulation of plant developmental and environmental responses within a 24 h photoperiod. Consisting of a series of interconnected transcription factor moderated feedback loops, each operating at specific times of day within the photoperiod, more than 30% of Arabidopsis genes show circadian regulation. REVEILLE (RVE) genes exhibit highest expression in the afternoon, and act as activators of afternoon-expressed clock genes, including TOC1 and PRR5. Specifically, RVE4, 6 and 8 have been identified as regulators of both plant growth and development, along with temperature responses. Previous work using Arabidopsis has implicated soybean RVE8-like proteins in drought responses, however, there remains a lack of understanding of how these RVEs control abiotic stress responses, particularly relating to proteome-level regulation. Here, using quantitative proteomics, we resolve how the rve4 6 8 proteome responds to osmotic and salt stress at end-of-day and end-of-night timepoints. Our results indicate that rve4 6 8 plants have substantially altered regulation of proteins related to osmotic stress, photosynthesis and phenylpropanoid metabolism, particularly at end-of-day. Further, we resolve new drought-responsive targets impacted by the loss of RVE4, 6, and 8 that are involved in fatty acid metabolism and abscission. Overall, our data provide a new resource for understanding how RVE8-like proteins impact plant drought-like responses, offering opportunities for future chronoculture-informed breeding of climate-resilient crops.

papers.title: Impact of AI-assisted Sedation on Early Cognitive Function and Sleep Quality in the Elderly Undergoing GI Endoscopy.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effect of ENDOANGLE-assisted sedation by the "ENDOANGLE" on early cognitive function and sleep quality in elderly patients after gastrointestinal endoscopy. A total of 180 patients (aged 65-80, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-III) scheduled for sedated endoscopy were randomly assigned to an ENDOANGLE-assisted group (AI group, n = 87) or a control group (C group, n = 85). We recorded procedural metrics (induction time, resuscitation time, directional force recovery, propofol dose), Ramsay scores, vital signs, and adverse events. Sleep quality was evaluated using the St. Mary's Hospital Sleep Questionnaire (SMH score) and actigraphy (Honor Band 6) at baseline (T0), on bowel preparation day (T1), post-procedure evening (T2), and 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days post-procedure. Cognitive function was assessed with the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Verbal Fluency Test (VFT), Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Trail Making Tests A and B (TMT-A/B) before examination (T1), 30 minutes post-emergence (T2), and at 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days postprocedure. The resuscitation time and directional force recovery in the AI group were significantly shorter than those in the C group. The induction time and total amount of propofol administered during examinations were comparable between the two groups. There were no statistically significant differences in cognitive test scores across time points between the two groups; however, on the day of enema administration, SMH scores in both groups were significantly lower than baseline. However, at night, the AI group had significantly higher SMH scores compared to the C group. On the third and seventh days after surgery, there were no differences in SMH scores from baseline within each group or between the two groups, and the sleep monitoring results from the Honor Band were largely consistent with the SMH scoring system. AI-assisted sedation with ENDOANGEL improved sleep quality on the procedure night in elderly patients but did not affect cognitive function or sleep at 3 and 7 days postoperatively. This early benefit may stem from optimized propofol titration, which reduces acute sleep disruption. The transient effect and unchanged cognition underscore the safety and limited duration of AI impact. Future research should explore mechanisms and whether early sleep improvement enhances overall recovery. AI-assisted sedation showed no difference in early cognitive function compared to conventional sedation, despite both groups experiencing transient post-procedural cognitive changes. The ENDOANGEL system can improve sleep quality in elderly patients at night. However, it did not affect sleep quality on the third and seventh days after painless gastrointestinal endoscopy.

papers.title: The Effects of Methylphenidate on the EEG of Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.abstract: AimsAttention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (AD/HD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder, with the symptom profile consisting of hyperactivity, impulsivity and inattention. Currently methylphenidate is the most widely used treatment for AD/HD. Studies on mixed stimulant use have found that stimulants result in normalisation of electroencephalogram (EEG) activity during an eyes-closed resting condition. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of Methylphenidate alone on the EEG of children with AD/HD and to extend the investigation into the gamma band.MethodFifty children with AD/HD and 50 typically developing children, between the ages of 8 and 12 years, participated in this study. Clinical participants were assessed for AD/HD at an initial session at which an EEG was performed. They returned within 1 week for a medication assessment, and a second EEG was recorded 1.5 h after ingestion of 10 mg of methylphenidate. EEG was recorded during an eyes-closed resting condition, and Fourier transformed to provide absolute and relative power estimates in delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands.ResultsUnmedicated, the AD/HD group had elevated global absolute and relative delta, elevated posterior absolute theta, elevated posterior relative theta, reduced global relative alpha, and reduced global absolute and relative gamma activity compared to the control group. Methylphenidate ingestion was associated with a global increase in absolute and relative beta, and in relative gamma activity.ConclusionsSignificant increases in fast wave activity were observed with methylphenidate use. However, unlike past research, it is not clear that this should be considered as normalisation of the EEG.

papers.title: Physical Activity Levels and Depressive Symptoms in US Adults: NHANES 2007-2020.
papers.abstract: Physical activity and sleep are modifiable depression risks, yet their integrated impact remains under-explored. We evaluated the association between moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and depressive symptoms, considering sleep duration and biological plausibility. We analyzed 25,109 US adults (NHANES 2007 to 2020). Exposure was MVPA guideline adherence (≥150 min/week). Outcome was depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥10); sensitivity analyses used ≥12 and ≥15 cutoffs. MVPA adherence was linked to 53% lower odds of depressive symptoms (aOR=0.47, 95% CI [0.35, 0.63]). Effects strengthened at higher thresholds (aOR=0.39 for ≥15), confirming robustness. Absolute risk reductions occurred across all sleep strata, particularly in short (-5.9 pp) and long sleepers (-8.2 pp). MVPA adherence is robustly associated with lower depressive risk, regardless of sleep duration. These protective effects are likely mediated by neuroinflammatory regulation and neuroplasticity. Promoting physical activity is a critical, scalable public health strategy.

papers.title: A Clinically Informed Cross-Attention Deep Learning Framework for Automated Diagnosis of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent breathing-related sleep disorder associated with a variety of cardiovascular comorbidities. Polysomnography (PSG) is the clinical gold standard for OSA diagnosis, with disease severity quantified by the apnea hypopnea index (AHI). However, deriving AHI requires manual annotation of overnight PSG recordings by certificated technicians, making the OSA diagnostic process costly and time-consuming. While it is highly desirable to automate this process with a reliable machine learning pipeline, conventional models often rely on handcrafted feature engineering and may therefore not sufficiently capture the complex dynamics of physiological signals. Deep learning models can learn nonlinear representations directly from raw PSG signals, but many existing works study PSG independently and give less consideration to clinical variables that are known to influence OSA risk, e.g., age, sex. More importantly, most prior research has focused on a single dataset, raising concerns about the robustness and generalizability of these models. To tackle these limitations, this project proposes a clinical knowledge-guided cross-attention deep learning framework for automated PSG annotation and AHI prediction from overnight PSG recordings, combined with clinical variables. The proposed framework employs a deep encoder to learn epoch-level features from PSG data and classify epochs based on whether an adverse respiratory event occurs, providing epoch-level PSG annotations that mimic manual evaluation in current practice. Then, the epoch-level embeddings will be integrated with clinical variables using a multi-head attention mechanism for patient-level AHI prediction. The framework is validated across four large real-world datasets.

Theoretical analysis of transfer learning for temporally dependent observations.
papers.abstract: Transfer learning has become increasingly important in recent years as it enables models to quickly adapt to new tasks, environments and data sets. It can improve the accuracy of machine learning models and reduce the training time required for them. However, theoretical foundation of transfer learning algorithms is rather scarce, particularly for time series models. In this work, we focus on high-dimensional vector autoregressive models and provide a two-step procedure to conduct transfer learning utilizing auxiliary data sets followed by constructing confidence intervals for model parameters in the high-dimensional regime. Further, a new method to select informative sets from auxiliary sets is introduced. Finally, two debiasing techniques are developed to perform inference for model parameters. Theoretical properties of all proposed algorithms are established under mild conditions which allow for heavy-tailed distributions and dependence among auxiliary and target data sets. Given certain level of similarity between the informative models and the target model, it is shown that the proposed algorithm achieves the minimax rate. Lastly, the empirical performance of proposed methods is tested through analyzing both simulated data as well as an EEG data set.

papers.title: Life's Essential 8 and Depression in the U.S.: Findings From National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular health and mental health are closely interconnected; however, the relationship between the American Heart Association's updated Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health metric and depression severity has not been fully characterized in U.S. adults. The association between Life's Essential 8 and depressive symptom severity was examined in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults. Cross-sectional data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were analyzed. Life's Essential 8 scores were calculated using behavioral (smoking, diet, physical activity, sleep health, and BMI) and health factor (blood pressure, cholesterol, and HbA1c) components. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 and categorized as no/minimal (scores <10), moderate (scores 10-18), and severe (scores ≥19) depression. Survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression models were used to estimate ORs and 95% CIs for moderate and severe depression relative to those for no/minimal depression after adjustment for sociodemographic covariates. Higher Life's Essential 8 scores were associated with lower odds of moderate depression, with each 1-point increase corresponding to approximately 0.4% lower odds (OR per 1-point increase=0.996; 95% CI=0.994, 0.998; p=0.001), whereas no significant association was observed for severe depression (OR=0.996; 95% CI=0.988, 1.003; p=0.230). Among individual Life's Essential 8 components, favorable smoking status and healthy sleep duration demonstrated the strongest inverse associations with moderate depression, whereas healthy sleep duration was also associated with lower odds of severe depression. Male gender and higher income-to-poverty ratios were associated with lower odds of moderate depression, whereas single marital status was associated with higher odds. Higher cardiovascular health, as measured by Life's Essential 8, was associated with lower odds of moderate but not severe depression among U.S. adults. Behavioral cardiovascular health indicators, particularly smoking status and sleep health, showed the strongest associations with depressive symptom severity. These findings support the broader relevance of cardiovascular health in relation to mental health and highlight the need for longitudinal studies to clarify temporal and potentially bidirectional relationships between Life's Essential 8 metrics and depression severity.

papers.title: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes: a dataset.
papers.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 30 adult participants exposed to two contrasting designed soundscapes - a natural, sustainability-conveying "organic jungle" soundscape and a contrasting "deconstruct" soundscape - together with their liking ratings of each soundscape and basic demographic information. The data extend the largely behavioral "sonic-seasoning" literature, which has shown that sound and music systematically shape the sensory and affective evaluation of consumer experiences, by adding a complementary neurophysiological measurement angle. EEG was acquired with a 14-channel consumer-grade EMOTIV EPOC X headset (128 Hz) on a web-based experiment platform that logged synchronized event markers. For each participant the dataset provides: a resting calibration recording (eyes-open and eyes-closed); the EEG recorded during a brief (∼17 s) isolated exposure to each of the two soundscapes; the corresponding liking ratings; the soundscape stimulus audio files; and demographic responses. EEG data are released as recorded, with the manufacturer's per-channel contact-quality and signal-quality indices retained, so that re-users can apply any preprocessing or analytic pipeline. These data are of value to researchers in sonic seasoning and multisensory marketing, affective and consumer neuroscience, and to those developing or benchmarking methods for consumer-grade EEG. The included liking ratings provide a behavioral anchor relating the neural data to the affective character of the soundscapes.

papers.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstates are successive global brain states whose temporal organization may reflect cognitive dynamics that conventional summary statistics do not capture. We applied a sequence-based framework, combining conditional successor analysis with multiple sequence alignment adapted from genomics, to microstate sequences recorded during a Go/NoGo task in 30 healthy adults. Generalized estimating equations showed no condition-level differences in standard microstate metrics. Conditional successor analysis identified three motifs enriched in the NoGo-early window (100-500 ms): A-C-D (p FDR = 0.013), B-A-D (p FDR = 0.029), and E-A-D (p FDR = 0.040), all passing through microstate A and ending in microstate D, consistent with fronto-central engagement. Multiple sequence alignment showed non-random temporal organization in all conditions (all z > 11.5 and p < 0.001). These results support sequence syntax as a framework for linking millisecond-scale brain dynamics to cognitive function.

papers.title: Infant carry sling-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and other circumstances surrounding such events in children under two years: A five-year regional registry analysis.
papers.abstract: Infant carry slings are widely used for infant transport and bonding. However, concerns regarding safety have been raised, including risks of positional asphyxia from improper use, particularly in younger infants. This service evaluation explored the frequency of infant carry sling-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in children under two years old over a five-year period within a regional English ambulance service, placing these findings within the wider epidemiological context. This retrospective observational service evaluation used data from an existing OHCA registry and included all patients aged under 2 years who received a resuscitation attempt following cardiac arrest between 1 April 2020 and 31 March 2025. Free-text narratives were reviewed to identify circumstances associated with OHCA, with particular attention paid to carry sling-associated OHCAs. A total of 162 OHCA incidents in children aged under two years were identified, representing 1.0% of all resuscitation attempts during the five-year period. This included 114 infants aged under one year (excluding neonatal life support patients, n = 28). Only two carry sling-associated incidents were identified, both occurring in patients under one year, representing 1.8% of infant OHCAs. The most frequently documented circumstances surrounding OHCA were co-sleeping (33.3%) and patients found unresponsive (e.g. in a cot, bed, sofa or pushchair) (26.3%). Only two carry sling-associated OHCA incidents were identified over five years, suggesting such events were uncommon within this regional registry. In contrast, other sleep-related circumstances, particularly co-sleeping, accounted for a substantially larger proportion of infant OHCA cases.

papers.title: Sleep duration and risk of post-stroke depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke depression frequently occurs as a complication following a stroke, with sleep duration identified as a risk factor. However, the relationship between sleep duration and the risk of post-stroke depression remains controversial. To investigate the association between sleep duration and the risk of post-stroke depression. Relevant studies investigating the association between sleep duration and post-stroke depression were searched in five English databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL) and four Chinese databases (CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, and China Biology Medicine Database) from inception to January 2026. Data extraction and quality assessment of the included literature were independently performed by two investigators. Meta-analyses were conducted using Stata 16.0 software. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using either a fixed-effects or a random-effects model. The analysis included 6 articles, encompassing a total of 5,624 cases. Meta-analysis showed that short sleep duration was associated with an increased risk of post-stroke depression [OR = 1.93, 95% CI(1.56-2.38), p < 0.05], whereas long sleep duration was not significantly associated with the risk [OR = 1.29, 95% CI(1.00-1.66), p > 0.05]. Sleep duration is associated with the risk of post-stroke depression, with shorter sleep duration elevating this risk. Future studies should be incorporated to enhance the reliability of these findings. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024609869, identifier CRD42024609869.

papers.title: The interplay of exercise, immunity, and suboptimal health in college students: an integrative narrative review with public health implications.
papers.abstract: The immune system, vital for pathogen defense and tissue repair, is strongly influenced by lifestyle. With declining physical activity and rising chronic disease burdens, the role of exercise in modulating immunity has drawn growing attention. College students, undergoing critical life transitions, are susceptible to lifestyle-related risks such as sedentary behavior, insufficient sleep, and high psychological stress, which often lead to suboptimal health status. Immune and inflammatory risks are a concern among college students: prolonged sedentary behavior, chronic sleep deprivation, and elevated psychological stress frequently co-occur. Each of these behaviors is associated with low-grade inflammation and altered immune regulation in adults, and their clustering in students is therefore a reasonable basis for concern, although the strength of the association with immune outcomes has seldom been measured directly in this group. The term suboptimal health status is used in this review as a self-reported functional syndrome, defined in Section 3.4, rather than as an established clinical entity. We examine the effects of different physical activities on immune function, chronic low-grade inflammation, and suboptimal health status in college students, outlining the basic framework of exercise immunology and distinguishing acute from chronic exercise responses. Evidence is categorized by exercise type, including moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, high-intensity training, resistance training, and mind-body practices, and their mechanisms, such as myokine-mediated anti-inflammatory signaling, immune cell mobilization, fat loss, and the mediation of sleep and emotion, are summarized. We critically discuss the methodological challenges in this field, separating two sources of disagreement that are often conflated: study design, which determines the causal question a study can answer, and measurement method, which determines how accurately exposure and outcome are captured. We analyze the limitations of each, including the inability of cross-sectional studies to establish causality, measurement bias in self-reported data, and ecological validity and compliance issues in trials, and we note how the same distinction applies to outcome assessment, from self-reported symptoms to immune-cell, cytokine, and clinical infection measures. Notable gaps are identified, including the "population mismatch" whereby findings from other populations are extrapolated to college students, limitations in sample selection and measurement standardization, and the lack of individualized and comprehensive intervention studies. This narrative review underscores the importance of understanding the relationship between exercise and immunity in college students, provides an overview of current knowledge, identifies critical limitations, and proposes future directions. Evidence was assembled through a structured narrative search, and findings obtained directly in college students are distinguished throughout from those extrapolated from athletic or clinical populations. It also offers public health implications for Chinese university settings, emphasizing targeted health education, campus-wide exercise interventions, sedentary behavior reduction, and integrated sleep and stress management to promote student wellbeing.

papers.title: Sleep and burnout syndrome among public high school teachers.
papers.abstract: Schoolteachers face challenges inherent to the academic environment, characterized by an intense workload and high physical, mental, and emotional demands. To characterize the profile of public high school teachers and investigate its association with sleep quality and burnout syndrome. This cross-sectional, descriptive study employed a quantitative approach. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory, administered to a sample of 252 high school teachers. Most participants were female, married, had a mean age of 43 years, and worked 40 hours per week across two daily shifts (morning and afternoon). More than half engaged in regular physical activity. Overall, 61% of participants had poor sleep quality. Most did not use sleep-inducing medications, although 88.31% reported using electronic devices, such as smartphones, before bedtime. The prevalence of burnout syndrome was 11.01%. Higher levels of emotional exhaustion were associated with poorer sleep quality. Working across two school shifts was also associated with increased emotional exhaustion and poorer sleep quality. The findings indicate that emotional exhaustion may adversely affect sleep quality among public high school teachers. Furthermore, the absence of healthy lifestyle habits, such as regular physical activity and leisure activities, may also contribute to poorer sleep quality.

papers.title: Individual olfactory channels shape distinct parameters of sleep architecture.
papers.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction and anosmia are associated with disruptions in sleep. In Drosophila melanogaster, broadly inhibiting olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) similarly disrupts sleep. However, due to the diversity of ORNs and the combinatorial nature of olfactory processing, the circuit logic by which ORNs modulate sleep remains unclear. In this study, we paired driver lines of different ensembles of ORNs, individual ORN types, and a known modulator of ORNs with synaptic silencing tools and targeted gene disruptions to further characterize the contributions of ORNs to sleep architecture. We find that the activity of distinct ORN types modulates day and nighttime sleep and heterogeneously shapes parameters of sleep architecture. Furthermore, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are in part shaped by heterogeneous serotonin (5-HT) receptor expression. Together, this work identifies pathways bridging olfaction and sleep, and establishes a circuit model that can be used to further characterize the behavioral consequences of sensory dysfunction.

papers.title: The effect of Azaraghi herbal compound on craving, sexual function, mental health, and sleep quality in opioid-dependent patients under methadone maintenance therapy: a clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Substance use disorders are chronic disorders that cause an imbalance of neurotransmitters. Conventional treatments often have limited efficacy and potential adverse effects, highlighting the need for adjunctive therapies. Herbal formulations such as Azaraghi Majoon (AM), rich in antioxidant and anti-inflammatory compounds, may offer therapeutic benefits. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of AM in reducing drug craving and improving psychological status, sexual function, and sleep quality in individuals with opioid dependence. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 81 opioid-dependent patients on methadone maintenance therapy were randomly assigned to two groups: AM (n=40) or placebo (n=41). The herbal formulation was administered orally at 1-2 teaspoons/day, titrated to 4 teaspoons within one week, for four weeks. Methadone was continued at baseline doses, with up to 50% reduction allowed under supervision in improved patients. Primary outcomes were drug craving, depression, anxiety, and stress; secondary outcomes were sexual function and sleep quality. All outcomes were assessed at baseline, and week 2 and 4. AM significantly reduced drug craving compared to placebo (p<0.01), but improved depression, anxiety, stress, sexual function, and sleep quality (all p<0.01). No serious adverse effects or worsening of withdrawal symptoms were observed. AM is a promising adjunctive therapy for opioid dependence, reducing craving, enhancing mood and sleep, improving sexual function, and demonstrating a favorable safety profile.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults.
papers.abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder characterized by intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation, contributing to systemic inflammation and autonomic dysfunction. Long COVID refers to persistent symptoms following acute COVID-19 infection. Emerging evidence suggests an association between OSA and persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms, potentially mediated by overlapping biological pathways; however, the direction and causality of this relationship remain uncertain. This scoping review aimed to examine the current evidence regarding the different associations between OSA and Long COVID in adults, summarize the reported clinical findings, and explore the proposed pathophysiological mechanisms linking OSA and Long COVID. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Eligible studies included observational studies, clinical trials, and reviews involving adults with OSAand/or Long COVID syndrome. Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and synthesized findings thematically. Of 184 identified records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. Evidence suggested different associations between OSA and Long COVID across the included studies. Proposed mechanisms included intermittent hypoxia, systemic inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, sleep fragmentation, and circadian disturbance; however, these mechanisms were not consistently measured across studies. Reported Long COVID manifestations among patients with OSA included fatigue, respiratory impairment, cognitive dysfunction, and cardiovascular complications. Evidence regarding the impact of OSA treatment on Long COVID outcomes was limited. Current evidence suggests an association between OSA and Long COVID, although the nature and direction of this association vary across studies. However, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify this relationship and determine whether effective OSA management can improve Long COVID outcomes.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

papers.title: Hypothesis on energy storage by membrane proton buffers: Connections to sleep and memory.
papers.abstract: Extramitochondrial ATP synthesis appears widespread thanks to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDVs) that export the mitochondrial molecular machinery of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to cellular and extracellular membrane systems, where OXPHOS can occur in two phases: first, protons are charged into membrane proton buffers, and then, "discharge" occurs with the coupled synthesis of ATP. The capacitance of membrane proton buffers increases in the presence of abundant basic proteins (such as the myelin sheath, which contains nearly 30% myelin basic protein) allowing the first phase of OXPHOS to optimally charge the proton buffer, which then allows for an efficient discharge phase with the synthesis of large amounts of ATP. This provides an energy storage function that was not predicted by the chemiosmotic theory. Since memory depends on the accumulation and expenditure of brain energy, possible connections between energy buffers and memory are being considered. This study reevaluates the experiments of Russian scientists who, half a century ago, achieved a biphasic oxidative phosphorylation with intermediate proton accumulation by an artificial hydrophobic proton buffer embedded in the lipid phase.

papers.title: Single-cell dataset of juvenile mouse neurons from the thalamic reticular nucleus: whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology.
papers.abstract: This dataset provides single-cell whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology for 19 interneurons of the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) in juvenile mice. The recordings were obtained from male C57Bl/6J mice sampled within the developmental window of postnatal days 24 to 34. Acute horizontal brain slices were used, and visually targeted whole-cell recordings were performed in current-clamp mode. A standardized current-clamp stimulus battery was used identically across all cells to characterize their intrinsic electrophysiological properties-passive membrane behavior, action-potential threshold and waveform, suprathreshold firing patterns, and the hyperpolarization-evoked rebound-burst dynamics characteristic of reticular thalamic neurons. The release comprises 18,015 recorded sweeps and their full, un-decimated signal traces (400 million digitized samples), preserved in the community-standard NWB (icephys) format alongside the original Igor Pro source files, and indexed into tidy, queryable Apache Parquet tables-one record per recording session, one per sweep, and one per digitized sample-linked by a normalized recording identifier. Each recording includes animal metadata (postnatal age, body weight, strain, genotype, slice orientation, and recorded region) and its resting membrane potential. The dataset is released as a FAIR² Data Package under the Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 (ODC-By v1.0), with machine-readable metadata conforming to the MLCommons Croissant specification, QUDT units, and PROV-O provenance. It is intended for neuroscientists, computational modelers, and machine-learning researchers studying the intrinsic electrophysiology of TRN neurons.

papers.title: Lightweight audio-visual sentiment analysis with dynamic mouth-state modeling and multimodal LLM benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Sentiment analysis from video streams requires effective modeling of both temporal dynamics and multimodal cues. This paper presents a lightweight multimodal CNN-LSTM framework, designed for low-latency operation on live video streams, that classifies individuals' affective states as negative, neutral, or positive by jointly exploiting audio and visual information. The proposed system consists of four lightweight deep neural network models that fuse sequences of audio and visual features into a unified temporal stream, enabling the accumulation of sentiment evidence over time for robust prediction. To further enhance discriminative power, dynamic mouth state classification is incorporated, allowing the model to better capture subtle visual cues related to speech and sentiment. Experiments conducted on the Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech (RAVDESS) demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a test accuracy of 84.89% on the three-class sentiment recognition task, competitive with substantially larger audio-visual architectures, while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters and maintaining low-latency operation. In addition, we provide a comprehensive comparison with multiple multimodal large language models (LLMs), evaluated under diverse input configurations and prompting strategies. The results offer practical insights into the strengths and limitations of contemporary LLMs for audio-visual sentiment analysis and highlight the continued effectiveness of compact, task-specific neural architectures for streaming audio-visual input.

papers.title: Optogenetics in neurobiology and neurodegenerative disorders: from neural circuit mechanisms to precision neuromodulation.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, multiple sclerosis and stroke, are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction, synaptic impairment and neural circuit degeneration, leading to severe cognitive and motor deficits. Although considerable progress has been made in understanding their molecular pathology, the circuit level mechanisms driving disease onset and progression remain incompletely understood. Optogenetics, which combines microbial opsins, genetic engineering and optical stimulation, enables reversible, cell-specific control of neuronal activity with millisecond precision and has transformed neuroscience from observational analysis to causal investigation of neural circuits. This review summarizes recent advances in the molecular basis of optogenetics, microbial opsins, gene delivery strategies and optical stimulation technologies, together with their applications in basic neurobiology and neurodegenerative disease research. We discuss how optogenetics has advanced understanding of neural circuit organization, synaptic plasticity, memory, neurodevelopment, sleep regulation, protein aggregation, synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial impairment, oxidative stress and regulated cell death. Although these studies have generated important mechanistic insights and demonstrated functional improvements in experimental models, translation into human therapies remains investigational due to challenges associated with gene delivery, long-term opsin expression, immune compatibility and optical accessibility. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including closed-loop neuromodulation, wireless photostimulation, artificial intelligence-assisted neural decoding, nanotechnology enabled light delivery and brain computer interfaces, are critically evaluated with emphasis on their current evidence status, translational challenges and limitations for clinical implementation. Collectively, optogenetics provides an unprecedented platform for deciphering disease mechanisms and evaluating circuit-based neuromodulation strategies, while continued technological and biological validation will determine its future role in precision therapies for neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: From bouts to readiness to compete: temporal dynamics of stress, fatigue, recovery and monitoring-informed decisions in combat sports.
papers.abstract: Combat-sport tournaments require decisions before responses to previous efforts have resolved. Detecting a change does not establish that an indicator predicts the next task or improves a decision. This Perspective proposes a task- and time-specific framework linking prior bouts, recovery time and subsequent demands through three evidentiary requirements. Responsiveness concerns reproducible changes beyond measurement error when an indicator represents a response to effort. Predictive validity concerns anticipation of a pre-specified subsequent outcome and added information beyond simpler measures. Decision utility concerns improved outcomes relative to usual practice. Indicators interpreted as current status or stable capacity need not respond to prior effort, but still require adequate measurement properties and prospective evaluation. Evidence from repeated bouts, recovery interventions, mental fatigue, sleep restriction and weight loss suggests that monitoring domains are not interchangeable. The framework retains discordant indicators, evaluates combinations and communicates uncertainty without global clearance labels. Three hypotheses address task and time dependence, maintained performance with increasing effort cost, and indicator-informed decisions. Medical decisions remain independent and take precedence. This is an operational extension of existing principles, not a validated predictive tool.
