papers.title: Prosociality differences in neural reward processing during cooperation and competition: an ERP investigation.
papers.abstract: Reward evaluation is shaped by social context and individual traits, but how prosociality modulates neural gain-loss differentiation during real interpersonal cooperation and competition remains unclear. This study examined the feedback-related negativity difference wave (dFRN) in cooperative and competitive tasks. Forty participants (20 females; mean age = 22 years) completed face-to-face cooperation and competition tasks while EEG was recorded. Prosociality was measured with the Prosocial Scale. dFRN was calculated as loss-evoked minus gain-evoked mean voltage at Fz, FCz, and Cz within 220-300 ms after reward feedback. A 2 (Social Context) × 2 (Prosociality) mixed ANOVA and linear mixed-effects models using continuous prosociality scores were conducted. A significant Social Context × Prosocial Trait interaction emerged. High-prosocial participants showed a more negative dFRN in cooperation than in competition, whereas low-prosocial participants showed no reliable context difference. Continuous-score mixed-effects models adjusted for sex supported this association (b = -0.315 μV per scale point, SE = 0.152, z = -2.07, p = 0.039, 95% CI [-0.614, -0.016]); the group-based contrast (p = 0.054) and robust-standard-error analysis (p = 0.051) were marginal. These findings suggest that prosociality is associated with context-dependent reward differentiation, with shared cooperative outcomes eliciting stronger loss-gain differentiation among high-prosocial individuals. Causal interpretation is limited by the fixed task order, differing outcome-generation rules, and unmodeled dyadic dependence.

papers.title: Parental health literacy and multidimensional health education competencies in preschool children.
papers.abstract: Although parental health literacy is regarded as correlated with the health-related learning environment of preschool children, evidence addressing children's health education in a multidimensional manner remains limited. Thus, the aim of this study was to examine the relationship between parental health literacy and the parent-reported overall health education score and its subdimensions among preschool children-after controlling for child-, parent-, and family-related characteristics-as well as the incremental explanatory contribution of parental health literacy beyond these characteristics. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2024 with 407 parents of 5 and 6-year-old children enrolled in preschools in Tokat, Türkiye. Data were collected using the Health Literacy Scale-Short Form, the Parent-Reported Health Education Scale for Preschool Children, and the Sociodemographic and Health Information Form. Child-, parent-, and family-related characteristics, as well as parental health literacy, were included in hierarchical multiple linear regression models, respectively. The overall health education score and its six subscales were analyzed separately. The Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied to the p-values for parental health literacy in the subscale models. The final model explained 39.5% of the variance in the overall health education score. Including parental health literacy in the model contributed an additional 4.1% to the explained variance (ΔR 2 = 0.041; p < 0.001), and a higher level of parental health literacy correlated with higher overall scores in health education (B = 0.012; β = 0.215; 95% CI: 0.008-0.017). Following the Benjamini-Hochberg correction, parental health literacy remained significantly associated with higher scores on the subscales of personal safety and first aid, hygiene and self-care, nutrition, mental health and social relationships, and neglect and abuse; however, no significant relationship was found for the sleep subscale. Higher parental health literacy was found to be linked with higher overall health education scores among preschool children and higher scores in five of the six domains, after controlling for child, parent, and family characteristics. The findings suggest that parental health literacy could be a valuable element to consider in family-centered early childhood health promotion and preventive health education approaches.

papers.title: Symptom-related clinical phenotypes in adults with obstructive sleep apnea: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the variables and methods used to identify symptom-related clinical phenotypes in adults with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), summarize the major phenotypes and their associations with treatment and health outcomes, and provide evidence to inform multidimensional clinical assessment and long-term follow-up in OSA. This scoping review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were systematically searched from inception to 27 June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Using the symptom classes reported in the original studies as the units of analysis, we synthesized evidence on phenotype-defining variables, identification methods, recurrent symptom patterns across studies, associations with objective disease burden, positive airway pressure (PAP)-related measures, patient-reported outcomes, and long-term clinical outcomes, as well as longitudinal phenotype transitions. Thirty-six study reports were included. Latent class analysis and cluster analysis were the predominant approaches to phenotype identification. Descriptive cross-study synthesis identified three core phenotypes-daytime sleepiness-predominant, disturbed sleep/insomnia-predominant, and minimally symptomatic-and two extended phenotypes: upper airway/respiratory interruption symptom-predominant and mixed-symptom/high symptom burden. Differences across phenotypes were reported in daytime functioning, psychological status, quality of life, PAP prescription or early use, and symptom improvement following treatment. Symptom burden was not consistently aligned with objective disease burden, and some patients transitioned between symptom phenotypes over time. Recurrent symptom-related clinical phenotypes were observed across studies of adults with OSA. Symptom phenotypes may serve as a complementary component of multidimensional clinical assessment and should be interpreted alongside objective respiratory and hypoxic burden, comorbidities, and treatment information. They may also inform the assessment of changes in symptoms and functional status during long-term follow-up. Future research should refine phenotype identification, strengthen external validation across populations, and further examine associations of symptom phenotypes with treatment response and long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Simulation-based neural dynamics of stress-related negative cognitive bias in depressive symptoms: a dynamical EEG/ERP framework.
papers.abstract: This simulation-based computational study develops a non-linear state-space framework for stress-related negative cognitive bias and multivariate EEG/ERP observations. A three-state model represents negative bias, cognitive control, and arousal, while symptom load and normalized model stress input reshape a quartic bias potential. N2, P3, late positive potential, frontal theta, frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA), and frontoparietal phase locking provide complementary observation channels. Additional checks distinguish the non-linear benchmark from additive and interaction-only competing generators, examine equilibria of the full coupled system, and perturb the observation model. We establish bounded stochastic dynamics, a conditional scalar multistability boundary, stable-branch stress sensitivity, and a sufficient local state-observability condition. A seeded benchmark with 180 simulated participants yields model-implied stress-by-symptom slopes of 66.83 ms for response time, 1.12 μV for LPP, 0.775 dB for frontal theta, 0.133 for FAA, and 0.0769 for frontoparietal PLV. Under a non-linear generating process, mean held-out RMSE was 0.060 for the pre-specified quartic candidate vs. 0.436 for the interaction-only candidate. State-reconstruction RMSE increased from 0.152 under the nominal loading matrix to 0.232 under 15% loading perturbations. These results demonstrate implementation consistency and characterize model sensitivity; they are not clinical effect estimates or evidence of empirical parameter identifiability.

papers.title: Effects of mindfulness-based interventions on sleep quality in university students: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems are common among university students due to academic stress, lifestyle factors, and psychological distress and may adversely affect physical and mental health, academic performance, and social functioning. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have increasingly been used as a non-pharmacological approach to improve sleep health; however, previous findings remain inconsistent, and evidence specifically addressing sleep quality in university students remains limited. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of MBIs on sleep quality in university students and explore factors that may account for variations in intervention effects. We searched seven databases-PubMed, Web of Science, EBSCO, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, Embase, and ScienceDirect-from inception to June 26, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating MBIs for sleep quality in university students were included. Two reviewers independently conducted study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the RoB 2 tool. Meta-analysis was conducted in Stata 17.0 using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, publication bias assessment, and GRADE assessment were also performed. Ten RCTs involving 638 university students were included, with 335 participants in the intervention groups and 303 in the control groups. MBIs significantly improved sleep quality [SMD = -0.97, 95% CI (-1.43, -0.51), p < 0.001], although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 85.1%). Subgroup analyses revealed statistically significant between-group differences with respect to sleep-outcome measurement instrument (p = 0.001), intervention type (p = 0.009), and session duration (p = 0.030), indicating that these variables may partially account for the observed heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled results. Egger's test revealed no evidence of significant publication bias (p = 0.270). The certainty of the evidence was rated as low according to the GRADE framework. MBIs may improve sleep quality in university students. However, given the substantial heterogeneity and low certainty of evidence, further high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm these findings. CRD420261458068, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261458068.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: clinical evidence and mechanistic perspectives.
papers.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common neurological complications in older surgical patients and are associated with impaired recovery, loss of independence, and worse quality of life. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive neuromodulatory intervention with plausible effects on inflammatory, autonomic, sleep, pain, and cognitive-network pathways. We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review of direct perioperative randomized clinical evidence and, when outcomes were sufficiently comparable, an exploratory meta-analysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 5 August 2026. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Mechanistic and translational evidence was synthesized separately using a structured narrative approach. Four randomized trials enrolled or randomized 480 participants, of whom 469 contributed to reported analyses. Two trials involving 220 participants assessed related but non-identical early postoperative cognitive-decline constructs: one used dNCR and the other investigator-defined traditional POCD. Both studies individually favored taVNS, and the individual study estimates were treated as the primary evidence. A post hoc exploratory cross-construct synthesis yielded an RR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.18-0.64). Because the contributing trials used non-equivalent cognitive definitions, stimulation regimens, and comparator conditions, this secondary pooled estimate should not be interpreted as representing either a single standardized cognitive outcome or the effect of a single standardized taVNS intervention. A separate multicenter trial reported postoperative delirium in 12.0% versus 25.3% of participants (risk ratio 0.47, 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.98), and another trial showed more favorable postoperative Montreal Cognitive Assessment trajectories. Beyond clinical outcomes, the broader mechanistic literature supports a multilevel neurophysiological rationale for taVNS, consistent with possible modulation of auricular vagal afferent-nucleus tractus solitarius signaling, locus coeruleus and autonomic regulation, inflammatory reflex pathways, splenic sympathetic-cholinergic immune modulation, blood-brain barrier/neurovascular unit protection, glial responses, sleep-arousal regulation, and cognitive-network plasticity. However, most mechanistic evidence remains derived from preclinical or non-perioperative studies, and no causal pathway linking target engagement to cognitive improvement has been established. Current evidence suggests a promising but preliminary clinical signal for taVNS in perioperative neurocognitive disorders. However, certainty remains low to very low, and routine clinical implementation is not yet supported. Available adverse-event data are insufficient to establish perioperative safety or to exclude uncommon cardiovascular or autonomic adverse events. Standardized PND outcomes, credible sham conditions, optimized stimulation dose and timing, systematic adverse-event ascertainment, multimodal target-engagement biomarkers, and risk-enriched confirmatory trials are priorities for future development. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261468039, Identifier: CRD420261468039.

papers.title: A unified fixed-wavelet transformer decodes eight EEG classes across motor imagery, P300, and SSVEP paradigms.
papers.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) can support self-initiated control, whereas brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) based on the P300 or the steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) rely on ongoing visual stimulation. Repetitive visual stimulation can cause visual fatigue; when the stimuli are suspended, however, the corresponding P300 and SSVEP responses can no longer be elicited, and these paradigms alone cannot support a self-initiated command to restart visual stimulation. By contrast, self-initiated MI can provide a voluntary gating signal for switching visual stimulation on or off. Developing a single architecture capable of learning these heterogeneous EEG signatures and decoding multiple user intentions is therefore an important step toward a voluntarily controlled hybrid BCI. To this end, we developed a unified model by extending our previously proposed Analformer, a Transformer-based architecture designed for high classification performance while enabling the analysis of neurophysiologically meaningful EEG representations through AnalNet. We evaluated whether the model could classify EEG trials into eight mutually exclusive classes drawn from MI, P300, and SSVEP paradigms in the OpenBMI dataset. Analformer uses fixed Morlet wavelet kernels to extract frequency-specific EEG features, six Transformer blocks model dependencies across 31 pooled temporal tokens, and a two-stage training procedure to capture both population-level and participant-specific features. Across 54 participants, the mean accuracy obtained from the model after participant-specific fine-tuning was 71.00%, compared with 54.53% for EEG-Conformer, 52.30% for EEGNet, and 45.35% for ShallowConvNet under the same evaluation protocol. Ablation analyses showed that replacing the fixed wavelets with learnable convolutions reduced the mean accuracy to 63.15%, whereas omitting the two-stage training procedure reduced it to 47.38%. AnalNet, the built-in analysis module of Analformer, identified class-discriminative patterns, including sensorimotor mu- and beta-band activity during MI and stimulus-locked occipital responses during SSVEP. Together, these findings indicate that a single Transformer-based architecture can distinguish heterogeneous EEG classes and provide a foundation for unified decoding in hybrid BCIs that combine self-initiated MI gating with P300- and SSVEP-based command selection.

papers.title: Bilateral cerebellar high-frequency rTMS for refractory epilepsy: a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled study.
papers.abstract: For patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who are not suitable for surgery, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an important non-invasive neuromodulation therapy. The cerebellar cortex can inhibit cortical excitability via the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway. Here, we explore whether high-frequency (20 Hz) cerebellar repetitive TMS (rTMS) reduces seizure frequency and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in refractory epilepsy. Eighty-seven patients with refractory epilepsy were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population (n = 87) and then randomized to active rTMS (n = 44) or sham stimulation (n = 43). One patient in treatment group had no post-baseline efficacy data; efficacy analyses were therefore performed in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (n = 86). The active group received two cycles of 20 Hz rTMS targeting the cerebellum. Seizure frequency and IEDs were assessed before and after treatment. Poisson generalized linear mixed models revealed a significant group×time interaction for seizure frequency [F(2,236) = 162.65, p < 0.001]. The active group had significantly lower seizure frequencies at months 1, 2, and 3 (all p < 0.001), with the largest difference at month 2. Percentage reductions of seizure frequency in the active group were 64.6%, 73.2%, and 13.3%, respectively, compared with 3.9%, 0.6%, and -8.4% in the control group (all P < 0.001). Responder rates (≥50% reduction) in the active group were 90.7%, 95.3%, and 0% vs. 0% in controls (p < 0.001 for months 1-2). Within-group analysis showed significant IED reduction after active rTMS (p < 0.001) but no change in controls. Moreover, a significant group × baseline interaction (p < 0.001) indicated greater suppression in patients with higher baseline IEDs. Exploratory subgroup analysis further confirmed this. All adverse events were mild, with no significant difference in the incidence between the two groups. Active cerebellar rTMS was associated with reduced seizure frequency, improved responder rates, and suppressed IEDs in refractory epilepsy with no obvious discomfort. The optimal efficacy duration was approximately 2 months, with greater IED suppression in patients with higher baseline levels.

papers.title: Factors associated with AD8-defined high cognitive risk in community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: With the accelerating global population aging, cognitive dysfunction has become an important public health challenge among middle-aged and older adults. The Ascertain Dementia 8-item Informant Questionnaire (AD8) is a simple and sensitive screening tool for identifying individuals at risk of cognitive impairment in community settings. However, evidence regarding factors associated with AD8-defined high cognitive risk (AD8 positivity) among community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults remains limited. This study aimed to investigate factors associated with AD8 positivity in a large community-based population. A total of 7,601 participants were included in the descriptive and univariate analyses. All 14 candidate variables were entered into the multivariable logistic regression model, which was fitted using complete cases (n = 7,293). Household economic status was retained a priori based on previous epidemiological evidence. Among the 7,601 participants, 6,116 (80.5%) were classified as having AD8 positivity. Univariate analyses showed that thirteen of the fourteen candidate variables were significantly associated with AD8 positivity. Multivariable logistic regression identified nine factors independently associated with AD8 positivity. Advanced age, female sex, marital status, poor self-rated health, depressive symptoms, and sleep disturbances were positively associated with AD8 positivity, whereas higher educational attainment and regular physical activity were negatively associated with AD8 positivity (indicating a lower risk). In addition, household economic status remained significantly associated with AD8 positivity after adjustment for potential confounders. AD8 positivity was highly prevalent among community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults in this study population. Age, sex, marital status, educational level, household economic status, regular physical activity, self-rated health, depressive symptoms, and sleep disturbances were independently associated with AD8 positivity. These findings may help identify vulnerable populations and provide evidence for community-based cognitive health management and early intervention strategies.

papers.title: Under-recognized Autoimmune Encephalitis in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Case Series Emphasizing EEG Screening.
papers.abstract: AD and AE present overlapping cognitive decline, often causing misdiagnosis and delayed immunotherapy. AD has an insidious onset and slow progression with typical Aβ and tau abnormalities, while AE manifests subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms and inflammatory imaging or CSF changes. Rapid cognitive decline in AD patients with superimposed AE is easily misdiagnosed as simple neurodegeneration. EEG is a convenient non-invasive test that can serve as a screening tool to trigger further autoimmune evaluation in AD patients with unexplained rapid deterioration. This case series reports two verified AD patients complicated with anti-LGI1 encephalitis and probable seronegative AE. It adds to the literature on the pathological coexistence and interaction of AD and AE, highlights the underutilized diagnostic value of EEG, and supports routine EEG screening for rapidly progressive AD cognitive decline. Two biomarker-confirmed AD female patients with comorbid AE were included. The 75-year-old patient had 4 years of cognitive decline (baseline MMSE=10), with typical AD imaging and biomarker abnormalities, positive anti-LGI1 IgG and abnormal EEG, diagnosed with AD combined with LGI1 encephalitis. She received IVIg, rituximab, anti-amyloid and anti-dementia treatment. MMSE improved from 10 to 18 at 1 month but fluctuated thereafter (MMSE 11-12, MoCA 3-9) with treatment pause and irregular adherence; serum LGI1 antibody and AD biomarkers remained normal throughout. The 62-year-old patient had 7 years of cognitive decline, personality changes, and hallucinations (MMSE=0, MoCA=0). She was diagnosed with probable seronegative AE complicated with AD based on AD imaging changes, positive CSF indicators, and positive TBA findings. Treatment with telitacicept and lecanemab was associated with modest cognitive improvement (MMSE +3, MoCA +2) at short-term follow-up. Rapid cognitive exacerbation in AD patients should not be attributed to natural neurodegeneration. Routine EEG is an essential noninvasive tool for cognitive evaluation in AD. EEG abnormalities in AD patients require comprehensive autoimmune examinations. Concurrent AE is a reversible and treatable factor worsening AD cognitive impairment. Combined immunotherapy and anti-amyloid treatment can significantly improve patient cognition and biomarkers. EEG should be a routine screening item for rapidly progressive AD. Autoimmune inflammation may accelerate AD progression, providing new insights for AD immunological pathogenesis and targeted therapy research.

papers.title: Association of Self-Reported Sleep and Circadian Variability and Moral Judgements and Decision-Making.
papers.abstract: Sleep and social processes are bidirectionally interrelated. Circadian factors such as sleep duration, quality, and chronotype can influence social processing, including moral judgements and decision-making. We investigated the associations of self-reported sleep and circadian factors with measures of human moral and social judgements, including online vigilantism, aversion to causing and witnessing harm, and generosity. A total of 109 healthy adults (18-39 years) completed an observational online survey of self-report measures of sleep and circadian factors (quality, chronotype, sleep regularity, social jetlag), as well as self-report or behavioural measures related to moral concerns, such as willingness to engage in online vigilantism, aversion to causing and witnessing harm to others, and generosity (the Dictator Game). We found significant associations between increased online vigilantism and earlier chronotype, higher sleep regularity, and less social jetlag (r > 0.20, all p < 0.05), and between aversion to causing and witnessing harm and sleep regularity (r > 0.20, all p < 0.05), but not for dictator game generosity (p > 0.06). Hierarchical regression analyses identified moderate effect sizes for sleep regularity and (to a lesser extent) social jetlag as significant contributors to vigilantism and aversion to causing and witnessing harm (R2 > 0.21, all p < 0.05), after controlling for sociodemographic characteristics, mental health conditions, and medication intake. A small, non-significant effect size was identified for sleep quality and dictator game generosity (R2 = 0.13, p = 0.06). The findings highlight the importance of considering sleep and circadian regularity in human moral judgements and decision-making.

papers.title: Reversal of photoperiodic flowering in temperate grasses rewired light inputs and floral outputs of the circadian clock.
papers.abstract: The transition from long-day (LD) to short-day (SD) flowering enabled temperate grasses of the tribe Stipeae (Poaceae: Pooideae) to colonise neotropical montane habitats, yet the transcriptomic basis of this shift remains poorly understood. Here, we used comparative transcriptomics and functional principal component analysis to examine diel gene expression in SD-flowering Nassella pubiflora and LD-flowering Oloptum miliaceum. Although photoperiod substantially rewired the diel transcriptome in both species, interspecific expression differences were limited to a small subset of orthologous genes. Divergence was most pronounced under SDs and involved floral integrators, light-signalling genes, and circadian clock targets, while core circadian clock gene expression remained largely conserved. These results suggest that the reversal from LD to SD flowering in Stipeae involved modifications to relatively few but central flowering pathway genes that convey photoperiod signals, rather than widespread changes to the endogenous timekeeping system. Our findings provide insight into the genetic architecture underlying niche transitions and photoperiod responsiveness in grasses and identify candidate genes that could potentially be targeted to optimise flowering time in cereal crops.

papers.title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network for the P3.
papers.abstract: The event-related P3 is evoked by most task-relevant or salient stimuli, but its neural sources remain controversial. Here we reevaluate the role of hippocampus, unambiguously demonstrated in intracranial recordings, and retro-splenial cortex as sources of the P3 in magneto- and electroencephalography. Observers detected rare visual targets of a deviant shape and ignored rare non-targets of a deviant color. Source analysis was based on noise-normalized minimum-norm estimates in an individual, MRI-based source space. Critically, the cortical source space was extended to include the cornu ammonis of the hippocampus. Source analysis at the P3 peak showed strong sources in retrosplenial cortex and a weaker source in hippocampus. Activity in left somatosensory cortex was related to the button presses. Subsequent activity was observed in insula and anterior mid-cingulate cortex. Further simulation studies explored the spread of these sources and the plausibility of their combination to explain the data, and demonstrate that the combination of magneto- and electroencephalography increased the specificity of the source estimate. Overall, these data support an interpretation of the P3 as physiological indicator of activity in the limbic system for target and distractor stimuli.

papers.title: Associations of smartphone use, perceived stress, and sleep quality with diet quality and macronutrient intake among Korean young adults.
papers.abstract: Smartphone use, psychological stress, and sleep quality are increasingly recognized as lifestyle factors that may influence dietary behaviors in young adults; however, their associations with overall diet quality remain unclear. This cross-sectional study investigated the associations of daily smartphone use, perceived stress, and perceived sleep quality with diet quality and macronutrient intake among 497 Korean adults aged 20-39 years. Diet quality was assessed using the Nutrition Quotient for Korean Adults 2021 (NQ-2021), and dietary intake was evaluated using a 24-hour dietary recall. Longer smartphone use was inversely associated with total NQ and practice scores after adjustment for potential confounders. Participants with higher perceived stress consumed a greater amount of carbohydrates and a lower amount of fat per 1,000 kcal, whereas total NQ scores did not differ according to perceived stress level. Participants reporting poorer sleep quality had significantly lower total NQ, balance, and moderation scores and lower protein intake than those with better sleep quality. These findings suggest that self-reported smartphone use, perceived stress, and perceived sleep quality are associated with different aspects of diet quality and macronutrient intake among Korean young adults. Prospective studies using validated or objective measures are warranted to clarify the temporal relationships between these lifestyle-related factors and dietary behaviors.

papers.title: The cath lab readiness gap: a national survey of technology-driven role shifts and training needs among nurses and radiographers in France.
papers.abstract: Rapid technological change in cath labs is redistributing operational responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers. We aimed to quantify this redistribution, and to assess whether training, regulatory framing, and professional recognition have kept pace. A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2025 among 371 professionals in French catheterisation or electrophysiology laboratories (207 nurses, 60 radiographers, 78 cardiologists, 26 nurse managers). The primary outcome - perceived change in responsibilities - was analysed as binary (moderate or strong increase vs other responses) by logistic regression adjusted for profession, age, sex, and seniority. A strong increase in responsibilities of nurses and radiographers was reported by 54.6% of nurses and 48.3% of radiographers, versus 25.6% of cardiologists and 38.5% of nurse managers. Nurse/radiographer status was the strongest predictor (adjusted OR 6.11 [95% CI 2.86-13.66] vs cardiologists and nurse managers; p < 0.001). Training was predominantly apprenticeship-based (on-the-job mentoring, 66.3%); the perceived adequacy of nurses' and radiographers' initial training was rated 20/100 by nurses and 31.5/100 by radiographers, versus 40/100 by cardiologists (p < 0.001). About half of nurses and radiographers considered that procedures are often performed outside the formal regulatory scope (52% and 45%, respectively); 93% of nurses and 90% of radiographers demanded regulatory clarification. Technology is redistributing responsibilities towards nurses and radiographers faster than training, regulatory framing, or recognition - a readiness gap perceived far more acutely by paramedical than medical professionals. Every technology deployment should integrate team readiness, regulatory clarification, and recognition commensurate with current practice.

papers.title: Mosaic CDKL5 deficiency drives progressive inhibitory circuit remodelling.
papers.abstract: CDKL5 deficiency disorder predominantly affects heterozygous females, in whom random X-chromosome inactivation generates cellular CDKL5 mosaicism. Although mosaicism is a defining feature of the disease, whether it actively drives disease progression or simply reflects the genetic mode of inheritance remains unknown. Here, we combined age-comparative electrophysiology, quantitative synaptic imaging, transcriptomic profiling and postmortem human brain analyses to determine how mosaic CDKL5 deficiency shapes inhibitory circuit remodeling during disease progression. Heterozygous Cdkl5 female mice exhibited striking age- and region-specific remodeling of inhibitory neurotransmission. Hippocampal inhibition was initially enhanced but progressively declined with age, whereas cortical inhibitory transmission remained preserved at 3 months and increased in middle-aged animals. These functional changes were accompanied by dynamic remodeling of inhibitory presynaptic terminals, persistent disruption of inhibitory synapse organization and reduced hippocampal gephyrin-positive puncta despite preservation of the major inhibitory interneuron populations. At 12 months, heterozygous females also exhibited a higher density of IBA1/CD68 double-positive microglia in both regions compared with age-matched wild-type controls. Importantly, complete Cdkl5 deficiency failed to reproduce the progressive loss of inhibitory presynaptic terminals observed in heterozygous females, indicating that this phenotype is specific to the mosaic condition rather than a simple consequence of complete Cdkl5 loss. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a temporal transition from alterations detected at 3 months in immune-synaptic regulatory pathways to activity-dependent transcriptional programs associated with reduced structural and homeostatic support, consistent with progressive hippocampal circuit reorganization. Exploratory analyses of postmortem cortical tissue from individuals with CDD revealed differences in inhibitory presynaptic labeling between the available young and adult cases, suggesting that inhibitory alterations may also vary with age in human CDD. Together, these findings identify mosaic CDKL5 deficiency as a biologically distinct circuit state characterized by progressive, region-specific inhibitory circuit remodeling and provide a mechanistic framework for disease progression in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.

papers.title: Evaluation of the role of P2 neurons on female post-mating changes in sleep and feeding in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: In many insects, females exhibit behavioral changes after mating. This plasticity can be mediated by interactions between male-derived seminal fluid proteins (SFPs) and the female nervous system. The Drosophila melanogaster seminal fluid protein Sex Peptide (SP) causes mated females to sleep less during the day and consume more food than unmated females, among other behavioral changes. Although the SP-sensing neural circuits that convey information to the female's brain are known, the downstream neurons that affect post-mating behaviors remain unknown. P2 neurons in the fly's central brain are good candidates for regulating post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption, as they express feeding- and sleep-responsive neuropeptide F (NPF), directly innervate the fly's sleep center (the dorsal fan-shaped body, dFB), and are responsible for social-isolation-induced changes in sleep and food consumption. Using the GAL4/UAS system, we activated or silenced P2 neurons in mated and unmated females. We measured sleep duration using Drosophila Activity Monitors (DAM) and food consumption using Capillary Feeder (CAFE) and blue-dye assays. We found that P2-neurons are not responsible for post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption: mated females slept less during the day and ate more compared to unmated females irrespective of P2 neuron perturbation. Together, these results indicate that P2 neurons are unlikely to be primary downstream neurons through which male-transferred SP regulates post-mating sleep and food consumption. Future studies could determine whether P2 neurons regulate other post-mating behaviors or modulate sleep and feeding behaviors in a context-dependent manner.

papers.title: Dairy consumption in relation to psychological distress and sleep quality: findings from a large cross-sectional study in Turkish adults.
papers.abstract: Growing evidence suggests that dairy consumption may play a multifaceted role in human health; however, its simultaneous association with mental well-being and sleep quality remains poorly understood. This study investigated the associations between dairy product consumption and psychological status, and sleep quality in healthy Turkish adults. Data were collected from 4008 adults, including demographics, general health, and anthropometric measurements. Dairy consumption was determined using a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire, and daily intake was calculated. Sleep quality was measured using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and psychological status using the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Multinomial logistic regression models were used to examine the association between dairy consumption and psychological status, with adjustment for age, gender, and PSQI score. The mean age of participants was 37.9 ± 11.3 years (52%, female). In total, 2188 participants (54.6%) had poor sleep quality. Increasing stress, anxiety, and depression severity were associated with a lower likelihood of meeting the recommended dairy products intake. Specifically, moderate stress (OR = 0.61; 95%CI: 0.48-0.79; p < 0.001), extremely severe anxiety (OR = 0.51; 95%CI: 0.38-0.69; p < 0.001), and moderate depression (OR = 0.75; 95%CI: 0.60-0.95; p = 0.017) were associated with a lower probability of adequate dairy consumption. No significant differences were observed regarding sleep quality (p = 0.252). Higher levels of stress, anxiety, and depression were associated with a lower likelihood of meeting the recommended daily intake of dairy products, while no significant association was observed between dairy consumption and sleep quality. However, due to our cross-sectional design, these findings indicate associations rather than causal relationships. Therefore, both dairy consumption quantities and personal, psychological, and metabolic factors should be considered, and prospective studies are needed to clarify directionality.

papers.title: Health-related quality of life and its factors among rural middle-aged and older adults with multimorbidity in China: based on the health ecology model.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is common among rural middle-aged and older adults and is associated with poorer health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Evidence on HRQoL in this population remains limited in China, particularly from nationally representative data. This study examined factors associated with HRQoL among rural Chinese middle-aged and older adults with multimorbidity. We conducted a secondary analysis of the 2020 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. The analysis included 1,411 rural participants aged 45 years or older with multimorbidity. HRQoL was measured using the EuroQol five-dimensional three-level questionnaire (EQ-5D-3 L). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for variable selection, and Tobit regression was used to estimate associations between selected variables and EQ-5D-3 L utility score. In the Tobit regression model, male was positively associated with EQ-5D-3 L utility score (β = 0.089, 95% CI: 0.018 to 0.159). Having three or more chronic conditions (β = - 0.175, 95% CI: - 0.287 to-0.063), poorer self-rated health (β = - 0.148, 95% CI: - 0.184 to-0.112), depressive symptoms (β = - 0.524, 95% CI: - 0.591 to-0.458), and disability (β = - 0.576, 95% CI: - 0.734 to-0.418) were negatively associated with EQ-5D-3 L utility score. Sleep duration of ≥ 9 h (β = 0.138, 95% CI: 0.015 to 0.261) and alcohol drinking (β = 0.109, 95% CI: 0.003 to 0.215) were positively associated with EQ-5D-3 L utility score. Healthcare utilization was also associated with EQ-5D-3 L utility score (β = - 0.069, 95% CI: - 0.132 to-0.005). In this secondary analysis of CHARLS data, several individual, behavioural, and policy-related factors were associated with HRQoL among rural Chinese middle-aged and older adults with multimorbidity. These findings may help identify population groups with lower HRQoL and inform future studies and health-management strategies in rural settings.
papers.journal: Health and quality of life outcomes

papers.title: Latent profile analysis of sleep quality among newly employed nurses: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Newly employed nurses face unique challenges during role transition, making them particularly vulnerable to sleep disturbances. However, traditional assessments overlook the heterogeneity of sleep problems in this population. This study employed latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify distinct sleep quality subgroups and explore factors associated with profile membership. A cross-sectional study was conducted from July to September 2024, recruiting 398 newly employed nurses (mean age 22.7 ± 1.7 years; 91.5% female) from a tertiary hospital in China. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) (poor sleep quality defined as total score > 5), and psychological status was evaluated with the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21). LPA was performed based on seven PSQI dimensions, followed by chi-square tests, ANOVA, and multinomial logistic regression to identify factors associated with profile membership. Three latent profiles were identified: healthy sleep group (19.6%, n = 78), suboptimal sleep group (48.5%, n = 193), and sleep disorder group (31.9%, n = 127). The three profiles were approximately parallel and differed primarily in overall severity rather than in the shape of the component profile: mean component scores were uniformly low in the healthy sleep group (0.47-0.67), intermediate in the suboptimal sleep group (1.74-1.89) and uniformly high in the sleep disorder group (2.43-2.65), with subjective sleep quality showing the highest relative elevation in the latter. Multinomial logistic regression (with the healthy sleep group as reference) revealed that regular physical activity was significantly associated with better sleep quality in both the suboptimal sleep group (OR = 0.495, 95%CI: 0.279-0.880) and sleep disorder group (OR = 0.410, 95%CI: 0.212-0.795). Anxiety was significantly associated with poorer sleep quality in both groups (suboptimal: OR = 1.138, 95%CI: 1.044-1.241; sleep disorder: OR = 1.161, 95%CI: 1.055-1.277). Compared to neurotic personality (reference), extraversion (OR = 0.084, 95%CI: 0.010-0.706), agreeableness (OR = 0.060, 95%CI: 0.007-0.487), conscientiousness (OR = 0.088, 95%CI: 0.010-0.747), and openness (OR = 0.047, 95%CI: 0.005-0.445) were associated with significantly lower odds of belonging to the sleep disorder group. Passive avoidance coping style (OR = 5.729, 95%CI: 1.200-27.349) was also significantly associated with the sleep disorder group. Sleep quality among newly employed nurses demonstrates significant heterogeneity, with 80.4% classified into one of the two profiles characterized by sleep problems. Given the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported measures, causal relationships cannot be established and associations may be subject to recall and social desirability biases. Because the profiles differed in overall severity rather than in symptom pattern, nursing administrators should develop graded, stepped-care intervention strategies matched to profile severity, focusing on promoting physical activity participation, enhancing anxiety management, and cultivating adaptive coping strategies to improve sleep quality in this population.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration and sleep-timing patterns with depressive mood and suicidal outcomes in Korean adolescents.
papers.abstract: Sleep duration, sleep timing, and weekday-weekend sleep-timing differences are interrelated characteristics associated with adolescent mental health. Categorizing continuous measures and interpreting mutually adjusted estimates as independent effects may obscure nonlinear patterns and their shared derivation. We examined associations of corrected mid-sleep on free days (MSFsc), weekly average sleep duration, and the absolute weekday-weekend sleep midpoint difference with depressive mood and suicidal outcomes. This cross-sectional study used data from the nationally representative 2025 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey. Descriptive analyses included 48,426 adolescents with valid sleep-derived variables, and adjusted models included 48,416 complete cases. Survey-weighted logistic regression with restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinear associations of the three continuous sleep descriptors with depressive mood, suicidal ideation, suicide plan, and suicide attempt. Secondary analyses examined categorical sleep-timing groups, sequential adjustment models, and exploratory combined sleep-timing group-sleep-duration profiles. Weekly average sleep duration and the absolute weekday-weekend sleep midpoint difference were associated with all four outcomes. Sleep duration was nonlinear for all outcomes, with higher odds at shorter durations. The midpoint difference was nonlinear only for depressive mood and was otherwise generally monotonic. MSFsc showed overall and nonlinear associations with depressive mood, suicidal ideation, and suicide plan, but not suicide attempt in the primary analysis (overall p = 0.054; nonlinearity p = 0.993); this result was sensitive to exclusion of extreme MSFsc values. Categorical sleep-timing group estimates changed substantially after adjustment for sleep duration and midpoint difference. In exploratory combined-profile analyses, < 5 h of sleep was associated with higher odds across all sleep-timing groups, but only 4 of 72 direct contrasts remained significant after false-discovery-rate adjustment. Very short sleep duration and larger weekday-weekend sleep midpoint differences showed the most consistent associations with depressive mood and suicidal outcomes. MSFsc associations varied across outcomes and were less robust for suicide attempt. Because the sleep descriptors share timing information, mutually adjusted estimates should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than independent causal effects. Longitudinal studies using more detailed circadian and sleep measures are needed.

papers.title: Associations of rotating shift work with depressive symptoms among Chinese nurses: exploratory indirect associations through sleep problems.
papers.abstract: Rotating shift work has been associated with depressive symptoms, but its association with depressive symptom severity and the statistical intermediary pattern involving sleep quality remain incompletely understood. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data (2021-2024) from the Chinese Nurses' Health Cohort Study (TARGET), including 43,697 registered nurses from 105 hospitals across 15 provinces in China. Primary analyses compared rotating shifts with fixed day shifts, while fixed night shifts were included in sensitivity analyses. Depressive symptoms and sleep quality were assessed using the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Multivariable ordinal and binary logistic regression models were used to estimate associations. Exploratory model-based indirect associations were estimated using probit models with bootstrap resampling. Among the participants, 93.8% were women and 64.4% worked rotating shifts. Compared with fixed day shifts, rotating shifts were consistently associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms across four cumulative PHQ-9 contrasts (OR range, 1.471-1.500; all P < 0.001) and with poor sleep quality (OR, 1.592; 95% CI, 1.514-1.674; P < 0.001). Poor sleep quality statistically accounted for 38.6% (95% CI, 34.2%-43.2%) of the observed association between rotating shifts and depressive symptoms under the fitted model. All seven PSQI components showed statistically supported indirect associations. Sleep latency had the numerically largest estimated percentage statistically accounted for (39.3%; 95% CI, 24.2%-45.0%). In the reverse-pathway specification, depressive symptoms statistically accounted for 14.8% (95% CI, 13.7%-16.0%) of the observed association between rotating shifts and poor sleep quality. Rotating shifts were consistently associated with greater depressive symptom severity and poor sleep quality. The observed statistical intermediary patterns highlight sleep quality, particularly sleep latency, as an important priority for assessment and for prospective evaluation of sleep-focused strategies among nurses working rotating shifts. Although causal direction cannot be established from these cross-sectional data, the findings provide a focused basis for future longitudinal and interventional research. TARGET, ChiCTR2100043202 and ChiCTR2300072756. Initial registration completed on 8 February, 2021.

papers.title: Sleep apnea is associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
papers.abstract: There are few data on the incidence and related risk factors and adverse outcomes of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in patients receiving maintenance peritoneal dialysis (PD). In this observational retrospective, multicenter real-world study we included all patients that received PD for over 30 days in 2009-2019 in two research hospitals. The primary and secondary outcomes of the study were the incidence of NOAF and electrical direct current cardioversion (DCCV) during PD. Incident strokes and mortality were also recorded. Altogether 401 patients with a median PD treatment duration of 1.6 years (IQR 0.9-2.8 years or 850 patient-years) comprised the total study cohort and 64 (16%) had a prior diagnosis of AF. NOAF was observed in 46 (13.6%) of the 337 patients without prior history of AF corresponding with the incidence rate of 6.3 per 100 patient-years. In a multivariable Cox model, cirrhosis (HR 5.536, CI95% 1.266-24.207, p = 0.023) coronary artery disease (CAD) (HR 2.268, CI95% 1.178-4.366, p = 0.014) and sleep apnea (HR 2.472, CI95% 1.010-6.048, p = 0.047) were independently associated with incident NOAF during PD but only the association with sleep apnea remained significant (HR 3.182, CI95% 1.399-7.238, p = 0.006) in a further multivariable Cox model adjusted with age, sex, CAD and PD vintage. Moreover, the observed percentage of NOAF during PD was as high as 50% in patients over 60 years old with a prior diagnosis of sleep apnea. Furthermore, 18 DCCVs in 6 patients and 27 (6.7%) strokes were observed and 100 (24.9%) patients died during PD care out of the total study cohort. The occurrence of NOAF was not associated with the incidence of stroke or mortality during PD. In this real-world multicenter study, a substantially high incidence of NOAF and an expectedly low occurrence of DCCVs in patients receiving maintenance PD was observed. Furthermore, an independent association between sleep apnea and the risk of NOAF in this patient population was observed.

papers.title: Daily patterns and prevalence of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia in Swedish nursing homes.
papers.abstract: Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) are among the principal observable expressions of psychological distress and unmet need in nursing home residents who can no longer reliably verbalize internal experiences, and recognizing their day-to-day variation underpins timely, person-centered care. Yet BPSD fluctuate across days, shifts, and contexts, while established instruments such as the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Nursing Home version (NPI-NH) assess them retrospectively over the preceding weeks or months. This mismatch leaves basic descriptive questions about the day-to-day symptom landscape in routine care unanswered. This study describes the prevalence, severity, co-occurrence, between-unit variation, and shift and weekday patterns of BPSD documented through structured daily registrations in nursing home care. Descriptive longitudinal observational study of 230 individuals with dementia in six nursing homes across six Swedish municipalities, followed for a median observation period of 270 days (interquartile range 120 to 446). Care staff used a digital tool to rate the severity (0-3) of twelve common BPSD, adapted from the NPI-NH, at the end of every work shift, yielding over one million symptom registrations. Analyses were descriptive and person-weighted, giving each individual equal weight regardless of observation length. Cumulative symptom prevalence (at any point during observation) ranged from 90% (agitation) to 70% (euphoria). Each symptom's mean daily prevalence was much lower (4-18%), and symptoms were predominantly of low severity. At least one symptom was recorded on a median of 43.5% of registered days, varying widely between individuals. Clinically related symptoms tended to occur together, consistent with established NPI-NH domain structures, and the mean number of symptoms per day varied more than twofold across the six units. Symptoms were most frequent on evening shifts and least frequent at night, except sleep disturbances, with little variation across weekdays. Just under half of all possible shift registrations were completed. Daily registrations describe an intermittent and heterogeneous symptom landscape at a resolution that periodic assessments are not designed to provide. These findings provide an empirical baseline for future multilevel analyses and support BPSD monitoring that covers both individual symptoms and the daily number of symptoms in nursing homes. Not applicable.

papers.title: Delayed-onset seizure after dantrolene-treated malignant hyperthermia in a patient with traumatic brain injury and a pathogenic RYR1 variant: a multiple-hit model.
papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a life-threatening pharmacogenetic disorder primarily affecting skeletal muscle via ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1) hyperactivation. Central nervous system (CNS) complications following MH are rarely reported, and the role of dantrolene in preventing or treating such sequelae remains unclear. Patients with concurrent traumatic brain injury (TBI) present a particularly complex scenario where multiple etiologies for neurological complications may converge. We report a 53-year-old male with a confirmed pathogenic RYR1 variant (c.7108_7109delinsAAGCC, p.Gly2370delinsLysPro) who developed fulminant MH during emergency intracranial hematoma evacuation following traumatic brain injury with extensive cerebral contusions. Clinical data were collected prospectively during the ICU course, including continuous EEG monitoring, serial neuroimaging, and detailed documentation of seizure characteristics and treatment responses. The relationship between MH, TBI, and delayed seizure was analyzed through a multifactorial etiological framework. In patients with MH and concomitant TBI, delayed seizures may arise primarily from the structural brain injury (cerebral contusions and/or the surgical manipulation of hematoma evacuation), although acute systemic insult (MH) and potential genetic susceptibility (RYR1 variant) could represent additional, unconfirmed contributing factors.Dantrolene should not be relied upon for CNS complications, as its limited CNS penetration and RyR1 selectivity render it ineffective for seizure control.This case suggests that CNS sequelae deserve consideration in MH patients with overlapping risk factors, while recognizing that traumatic brain injury remains the most likely primary cause of seizure in this setting.

papers.title: Sleep quality is associated with gut microbiome signatures of hyperuricemia in Chinese elderly adults: a community-based case-control study.
papers.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) has become a global health issue due to its rapidly increasing prevalence. Growing evidence from population and animal studies suggests that gut microbial dysbiosis and lifestyle changes are involved in serum uric acid metabolism. However, most existing studies are limited by small sample sizes or have yielded inconsistent findings. This study aimed to jointly investigate the associations of the gut microbiome, lifestyles, and dietary habits with HUA in Chinese elderly adults. A community-based case-control study was conducted across nine provincial-level regions in China, involving 617 participants. Data collection included lifestyle and dietary habit questionnaires, chronic disease history, serum uric acid (sUA) measurement, and 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal samples. Taxonomic composition and diversity analyses revealed significant difference between the HUA and controls in gut microbiota structure and diversity. Through differential abundance and co-occurrence network analyses, 42 microbial signatures associated with HUA or sUA were identified. Notably, the prevalence of g_Stenotrophomonas was positively associated with short sleep duration. A microbial risk score (MRS) model constructed using these signatures demonstrated an area under curve (AUC) of 0.761 in the discovery cohort and 0.675 in the validation cohort. Furthermore, a significant positive association was observed between sleep quality (sleep duration, number of awakenings, and short sleep duration) and the MRS model. These results add to the accumulating evidence implicating the role of gut microbiota and sleep in HUA, such as g_Stenotrophomonas, and inform the potential effect of the microbiome-based association between sleep duration and HUA. However, due to the cross-sectional design, we cannot infer causality from these associations, and the observed findings should be confirmed in prospective studies.

papers.title: Neuronal Firing Frequency-based State Classification of the Lateral Habenula and Ventral Tegmental Area Microcircuit under Deep Brain Stimulation.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have suggested that depression is associated with hyperactivity of the lateal habenula (LHb), which is characterized by high-frequency burst firing, accompanied by increased firing frequency of GABAergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA). In this study, we constructed a L H b ↔ V T A GABA microcircuit model to investigate this phenomenon from three perspectives. First, by modulating the conductances of the T-type calcium channel and NMDA receptor in the LHb neuron, two circuit firing activity patterns corresponding to the normal and depressed states were simulated, and the corresponding datasets X n and X d were obtained. Then, in the depressed state, strengthening the GABAergic inhibitory projection to the LHb neuron could partially reverse this firing pattern. Finally, with the LHb neuron as the deep brain stimulation (DBS) target, Mahalanobis distance (MD)-based state quantification revealed difference in circuit states under different DBS parameter conditions. Combined with a clustering-based approach, the circuit state was further classified using the clustering results associated with the minimum summed MDs from samples x DBS in each cluster to the X n and X d . The results showed that the circuit state can be classified as normal under certain DBS parameter conditions, suggesting that DBS can alleviate the depressed state of the circuit to some extent. The findings may provide insights for further research on the firing activity of depression-related neurons and the identification of the depression.

papers.title: Altered heart-brain coupling in awake patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) represents a prodromal stage of alpha-synucleinopathies, frequently preceding Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Beyond the characteristic sleep disturbances, alterations in brain-body coupling, reflecting neural peripheral physiological interactions, have yet to be determined. Using whole-night polysomnography, we quantified brain-body coupling via heartbeat evoked potentials (HEPs) across wakefulness, NREM, and REM sleep. Individuals with iRBD (n = 13) were compared with healthy controls (n = 23), alongside analyses of ECG-derived features. During wakefulness, iRBD patients showed altered HEPs over frontal regions between 305 and 445 ms after the R-peak. No significant group differences were observed during NREM or REM sleep, and HEP amplitude alterations were not explained by ECG differences. These diurnal HEP changes may represent a novel quantitative biomarker for iRBD during wakefulness and, in the future, could serve as a marker for phenoconversion to alpha-synucleinopathy.

papers.title: The relationship of sleep and sexual function in bipolar disorder during remission.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSleep disturbances and sexual dysfunction are common residual symptoms in bipolar disorder(BD) and may persist during remission. This study aimed to investigate the association between sleep quality and sexual functioning in patients with BD during remission.MethodsThe study included 200 outpatients with BD(100 women, 100 men)who were in remission Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 Disorders(SCID-5), Young Mania Rating Scale(YMRS), and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale(HDRS) criteria were used for clinical evaluations.Sleep quality and daytime sleepiness was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index(PSQI) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale(ESS). Sexual functioning was evaluated with the Female Sexual Function Index(FSFI) in women and the International Index of Erectile Function-15(IIEF-15) in men.ResultsPoor sleep quality was observed in 45.5% of patients. Higher ESS and PSQI scores were associated with lower sexual-function scores in both sexes. Poor sleepers had significantly lower FSFI and IIEF scores, whereas categorical excessive daytime sleepiness was not associated with sexual-function scores. In adjusted sex-specific models, higher PSQI scores remained associated with lower FSFI and IIEF scores.ConclusionPoorer sleep quality was associated with poorer sexual functioning in both women and men with BD during remission.These findings support the clinical relevance of assessing sleep quality and sexual functioning concurrently.

papers.title: Disentangling the Spatiotemporal Neural Dynamics of Conflict Detection and Resolution between Lexical and Sublexical Processes in Oral Word Reading: An Intracranial SEEG Study.
papers.abstract: Object recognition relies on correspondence between whole objects and their subcomponents. When this correspondence is disrupted, accurate recognition requires detecting conflicts and inhibiting misleading subcomponent information, yet the neural basis underlying these processes remain unclear. Written language, with sublexical components that may conflict with whole words, provides an ideal testbed. Using stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recorded from 39 participants (both sexes) during Chinese character reading, we revealed a functional dissociation between neural systems supporting conflict detection and inhibitory control. Conflict detection was associated with β band activity in the fusiform gyrus and widespread θ and α band effects across temporal and parietal regions. Inhibitory control was associated with α and β band activity in the inferior frontal and precentral gyri. Granger causality analysis showed increased β band connectivity from conflict-processing to inhibitory-control regions under conflict conditions. These findings demonstrate that disruptions of whole-sublexical correspondence engage dissociable neural systems for conflict detection and inhibitory control, implemented through frequency- and region-specific neural oscillations and coordinated via increased information transfer from posterior to frontal regions.Significance Statement Reading often requires resolving conflicts between competing linguistic representations, yet the neural mechanisms that detect such conflicts and resolve them remain poorly understood. Using stereo-electroencephalography with millimeter-scale spatial and millisecond-scale temporal resolution, we dissociated sublexical conflict detection from inhibitory control during Chinese character reading. We show that these processes are supported by distinct low-frequency oscillatory networks and are linked through directed functional interactions. These findings move beyond traditional accounts of sublexical effects by identifying their underlying cognitive components and neural dynamics, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how cognitive control supports fluent word recognition.
