papers.title: What Associations Exist Between Physical Activity and Sleep Quality Across College Students' Latent Negative Emotion? Heterogeneity in Negative Emotion Mediation.
papers.abstract: Elevated negative emotions and poor sleep are prevalent among Chinese college students. From the perspective of negative emotion heterogeneity, this study explored group differences in the mediation patterns between physical activity and sleep quality to inform targeted interventions. A cross-sectional design was employed. A total of 1953 college students completed the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Depression-Anxiety-Stress Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Latent profile analysis and mediation analyses were performed using SPSS, Mplus, and MATLAB. Three latent subgroups were identified: the psychological resilience group, the sub-health psychological group, and the multiple distress group. Significant gradient differences in physical activity and sleep quality existed across groups. For the full sample, both direct and indirect associations (mediated by negative emotions) were observed between physical activity and sleep quality. Profile-specific analyses confirmed stable mediation patterns across subgroups. Indirect effects decreased sequentially from the psychological resilience group to the sub-health psychological and multiple distress groups, with mediation proportions of 21.4%, 16.3%, and 17.0%. Given the distinct features of each profile, universities may deliver stratified physical activity guidance. Customized exercise programs are recommended for students with multiple psychological concerns, those from economically disadvantaged families, and freshmen, to help stabilize mental status and improve sleep quality.

papers.title: Unruptured bilateral sinus of Valsalva aneurysms including a giant right coronary sinus aneurysm, presenting as recurrent syncope secondary to ventricular tachycardia.
Cue modality modulates dynamic functional network organization during motor imagery: Evidence from EEG functional connectivity and spatiotemporal decoding.
papers.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) is typically guided by external sensory cues; however, how cue modality and imagery type jointly influence functional connectivity during post-cue MI remains unclear. This study combined functional connectivity analysis with a CNN-TemporalConv-MLP spatiotemporal decoding model to investigate phase-locking value (PLV) differences across visual versus auditory cues and kinesthetic (KMI) versus visual (VMI) motor imagery. Functional connectivity analyses revealed that all connections with significant cue-modality effects in the early theta band showed higher PLV following visual cues. In the beta band, PLV was higher under visual cues in the earlier significant time window, whereas it was higher under auditory cues in the later significant time window. In contrast, differences between KMI and VMI were primarily localized to connections in the theta and alpha bands, while interactions between cue modality and imagery type emerged selectively in the theta, beta, and gamma bands. Decoding analyses showed that PLV functional connectivity features contained discriminative information about both factors. Overall cue-modality decoding achieved moderate performance, and performance improved when KMI and VMI conditions were held constant. By contrast, overall imagery-type classification showed relatively low discriminability. However, KMI versus VMI classification improved within specific cueing backgrounds, with better performance under fixed visual or auditory cues than under mixed cue-modality conditions. These findings indicate that the influence of cue modality can extend into subsequent MI, with functional connectivity differences showing selectivity across time, frequency, and connections. Condition-related differences were evident in both connection-specific PLV effects and deep learning decoding of PLV features.

papers.title: Usefulness of the Current of Injury Function in a Pacing System Analyzers for Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Implantation : A Case Report.
papers.abstract: During left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), the current of injury (COI) follows a characteristic depth-dependent course: it rises as the lead advances through the interventricular septum, then falls as the tip approaches the left ventricular endocardium. This transition has been proposed as a practical procedural endpoint. Such monitoring has conventionally required an electrophysiology (EP) laboratory system, as pacing system analyzers (PSAs) were thought to lack real-time capability. This report describes a 76-year-old man with complete atrioventricular block and preserved ejection fraction (70%) who underwent LBBAP because a high pacing burden was anticipated. An INGEVITY lead and SSPC NXT guiding catheter were used, with simultaneous recording by an EP system and a Boston Scientific PSA equipped with beat-by-beat COI monitoring and a reference-waveform storage function. After the initial screw-in, the COI waveform was stored as a reference at the right ventricular septal position. During subsequent body turns, the COI rose sharply relative to this reference and then declined within tens of seconds. Lead V1 showed a right bundle branch block-like morphology with stable threshold and impedance, and this position was accepted as final. Waveforms from the PSA and the EP system showed comparable temporal patterns. Because absolute COI amplitude varies widely between patients, within-patient comparison against a stored reference allows assessment not only of whether the COI has begun to fall, but how far it has fallen - relevant to the risk of endocardial penetration. Limitations include the single-case design and absence of quantitative analysis.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian disruption as systemic drivers of breast cancer metastasis: A tri-pathway mechanistic model.
papers.abstract: Sleep deficiency and circadian disruption are emerging modifiable risk factors in breast cancer. However, their specific role in driving metastasis remains incompletely defined. This review maps circadian disturbance to metastatic competence through three convergent systemic pathways. First is neuroendocrine disruption via melatonin suppression. Second is immunological dysregulation characterized by chronic inflammation and myeloid derived suppressor cell expansion. Third is metabolic reprogramming involving insulin resistance and altered adipokine signaling. These converging signals lower critical barriers at every step of metastasis. They promote epithelial mesenchymal transition and local invasion. They support circulating tumor cell survival. They enable pre metastatic niche formation. They also trigger reactivation of dormant micrometastases. We evaluate clinical biomarkers of circadian disruption including cortisol rhythms, urinary melatonin, and actigraphy. We link these sleep metrics to patient outcomes. We also discuss therapeutic opportunities such as melatonin supplementation, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, and personalized chrono chemotherapy. By establishing circadian health as an actionable axis in metastasis prevention, this review provides a framework for integrating chronobiology into breast cancer management and survivorship care.

papers.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea, Ferroptosis, and Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Potential Second-Hit Mechanism Linking Intermittent Hypoxia to Fibrotic Progression.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) frequently coexists with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). We examine ferroptosis as a possible mediator of chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH)-associated progression of established fibrosis. PubMed was searched through 11 June 2026 using a defined ferroptosis-fibrosis/sleep-apnea strategy and reference screening. Clinical and experimental evidence was classified qualitatively by model relevance and causal strength. CIH may alter oxidative stress, iron handling, antioxidant defenses and lipid peroxidation. Experimental fibrosis studies implicate ferroptosis-related alveolar epithelial injury and iron-dependent fibroblast activation, while combined IH-fibrosis models demonstrate enhanced injury without establishing ferroptosis mediation. Human OSA-IPF findings are heterogeneous and observational. These observations collectively support a proposed "second-hit" model linking OSA-associated intermittent hypoxia to ferroptosis-related mechanisms in IPF progression. Ferroptosis is a plausible yet unconfirmed mechanism of CIH-associated fibrotic progression. Ferroptosis-targeted treatments have not improved clinical outcomes in OSA-IPF. Cell-specific factorial experiments and prospective cohorts are required.

papers.title: Acute Neurotoxicity Syndromes from Immunotherapy: Emergency and ICU Management.
papers.abstract: Advances in cancer immunotherapy have transformed survival outcomes and driven widespread adoption of these treatments. However, as the population receiving immunotherapy has grown, neurologic complications have increasingly emerged, with rates of 1 to 3% among patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors and 26.9% among chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy recipients across all FDA-approved products. This review focuses on the early recognition and acute management of neurologic toxicities associated with immunotherapy, with particular emphasis on immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) related to CD19 and BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapies. Herein we synthesize current understanding of clinical phenotypes and risk factors for severe neurotoxicity, and review evidence-based approaches to diagnostic evaluation, including neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and laboratory markers. Practical management strategies for severe cases are discussed, including corticosteroid initiation, cytokine-directed immunomodulatory therapies, exploratory therapies, and neurocritical supportive care for fulminant cerebral edema and status epilepticus. We address less common but high-risk neurologic complications associated with CAR T cell therapy beyond ICANS. Lastly, we touch upon key clinical findings and treatments for acute neurologic complications related to immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T cell engagers, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, and engineered T cell receptor therapies.

papers.title: Human neocortical glutamatergic neurons revealed through multimodal profiling.
papers.abstract: The human neocortex underlies higher cognition, yet our understanding of its neuronal diversity is limited by sparse access to viable tissue, inconsistent cell-type definitions, and limited multimodal data. Although single-cell transcriptomics has transformed our understanding of cell type diversity, transcriptomic data alone cannot explain neuronal function. Here, we introduce a multimodal patch sequencing (patch-seq) resource of human neocortical glutamatergic neurons spanning cortical layers 2-6. Combining morphoelectric features with spatial transcriptomic data to provide laminar context, we sampled 39 of 42 transcriptomically defined glutamatergic neuron types. This systematic approach enabled the identification of unique phenotypes for understudied populations in the human neocortex including L4 intratelencephalic, L5/6 near-projecting, and diverse L6 neurons. Human, macaque, and mouse comparisons of transcriptomically homologous L5 neurons reveal that morphoelectric differences across species were subclass specific. This dataset provides a unified multimodal reference for studying human cortical circuitry and neuronal diversity.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses identify candidate regulatory networks associated with cold responses in Winter Rapeseed (Brassica rapa L.).
papers.abstract: Low-temperature stress is a major abiotic factor limiting growth, yield formation, and regional adaptation in rapeseed (Brassica rapa). Elucidating transcriptional regulation and chromatin accessibility changes in cold-tolerant cultivars is essential for understanding cold-adaptation mechanisms and identifying valuable genetic resources. In this study, integrated RNA-seq and ATAC-seq analyses were performed on the cold-tolerant cultivar L7 (Longyou-7) and the cold-sensitive cultivar Lenox under low-temperature stress. L7 exhibited less injury than Lenox after cold treatment, and showed stronger antioxidant defense and osmotic adjustment capacities. Transcriptome analysis revealed more cold-responsive differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in L7 than in Lenox. L7-specific response genes were significantly enriched in MAPK signaling, glutathione metabolism, phenylpropanoid and flavonoid biosynthesis, and circadian rhythm pathways. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) further identified key co-expression modules and candidate hub genes positively correlated with antioxidant capacity and osmotic adjustment. ATAC-seq analysis showed that low-temperature stress induced extensive chromatin accessibility remodeling in rapeseed, with a greater number of differentially accessible regions (DARs) detected in L7 than in Lenox. Integrated analysis of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data identified 613 upregulated and 1068 downregulated genes associated with DARs in L7, exceeding the corresponding numbers in Lenox, namely 429 and 802, respectively. These results indicate more extensive chromatin accessibility changes in L7 and partial overlap between accessibility and expression changes. Commonly responsive genes were mainly enriched in MAPK signaling, phenylpropanoid and flavonoid biosynthesis, starch and sucrose metabolism, and circadian rhythm pathways. The integrated analysis further suggested that ERF, WRKY, MYB, NAC, bHLH, and bZIP transcription factors may play central roles in the regulatory network, although these candidate regulatory relationships require functional validation. Overall, the cold tolerance of L7 may rely on enhanced chromatin accessibility remodeling, transcriptional reprogramming, antioxidant defense, and osmotic adjustment. This study provides candidate regulatory modules and gene resources for deciphering cold-tolerance mechanisms and supporting cold-tolerance breeding in rapeseed.

papers.title: Parents' experiences of supporting their child with down syndrome and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome undergoing non-invasive ventilation.
papers.abstract: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is the standard of care treatment for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome (OSAS) in children with Down Syndrome (DS). Implementation and adherence can be difficult. The aim of this study was to conduct a qualitative exploration of parental experiences of NIV. Semi-structured interviews were completed with 18 parents of children with DS and OSAS treated with NIV. Reflexive Thematic Analysis was utilised. Parents' narratives reflected a journey characterised as "a rollercoaster of ups and downs." Five themes were generated from the interviews including: being intrinsically motivated, sharing the burden, maintaining hope while grappling with the challenges, taking account of the developmental context and finding balance. Unique insights underscored the dynamic role parents play in managing NIV amidst the complexities of their daily lives. The findings highlight the dynamic role parents play in managing NIV alongside the emotional, relational, and practical demands of daily life. By providing insight into both the challenges and adaptations involved, the study may help inform family-centred approaches to supporting children with Down syndrome undergoing NIV.

papers.title: Chronic buprenorphine-associated severe central sleep apnea and desaturation proof of concept.
papers.abstract: Individuals on opioids are found dead in bed and respiratory depression is a potential cause. In contrast to other opioids, buprenorphine, a partial μ-opioid receptor agonist has reduced respiratory depression. However, death has also been reported in individuals using buprenorphine; yet, it is not known if chronic use of buprenorphine could be associated with clinically significant respiratory depression. The purpose of this preliminary study was to determine if chronic buprenorphine use is associated with sleep disordered breathing. A retrospective study of 11 consecutive patients who were using buprenorphine chronically and referred for sleep evaluation. All underwent full night attended polysomnography and polysomnograms were scored page by page by a board-certified sleep physician. Two breathing patterns were observed. First, four patients had central sleep apnea (CSA) with an index of ≥5/h of sleep and an average of 13. When compared to those without CSA, patients with CSA suffered from severe sleep apnea with an apnea hypopnea index (AHI) of 35 (vs.9/hour of sleep) and associated with clinically significant low saturation (75% vs. 87%). Second, the group without significant CSA (CAI <5, n = 7), despite a low AHI, had relatively more sustained desaturation time below 90% (91 vs 51 min), suggesting hypoventilation. Despite improved respiratory safety profile, this preliminary study is the first to provide evidence that chronic use of buprenorphine is associated with clinically significant sleep disorders with two distinct patterns shared with other opioids. These disordered breathing events could be a potential cause of buprenorphine-associated death reported in the literature, a finding also shared with other opioids. Clinicians should be aware of this association.

papers.title: Prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation combined with cognitive training reduces anxiety, daytime sleepiness, and cognitive complaints in women after COVID-19: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Persistent anxiety, disturbed sleep, and subjective cognitive complaints are frequent and often co-occur after COVID-19, especially in women, yet interventions addressing them together are limited. We examined whether adding left-prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to cognitive training reduces these symptoms in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints. In a single-centre, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 30 women with confirmed prior COVID-19 and self-reported cognitive decline (Mini-Mental State Examination ≥ 24; no diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder) were allocated to three groups (n = 10 each): cognitive training plus active tDCS (CT + tDCS), cognitive training plus sham tDCS (CT + sham), or cognitive training only (CT only). Active tDCS targeted the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (2 mA, 20 min; anode F3, return F7) across nine sessions over three weeks. Anxiety (Beck Anxiety Inventory), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), cognition (Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-Revised), reaction times (psychomotor speed), and prefrontal electroencephalographic (EEG) cortical arousal and frontal asymmetry were assessed at baseline and after the ninth session; there was no follow-up. All participants completed the trial (no dropout). Groups were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for the corresponding baseline score, with non-parametric confirmation and false-discovery-rate correction. Relative to both comparison groups, the CT + tDCS group showed significantly lower anxiety and daytime sleepiness and higher global cognition, memory, and fluency, with faster reaction times (all corrected p < .05). Cortical arousal increased and frontal asymmetry shifted toward greater relative left-frontal activation. The CT + sham and CT only groups did not differ from each other, and near-ceiling attention and visuospatial scores were unchanged. Adding left-prefrontal tDCS to cognitive training reduced anxiety and daytime sleepiness and improved cognition and psychomotor speed in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints, with parallel changes in prefrontal EEG markers. Confirmation in larger samples is needed.

papers.title: Time-use composition between sleep, screen use, and physical activity: one-year longitudinal associations with substance use in Canadian adolescents.
papers.abstract: This study examined associations between baseline movement behaviour composition and substance use at one-year follow-up among Canadian adolescents. Longitudinal data from 16,914 students in grades 7 to 12 participating in the 2022-2023 and 2023-2024 waves of the Cannabis, Obesity, Mental health, Physical activity, Alcohol, Smoking, and Sedentary behaviour project in Canada were analyzed. Participants self-reported past-30-day use of alcohol, cannabis, cigarettes, and vapes. Movement behaviours included self-reported sleep duration, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and screen time (television viewing, video gaming, internet surfing, social media use, online communication). Multilevel compositional logistic regression models, adjusted for sociodemographics, school clustering, and baseline use, compared the sample-average composition with compositions differing by 30 min/day between behaviours. Higher relative social media use and online communication were associated with increased odds of substance use, whereas longer relative sleep was associated with lower odds. Compositions with 30 min/day less social media or online communication and more MVPA, sleep, television, or video gaming were associated with lower odds of all four outcomes (OR range: 0.81 to 0.97). Compositions with less television and more sleep were associated with lower odds of cannabis use (OR = 0.93) and smoking (OR = 0.91). Compositions with less video gaming and more MVPA or social media were associated with higher odds of alcohol consumption (OR = 1.08 and OR = 1.09, respectively). Movement behaviours and adolescent substance use appear to share a compositional relationship. Findings suggest that public health interventions could move beyond generic screen time limits and prioritize targeted digital literacy and sleep promotion.

papers.title: Neural processing dynamics and social cognition in children with ADHD: a dimensional EEG/ERP approach.
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological correlates of social-cognitive difficulties in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remain inconsistent. We examined whether component-based EEG/ERP indices of facial emotion processing were associated with theory of mind and empathy, and whether any association held beyond diagnostic status. Sixty-one children aged 8-12 years (35 with ADHD, 26 healthy controls) completed the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET); parents completed the Griffith Empathy Measure (GEM). EEG was recorded while children viewed happy, sad and neutral faces. Peak amplitude and latency measures were organized into contrast and summary indices and reduced with principal component analysis. Bootstrap regression models were followed by sensitivity models adding group status, restricted to the ADHD group, and examining influential observations. Children with ADHD had lower RMET (r = .48) and GEM (r = .33) scores. Anterior and neutral-face latency indices were longer in ADHD (r = .30 and .35), but no electrophysiological index survived false discovery rate correction. Symptom severity predicted RMET only through the between-group difference: it was unrelated to RMET once group was modelled and within the ADHD group. In contrast, an amplitude-reactivity component (β = .38) and a latency-reactivity component (β = .55) predicted empathy independently of symptom severity, and remained significant after adjustment for group and within the ADHD group. Poorer theory of mind in ADHD reflected a categorical group difference, whereas ERP indices of emotional-versus-neutral differentiation tracked parent-reported empathy dimensionally, across and within groups. These exploratory findings require replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Effects of heart rate variability biofeedback and relaxation training on ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity in young patients with depressive disorders: An EEG study.
papers.abstract: Heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB) may enhance cardiac autonomic regulation and modulate emotion-related brain regions, including the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC). This study compared the effects of HRVB and relaxation training (RT) on electroencephalography (EEG) current source density (CSD) in the bilateral vmPFC of young patients with depressive disorder. Fifty-nine patients were assigned to the HRVB (n = 30) or RT (n = 29) groups and received 60-min sessions twice weekly for five weeks. The HRVB group underwent resonance-frequency breathing with heart rate variability feedback, whereas the RT group underwent relaxation training with heart-rate feedback. After exclusions due to arrhythmia, drop-out, or EEG-related issues, 45 patients were included in the final analysis (HRVB, n = 22; RT, n = 23). Eyes-closed EEG was recorded during pre test rest, post-test rest, and post-test transfer stages. Group × Time effects on bilateral vmPFC CSD were examined across six frequency bands. Compared with the RT group, the HRVB group exhibited greater right vmPFC beta3 CSD and left vmPFC high-beta CSD during the transfer stage. Both groups exhibited increased theta CSD across the stages, indicating shared relaxation effects. HRVB may engage vmPFC-related regulatory processes beyond the relaxation effect observed in RT.

papers.title: Retrieving mangrove biochemical traits under oil pollution using hyperspectral data and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Mangrove forests are essential in improving coastal resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration. However, they are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures, particularly pollution such as oil contamination, which can induce long-term physiological stress in mangrove vegetation. Yet, monitoring the health of such ecosystems across large areas is difficult due to the scarcity of ground-based data and the spatial resolution-coverage trade-off. In light of this, we propose a scalable deep learning framework that incorporates hyperspectral imagery and transfer learning to classify mangrove species and retrieve canopy-level biochemical traits, including pigments, sugars, and phenols. The framework is a Multi-Task Convolutional Neural Network (MTS-CNN) organized in a teacher-student architecture with pseudo-labeling. The teacher model, trained on airborne hyperspectral imagery at 0.5 m resolution, generates pseudo-labels and transfers its learned weights to student models developed on satellite datasets from PRISMA (5 m, pansharpened) and EnMAP (30 m), enabling knowledge transfer from high- to lower-resolution sensors. Despite differences in spatial resolution, the predicted biochemical patterns remained spatially consistent across sensors. Results show accuracies above 95% for airborne data, approximately 70% for PRISMA, and 60% for EnMAP. Spectral analysis additionally confirmed that the predicted classes retained key absorption features characteristic of the target biochemical compounds. Furthermore, the resulting maps could distinguish biochemical signatures associated with oil contamination from those caused by other stressors. These results demonstrate that cross-scale transfer learning can support broad monitoring of mangrove ecosystems by propagating biochemical information from high-resolution observations to satellite hyperspectral imagery.

papers.title: Multi-level insights into the umami perception of Agrocybe aegerita tripeptides: molecular docking, cell signaling, and electroencephalography.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides from Agrocybe aegerita exhibit distinctive umami characteristics, yet systematic studies integrating multiple umami-related receptors with multi-level evidence remain scarce. Here, five umami tripeptides (ENG, PEG, DEL, ECG, and DDL) were evaluated at the molecular, cellular, and neural levels. Molecular docking results suggest that these umami peptides may potentially interact with T1R1/T1R3, CaSR, and GPRC6A, and that different peptide-receptor combinations exhibit certain differences in interaction. In STC-1 cells, the peptides altered receptor mRNA expression and evoked biphasic, concentration-dependent intracellular Ca2+ responses and ATP increases. Electroencephalography showed that the peptides modulated cortical activity mainly in the low-frequency δ band associated with taste processing. DDL produced the strongest and most consistent responses across all assays-plausibly linked to its compact acidic sequence and preferential T1R3 binding. Overall, these findings provide multi-level evidence for the umami activity of A. aegerita peptides and a basis for developing natural flavor enhancers.

papers.title: From stomatal movements to immunity and long-distance signaling: Ion channels mark the spot.
papers.abstract: Beyond their established role in mineral nutrition, ion channels have been increasingly recognized as central hubs of plant signaling across multiple scales. Early research revealed functions in stomatal regulation and nutrient transport, with recent breakthroughs highlighting their critical involvement in immunity, development, and long-distance signaling via membrane potential dynamics and diverse ion fluxes. Multiple channels have been characterized as ligand, voltage, or mechanosensitive gated, often modulated by phosphorylation, effectively functioning as integrative hubs of defined stimuli. Structural characterization is now complementing electrophysiology, live-cell imaging, and mass spectrometry, allowing new levels of mechanistic characterization of ion channels in the context of signaling networks and offering new opportunities to engineer plant resilience to stress.

papers.title: The potential of transcranial direct current stimulation to enhance P300-based brain-computer interface speller performance: A feasibility study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) enhances the P300 event-related potential (ERP) and whether this enhancement translates into improved target-non-target automatic classification. Ten participants without known motor impairments, neurological or psychiatric disorders completed real and sham multichannel tDCS sessions in a randomized, counterbalanced, sham-controlled, single-blind crossover design. Each session included pre- and post-stimulation brain-computer interface (BCI) runs using a P300 speller and an attention-demanding task during stimulation. P300 peak amplitudes, R² discrimination between target and non-target events, and channel-wise offline classification accuracy were computed. Fatigue was assessed at four time points. Statistical analyses assessed effects of Stimulation type (real vs. sham) and Time (pre vs. post) on P300-related metrics. An exploratory analysis compared good and poor baseline performers using BCI calibration data. Significant Stimulation × Time interactions in P300 peak amplitude were observed at P3, PO8, POz, and Oz, reflecting differential pre-to-post changes between real and sham stimulation. Channel-wise classification accuracy demonstrated a significant interaction between Stimulation and Time at P4, indicating a localized improvement in offline target-non-target discrimination after real stimulation. This improvement was not accompanied by improved online character-level BCI performance. Multichannel anodal tDCS over the left DLPFC produced localized neurophysiological P300 modulation in parieto-occipital regions, with a positive trend in channel-wise classification accuracy, reaching statistical significance only at P4. Together with the larger, although non-significant, gains observed in participants with low baseline performance, these findings suggest that tDCS effects may be more pronounced in this subgroup, which is relevant for future translation to clinical populations. These findings support the feasibility of using left DLPFC tDCS to modulate P300-related activity and target-non-target discriminability, while highlighting the need to better understand how localized neurophysiological changes propagate through the complete BCI decoding pipeline.

papers.title: Shift Work Sleep Disorder Among Rotating Night Shift Textile Workers and Its Association with Occupational Accidents.
papers.abstract: Evaluate Shift Work Sleep Disorder (SWSD) prevalence, risk factors and occupational accident association among rotating shift textile workers. A cross-sectional survey of 217 workers was conducted (April-June 2024) using standardized scales (STOP-BANG, ESS, PSQI, ISI). SWSD was defined as ISI≥8 and/or ESS≥11, excluding high OSA-risk (STOP-BANG≥5). Logistic regression identified independent predictors. In 202 analyzed workers, SWSD prevalence was 34%. Workplace accidents were significantly higher in SWSD workers (46% vs 31%, p=0.036). Multivariable analysis revealed Body Mass Index (OR=1.140, 95% CI: 1.054-1.233, p=0.001) and insomnia (OR=2.399, 95% CI: 1.252-4.597, p=0.008) as independent predictors of accidents. SWSD affects one-third of rotating textile workers, significantly associated with higher accident rates. Industrial safety protocols must incorporate objective sleep health management.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine

papers.title: Ictal 18F-FDG PET/CT Findings in Clinically Silent Seizures Caused by a Frontoethmoidal Nasal Meningoencephalocele.
papers.abstract: A 55-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of drug-resistant epilepsy with monthly clinical seizures. Investigation revealed a left frontoethmoidal nasal meningoencephalocele secondary to osseous fibrous dysplasia. Video-EEG failed to capture scalp epileptiform activity, but a concomitant intranasal electrode recorded frequent, clinically silent electrographic seizures. This continuous intranasal EEG recording during the uptake phase of 18F-FDG PET/CT confirmed eight localized subclinical seizures, each lasting 1-3 minutes. The PET scan demonstrated intense focal hypermetabolism at the herniated tissue tip, matching the electrographic EEG ictal activity. Complete endoscopic endonasal lesionectomy rendered the patient seizure-free for 4 years.

papers.title: Investigating 24-Hour Movement Behaviors in Young People With Learning Disabilities: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study.
papers.abstract: Physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep play a key role in the health and development of young people. This has led to the development of guidelines on PA, SB, and sleep for children and young people aged 5 to 17 years. Adherence to these integrated guidelines is associated with favorable physical, mental, and cognitive health outcomes. However, evidence regarding 24-hour movement behaviors (MBs) among young people with learning disabilities is scarce, particularly in the United Kingdom, where no studies have comprehensively examined adherence to all guideline components or explored the factors influencing these behaviors in this population. This study aims to investigate 24-hour MBs among young people with learning disabilities in Scotland, United Kingdom; determine adherence to PA, SB, screen time, and sleep recommendations; assess the feasibility and acceptability of measuring 24-hour MBs in this population; and explore individual, social, and environmental barriers to and facilitators of MBs. This mixed methods study recruited young people aged 11 to 17 years who attended secondary schools for children with additional support needs (ASN) in Scotland. Participants were asked to wear an ActiGraph GT3X accelerometer continuously for 7 consecutive days to objectively assess PA, SB, and sleep. Parent- and youth-completed diaries captured sleep schedules, screen time, and monitored nonwear periods. Individualized activity profiles were produced to summarize participants' daily MBs and support engagement in the qualitative phase. A purposive subsample participated in semistructured interviews exploring experiences, barriers, and facilitators associated with MBs. Quantitative data will be analyzed descriptively to determine MB patterns and guideline adherence, while qualitative data will undergo thematic analysis informed by the capability, opportunity, and motivation-behavior (COM-B) model, the theoretical domains framework and the behavior change wheel. The study was funded by the Baily Thomas Charitable Fund from April 2025 to July 2026. Ethics approval was granted by the University of Strathclyde Ethics Committee (UEC25/10). Recruitment and data collection were completed in June 2026 across participating ASN schools in Scotland. This manuscript describes the study protocol and planned analyses; however, data cleaning and analysis were ongoing at the time of submission. Quantitative and qualitative findings are expected to be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations during 2027. This study is among the first in the United Kingdom to comprehensively examine all components of the 24-hour MB framework in young people with learning disabilities using objective measurement and qualitative inquiry. The findings will provide important evidence on MB patterns, guideline adherence, and modifiable determinants of behavior, informing the development of theory-informed, inclusive interventions designed to improve health and well-being among young people with learning disabilities. papers.title: Immersive Virtual Reality Exergaming vs Video-Guided Screen-Based Exercise for Cognitive and Neurophysiological Adaptations in Young Adults: Protocol for Acute and Chronic Experimental Studies.
papers.abstract: Physical exercise involving simultaneous cognitive demands, including dance-based exergames, has shown moderate effects on executive function. Immersive virtual reality (VR) may enhance these effects by increasing presence and frontal cortical activation; however, evidence in youth integrating objective neurophysiological measures remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous. This study aims to examine the acute and chronic effects of an immersive VR dance exergame, considered as an integrated package of immersion, interactivity, and real-time performance feedback, compared with a matched video-guided screen-based exercise condition (comparator condition [CS]), on inhibitory control as the primary outcome, and on frontal cortical activity, perceived self-efficacy, affective state, and physiological response as mechanistic or secondary outcomes. This protocol reports 2 methodologically independent studies, covered by a single prospective trial registration that describes both, in young adults aged 18 to 30 years: an acute randomized crossover study with up to 40 participants, and a 10-week 2-arm randomized controlled trial with a target sample of 64 participants and 3 sessions per week. In the VR condition, participants will play Beat Saber using Meta Quest 2 headsets. In the CS, they will follow a prerecorded video of the same playlist, matched for songs, tempo, movement sequence, difficulty, transition periods, and session duration. The primary outcome is the Stroop interference index. The confirmatory neurophysiological end point is absolute frontal theta power (4-7 Hz) averaged across F3, F4, AF3, and AF4 during the color-word interference condition. Secondary and exploratory outcomes include additional spectral measures, perceived self-efficacy, affective state, heart rate and percentage of heart rate reserve, rating of perceived exertion, wrist accelerometry, presence, cybersickness, enjoyment, and expectations. Assessments are conducted before and after each session in the acute study and at baseline, midpoint, postintervention, and 4-week follow-up in the chronic study. Linear mixed models accounting for period, sequence, participant, and the within-session pre/post structure will be used, with a prespecified hierarchy of confirmatory and exploratory analyses and false discovery rate correction applied within defined families. Recruitment is expected to begin in October 2026, with data collection completed by December 2027 and first results available by June 2028. No participants had been enrolled at submission. This protocol presents a controlled experimental design to examine the effects of immersive VR exergaming, compared with matched video-guided screen-based exercise, on neurocognitive, psychological, and physiological outcomes. Incorporating immersion-related variables may help clarify the mechanisms underlying VR-based exercise and inform future technology-supported interventions in exercise and cognitive health. papers.title: Linear and nonlinear associations between children's sleep-wake patterns and harsh parenting.
papers.abstract: Harsh parenting is a consistent predictor of children's development, including their sleep. Yet little work has considered how school-age children's sleep may also influence parenting. Addressing this gap, we examined the prospective linear and nonlinear effects of children's sleep on change in harsh parenting over 1 year. Children (N = 298, 46% female, 63% White/European American, 37% Black/African American) and their parents from socioeconomically diverse backgrounds participated in two data collection waves (ages 10 and 11, respectively). Children's sleep was assessed at age 10 utilizing seven nights of actigraphy to derive measures of sleep duration (minutes), sleep quality (efficiency, activity), and chronobiology (sleep midpoint). Parents reported on harsh parenting at ages 10 and 11. Results from latent change score modeling supported a linear dose-response association between sleep activity and change in harsh parenting such that greater sleep activity predicted increases in harsh parenting, and lower sleep activity predicted declines or less steep increases in harsh parenting (β = 0.13). Sleep duration (β = -0.12) and sleep midpoint (β = -0.10) predicted change in harsh parenting in a nonlinear manner. Consistent with a threshold-acceleration model, shorter sleep duration and later sleep midpoint were weakly associated with increases in harsh parenting. After surpassing a critical threshold, beneficial associations emerged such that longer sleep duration and earlier sleep midpoint were progressively linked to declines in harsh parenting. Novel findings build on the literature by considering nonlinear predictors of parenting and applying nonlinear models of sleep to associations beyond developmental outcomes. papers.title: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students.
papers.abstract: Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks. A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used. The network retained 27 non-zero edges, with stronger connections mainly within domains. Daytime dysfunction-stress had the largest positive cross-domain edge-weight point estimate, whereas exercise frequency-stress and exercise duration-subjective sleep quality were prominent negative connections. Stress showed relatively high expected influence and positive bridge expected influence point estimates, although bootstrap difference tests did not clearly distinguish these estimates from those of several other nodes. No gender-related differences were detected in global strength, network structure, or individual edges after multiple-comparison correction, while supplementary analyses indicated limited detection capability. Cross-domain associations among physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were concentrated in a limited number of dimensions, particularly stress, daytime dysfunction, exercise frequency, and exercise duration. Stress and daytime dysfunction showed relatively prominent sleep-psychological distress associations, whereas higher exercise frequency and longer exercise duration were associated with lower stress and fewer subjective sleep problems, respectively. No gender-related network differences were detected, but this does not establish network equivalence. These cross-sectional findings identify dimension-specific associations but cannot establish causal relationships or intervention targets.

papers.title: Social media-related dietary behaviors and integrated behavioral model constructs among university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Social media exposes young adults to nutrition information, food marketing, peer norms, and health-related content. However, evidence on social media-related dietary behaviors and their links to Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) constructs among Saudi university students is limited. This study examined these behaviors, IBM constructs, and factors associated with the Dietary Habits score among King Khalid University (KKU) students. A cross-sectional study included 385 KKU undergraduates, recruited through convenience sampling between February and April 2026. Participants completed the Arabic IBM-based Social Media and Dietary Habits Questionnaire. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc tests, and multiple linear regression. Regression coefficient p-values were adjusted using the Holm-Bonferroni procedure across the 32 coefficient tests. The mean dietary habits score was 12.06 ± 4.17. All IBM constructs were positively correlated with dietary habits (p < 0.001). Exploratory comparisons showed that Dietary Habits scores differed by gender, marital status, BMI, chronic illness, physical activity, smoking, sleep duration, healthy diet, and social media use. The regression model explained 57.6% of the variance in dietary scores (adjusted R² = 0.537). After Holm adjustment, higher scores were linked to attitude (B = 0.199, 95% CI: 0.079-0.319; adjusted p = 0.034), physical activity (B = 1.295, 95% CI: 0.536-2.054; adjusted p = 0.026), and social media use of 1-2 hours/day (B = 2.005, 95% CI: 0.921-3.089; adjusted p = 0.010) or 3-4 hours/day (B = 1.220, 95% CI: 0.511-1.929; adjusted p = 0.024), compared with >4 hours/day. IBM constructs were positively interrelated and associated with social media-related dietary behaviors. Positive attitudes, physical activity, and moderate daily social media use were associated with higher Dietary Habits scores. These findings suggest that behavioral beliefs and lifestyle context may be relevant in the design of digital nutrition programs for university students.

papers.title: Robotic Gait Multi-channel Mu Beta Neurofeedback Training in Paraplegics Enhanced Inter-regional Connectivity and Sensorimotor Functions.
papers.abstract: Complete spinal cord injury (SCI) that severely affects somatosensory and motor functions, greatly challenges advanced neuro-technologies and therapies addressed to repair neural system pathways and recover lost functions. Non-invasive solutions have been explored, reaching encouraging results. This study aims to explore the viability of a novel Neurofeedback (NFB) paradigm for enhancing the modulation of sensorimotor rhythms and cortical connectivity in a robotic-assisted gait training with complete traumatic and chronic SCI individuals. A motor imagery of gait therapy was conducted with Lokomat in two-stages of 12 electroencephalogram NFB sessions to teach the self-modulation of μ (8-12 Hz) and β (15-20 Hz) rhythms. First, a single-channel NFB over Cz using power bands was applied, and later a multi-channel NFB. This last consists of a brain-computer interface that accurately classifies when the individual is performing motor imagery of gait, and further computes μ and β power oscillations on the scalp surface covering motor and somatosensory areas. We observed in complete SCI individuals, improvements modulating power changes and inter-region connectivity for μ and β oscillations, as well as clinical gains covering motor functions, neurogenic bladder management, and functional independence. The encouraging outcomes open doors for developing brain-computer interfaces that empower and regulate both motor rhythms oscillations in brain areas which play an important role during lower-limb movements and walking.

papers.title: Characteristics of EEG Microstate Analysis of Power Grip and Precision Grip Hand Movements from Motor Planning to Execution.
papers.abstract: Hand movement is a fundamental daily motor behavior. Precision grip and power grip reflect distinct post-stroke recovery stages and neuroplasticity, making their neural mechanisms critical for motor control and neurorehabilitation. This study employed electroencephalographic (EEG) microstate analysis to investigate neural dynamic characteristics during motor planning and execution stages between precision grip (two-finger pinch, TP) and power grip (hand clenching, HC). High‑density EEG was acquired from 24 healthy participants across TP, HC, and resting states. Separate microstate analyses were conducted using an event-related potentials (ERP)-based approach for planning and an EEG‑based approach for execution. Results showed that nine ERP microstate templates identified during planning shared identical temporal sequences for both grips, with significantly longer duration of the fourth microstate (MS4) in TP than HC. During execution, four canonical microstates (MSA, B, C, and D) were extracted, which are generally associated with auditory processing, visual processing, default-mode network, and executive attention, respectively. Compared with HC, TP induces stronger suppression of MSC, greater activation of MSD, and distinct transition probabilities with enhanced shifts from MSA, MSB and MSC to MSD. Classification accuracy was higher in the execution stage, with Random Forest reaching 72.07% for TP versus rest. These findings indicate that precision and power grip present consistent temporal sequences of microstate templates during planning but undergo task-specific neural regulation during execution. Precision grip requires more extensive planning processing and stronger suppression of non-motor networks. This study reveals the spatiotemporal neural dynamics underlying different grip types, providing potential biomarkers for motor decoding and advancing neurorehabilitation and brain - computer interface applications.
