papers.title: Effects of mandibular advancement device versus continuous positive airway pressure on cardiac remodeling in obstructive sleep apnea: a randomized CMR substudy.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling, including diffuse myocardial fibrosis. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the standard treatment for OSA, while mandibular advancement devices (MAD) may represent an alternative. However, their comparative effects on myocardial structure remain incompletely defined. To compare the effects of MAD and CPAP on cardiac remodeling assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with OSA. This prespecified CMR substudy of the randomized CRESCENT trial included patients who agreed to participate in both baseline and 12-month CMR examinations (aged 59±8 years, 89% male, with hypertension, elevated cardiovascular risk and moderate-to-severe OSA). The mean body mass index was 28.6±4.6 kg/m2. Participants underwent contrast-enhanced CMR at baseline and after 12 months of treatment with either MAD (n = 36) or CPAP (n = 49). CMR-derived measures included left ventricular (LV) mass, cardiac volumes and function; and extracellular volume (ECV) fraction as a marker of diffuse myocardial fibrosis. At baseline, mean 24-hour systolic blood pressure was 126 ± 11mmHg, ECV fraction was 25.0 ± 2.0% and 27% of participants met CMR criteria of LV hypertrophy. After 12 months, a modest but significant reduction in ECV fraction was observed in patients treated with MAD (24.9 ± 2.3% to 24.0 ± 2.2%; P = 0.047) and CPAP (25.1 ± 1.9% to 24.4 ± 1.6%; P = 0.004). There was no significant difference in ECV fraction reduction between MAD and CPAP (P = 0.576). No significant between-group differences were observed for changes in LV mass, cardiac volumes and function. Both MAD and CPAP were associated with modest reductions in ECV fraction over 12 months, with no detectable between-group difference. No accompanying improvements in LV mass or cardiac function were observed, likely reflecting the predominantly preserved myocardial phenotype at baseline. (Cardiosleep Research Program on Obstructive Sleep Apnea, Blood Pressure Control and Maladaptive Myocardial Remodeling-Non-inferiority Trial [CRESCENT]; NCT04119999). The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-67940-w.

papers.title: Diurnal variation of islet autoantibody titers in established type 1 diabetes suggests restricted-time sampling improves aab measurement and detection.
papers.abstract: Diurnal islet autoantibody (Aab) variation in type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains poorly understood and could hinder efforts to develop, test and refine new therapies. We sought to describe the extent and pattern of diurnal variation in islet autoantibodies and, having found significant variation, translate to the clinical setting. We conducted two studies in human subjects with established T1D: (1) a prospective study (n = 10) of the range of islet autoantibody and immunoglobulin daily variation within humans and (2) an independent retrospective, cross-sectional study (n = 705) of the effect of time of sample collection on Aab titer and detection in clinical settings. We found that some individuals have wide Aab variations during the day and which can exceed expected levels of inter-assay variation. For some Aab, this variation followed a circadian pattern. We also found that, in clinical settings, time-restricted sampling can lead to increased IA-2A and ZnT8A detection within specific age-groups. We conclude that time-restriction can potentially improve the use of Radiobinding-measured Aabs as biomarkers for the development and monitoring of disease-modifying therapies and in developing islet transplantation strategies in established T1D. Investigation of diurnal Aab variation and time restriction is needed in early-stage disease. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-72569-w.

papers.title: Functional characterization and pharmacochaperone rescue of a novel SLC6A1 variant associated with developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
papers.abstract: Mutations in SLC6A1, encoding the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter 1 (GAT-1), are associated with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy syndromes, intellectual disability (ID), and autism. An important question is whether the impact of these mutations can be predicted at scale using artificial intelligence (AI), and how such predictions correlate with experimental findings. In this study, AI was explored as a predictive tool, not as a replacement for data collected experimentally. We reported clinical presentations including seizures and EEG features, autism related phenotypes and motor skills in a novel variant c.1069G > A (p.Ala357Thr, A357T) in two siblings. We used both AI tools and experimental approaches to characterize this novel mutation in the SLC6A1 gene and compared it with another variant in the same amino acid, c.1070 C > T (p.Ala357Val, A357V). Both AI and experimental approaches indicate that the GAT-1(A357T) and (A357V) mutations destabilize the global protein conformation and have increased localization inside the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Additionally, the presence of the mutant GAT-1 made the wildtype GAT-1 less mature. Radioactive 3H-labeled GABA uptake assay indicated the mutation drastically reduced the function of the GAT-1(A357T) compared with the wildtype across cell types and pharmacochaperones such as 4-phenylbutyrate rescued the trafficking and function of the mutant GAT-1. Common and differential clinical phenotypes were identified in the siblings carrying the same variant. Mutant GAT-1 caused increased ER retention and impaired the trafficking of wild type GAT-1. PBA treatment rescued the mutant GAT-1 protein expression and GABA uptake function. AI-assisted in silico protein structural modeling and experimental approaches consistently suggest that the A357T and A357V variants destabilize global GAT-1 protein conformation. AI-assisted protein stability predictions provide supportive structural insight but cannot replace experimental assessment of GAT-1 expression and function. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-72601-z.

papers.title: A mouse model of a rare ASD-implicated patient-derived SCN2A variant.
papers.abstract: Unbiased exome sequencing and family studies have repeatedly identified the voltage-gated NaV1.2 sodium channel gene SCN2A as a top affected ASD-associated locus. Most, but not all, SCN2A ASD-associated variants appear to cause NaV1.2 loss-of-function, and animal models have almost exclusively examined haploinsufficiency and have been studied in the context of the single affected SCN2A locus. De novo single-nucleotide variants, even in loci with large effect sizes like SCN2A, are identified in < 10% of ASD subjects while polygenic variation is additive and contributes to almost all ASD cases. How to interpret SCN2A variants in ASD subjects when the variants do not cause clear loss-of-function, however, is a clinical and experimental challenge. NaV1.2 channels with an R1902C variant in SCN2A previously linked to ASD show biophysical parameters distinct from wild type channels and have reduced interaction with and regulation by key auxiliary proteins, yet preserve significant NaV1.2 function. We generated Scn2a mice with the murine R1903C equivalent and characterized them for ASD phenotypes. We characterized consequences of the variant at the channel, cellular, and circuit level. Homozygous, but not heterozygous, R1903C mice showed key ASD-associated endophenotypes, showing a dose-dependent effect and suggesting that this variant, although insufficient in the heterozygous state, could contribute to ASD in a polygenic background. Electrophysiological characterization showed perturbations at the channel, cellular, and circuit level, many of which were explained by altered interaction with auxiliary subunits due to the amino acid substitution. Our data expand an understanding of the functions of SCN2A in neurons, how auxiliary subunits regulate NaV1.2 channels, and thus how dysregulation of NaV1.2 function can contribute to resulting endophenotypes. Further, the dose-dependent effect of this variant suggests how specific ASD-implicated variants from a locus associated with a large effect size may contribute part of an ASD-associated risk. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-65589-z.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.abstract: Altercentric and egocentric biases (AB, EB) refer to the impact of another agent's/own perspective on the speed with which one can report one's own/another visual perspective respectively. These biases are known to be affected by illnesses and in particular borderline personality (BPD). Coupling the dot-perspective taking task with high-density EEG recordings at the surface and in the inverse space, we analyzed the regional distribution of neural generators related to AB and EB in healthy controls (n = 24) and forensic BPD male patients (n = 14) making comparisons with previous functional MRI data obtained with the same experimental design. In both controls and BPD cases, AB was associated with early EEG activations of visual association areas. In contrast, EB was related to increased use of neural sources in salience, mentalizing networks and mirror neuron areas bilaterally. In forensic BPD patients, no statistically significant differential activation of neural generators was observed in respect to this variable. Our preliminary findings in a small sample of BPD patients show that unlike fMRI observations that pointed to an AB-related widespread increase of BOLD signal in central executive and mentalizing areas, this was not the case at the level of neural generators. Paralleling previous fMRI data, EB was related to increased need of activation of neural sources in visual association areas and later on in several networks involved in social cognition. Such activation was not observed in forensic BPD cases supporting the hypothesis of a decreased ability of these patients in mobilizing their brain resources when treating the Self-Other discrepancy. However, the limited statistical power and post-hoc group-level interaction analysis point to the need for further confirmatory analyses of these first experimental evidences. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64677-4.

papers.title: Mouse bio-behavioral phenotyping using a digital homecage framework for long-timescale, high-resolution, and multi-factor data collection and analytics.
papers.abstract: Long-term monitoring of behavioral and physiological processes is essential for elucidating complex brain-based phenomena and disorders that develop over extended periods, such as chronic stress, circadian disruption, and metabolic syndromes. Though digital phenotyping is well-established in humans via smart devices, comparable solutions for rodent models remain limited. To address this gap, we present the Digital Homecage (DHC) system, an open-source platform that enables uninterrupted, long-timescale recording of over 20 behavioral metrics in single-housed mice. The DHC integrates video capture, operant task modules, and wheel-running data to achieve sub-second resolution in monitoring behaviors such as actigraphy, sleep, grooming, and food choice over periods spanning weeks. Initial data validate the system's capability to reveal circadian patterns across multiple spontaneous behaviors, consistently reflecting nocturnal activity. The DHC offers unique opportunities for longitudinal analyses of chronic conditions and neuropsychiatric syndromes. Its accessibility and modular design promote community-driven innovation, establishing the DHC as a transformative tool for advancing the study of complex traits in rodent models of brain function and behavior. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-69041-0.

papers.title: Disaggregating between- and within- person effects of ovarian hormones on the association between worry and error-related brain activity in a female sample.
papers.abstract: Worry is associated with increased error monitoring in female populations, indexed by a larger error-related negativity (ERN). Although estradiol and progesterone influence anxiety and neural regions involved in error monitoring, little research has examined their role in the association between worry and the ERN. The current study examined how between- and within-person differences in gonadal hormones across the menstrual cycle moderate the association between worry and the ERN in a female sample. Participants (N = 132) provided saliva samples and completed the Penn State Worry Questionnaire daily across a full menstrual cycle. Participants attended up to four in-person laboratory visits during which they completed the Flanker task while concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded. A significant interaction between estradiol and worry emerged (p = .006), such that worry was associated with an enlarged ERN for those with lower estradiol levels. There was also a significant interaction between progesterone and worry in the opposite direction (p < .001). Higher average worry was associated with an enlarged ERN for those with high average progesterone. No significant effects emerged for within-person changes in worry, estradiol and progesterone on the ERN. Our findings highlight the critical need to understand the association between worry and the ERN within a larger neurocognitive framework to elucidate when and for whom worry's effects are more impairing. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-63308-2.

papers.title: Development of cortical auditory processing and its association with speech understanding from childhood to adulthood.
papers.abstract: The maturation of the auditory system is critical for the development of speech perception from childhood through early adulthood. However, the developmental trajectories and behavioral significance of cortical responses to speech sounds, particularly in relation to frequency specificity, remain poorly understood. Here, we presented low-frequency (/m/) and high-frequency (/s/) speech sounds to 70 typically developing individuals aged 5-24 years and recorded early cortical responses (P1 and N1) using electroencephalography. We also examined associations between these neural responses and speech understanding in quiet and in the presence of speech interferers. The developmental trajectories of P1 and N1 revealed distinct age- and stimulus-dependent patterns, including both linear and non-linear changes across development. These findings delineate frequency-specific maturational profiles within the cortical auditory system and identify potential neurophysiological markers of speech perception, providing a normative benchmark for assessing atypical auditory development. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-68625-0.

papers.title: A SIRT6-OVOL2 axis governs excitatory neuron resilience to chronic stress.
papers.abstract: Current antidepressants primarily target monoaminergic and glutamatergic systems, but insufficiently protect against stress-induced neuronal dysfunction, highlighting the need for mechanism-based therapies. Here, we propose SIRT6 as a determinant of stress resilience. Excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 overexpression attenuates chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced anhedonia, despair, anxiety-like phenotypes, and circadian disruption, whereas astrocytic or inhibitory neuronal overexpression provides no comparable effect. Conversely, excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 deletion induces depression-like behaviors and disrupts circadian locomotor activity under basal conditions. Hippocampal single-nucleus transcriptomics identifies a stress-sensitive excitatory neuronal subtype depleted following CUMS but restored by SIRT6 overexpression. Regulatory network analysis positions OVOL2 as a central transcription factor governing stress-associated transcriptional alterations. SIRT6 directly interacts with OVOL2 and modulates its stability, thereby driving transcription of downstream targets, including Nrg1. The SIRT6 allosteric agonist MDL-800 recapitulates these findings, eliciting antidepressant-like effects. These findings elucidate SIRT6's role in promoting stress resilience and support SIRT6-targeting strategies for treating depression.

papers.title: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus in chronic hemodialysis patients: Real world treatment approaches in a large Turkish cohort.
papers.abstract: BackgroundChronic kidney disease-associated pruritus is a common symptom in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis, which adversely affects the quality of life, sleep, and mortality. Despite increasing awareness, real-world data on treatment patterns and their relationship with symptom severity remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus and evaluate real-world management strategies in a large cohort of hemodialysis patients.MethodsThis multicenter, cross-sectional study included adults receiving hemodialysis at eight dialysis centers. Pruritus presence, severity, demographic, clinical, and treatment-related data were recorded. Patients with and without chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus were analyzed.ResultsIn total, 1093 patients were included. Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus was present in 224 patients (20.5%). Overall, 73.6% of patients with chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus sought medical evaluation, and 66.9% received pharmacological treatment. Antihistamines were the most prescribed agents (64.0%), followed by topical therapies (17.3%), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (9.3%), and gabapentinoids (9.3%).ConclusionsAlthough treatment rates increased with symptom severity, evidence-based therapies such as gabapentinoids and advanced antipruritic strategies remain underutilized. Antihistamines are frequently prescribed despite limited efficacy. These findings highlight a substantial gap between guideline-based recommendations and real-world clinical practice, underscoring the need for improved multidisciplinary management of chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus in hemodialysis populations.
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research

papers.title: A volumetric threshold and age-dependent remodeling are associated with residual obstructive sleep apnea after adenotonsillectomy in children.
papers.abstract: Adenotonsillectomy is first-line treatment for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet residual disease persists in a notable subset of children. Traditional preoperative assessments reflect patient characteristics rather than airway anatomy, while prior cone-beam CT (CBCT) studies required extra research-only scans. We evaluated whether postoperative CBCT-measured upper-airway volume distinguishes complete OSA resolution from residual disease, and assessed age-related postoperative soft-tissue remodeling. This single-center retrospective STROBE-compliant cohort enrolled 238 children aged 3-10 years with PSG-confirmed OSA who underwent coblation adenotonsillectomy, with clinically indicated pre- and 3-month postoperative CBCT. Postoperative OAHI <1 defined complete resolution, and OAHI ≥5 defined residual OSA. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Mean OAHI decreased from 16.8 to 5.4 events/h (*p*<0.001). Complete resolution was achieved in 63.4% patients. The optimal postoperative airway volume cutoff was 10.5 cm³ (AUC=0.89). Postoperative volume <10.5 cm³, adenoid regrowth, high preoperative OAHI, younger age (3.0-3.9 years), and tongue-base hypertrophy were independent predictors of residual OSA. Postoperative upper-airway volume of 10.5 cm³ effectively stratifies residual OSA risk. Young age independently predicts persistent disease, likely due to incomplete soft tissue remodeling. This CBCT-based stratification uses clinically acquired imaging without extra radiation exposure.

papers.title: Effect of magnesium bisglycinate following coronary syndrome in young adults: a retrospective cohort study of self-reported sleep quality, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms.
papers.abstract: Anxiety, depression, and poor sleep are common after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and adversely affect prognosis, yet treatment options are limited. Oral magnesium bisglycinate improves sleep and mood in non-cardiac populations but has not been studied following ACS. We investigated whether post-discharge magnesium bisglycinate use is associated with improvement in self-reported sleep quality and anxiety and depressive symptom scores. In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 120 patients (68 magnesium, 52 comparator) were followed for three months after ACS. Magnesium bisglycinate (240 mg elemental magnesium daily) was initiated at the first post-discharge visit. The primary outcome was sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI); anxiety (Beck Anxiety Inventory, BAI) and depression (Beck Depression Inventory, BDI) were secondary outcomes, assessed with serum magnesium at baseline and three months. Baseline characteristics were comparable. At three months, the magnesium group showed greater improvement in self-reported sleep quality (PSQI: 5.2 ± 2.6 vs 7.3 ± 3.1; p < 0.001), anxiety (BAI: 12.1 ± 4.9 vs 15.8 ± 5.3; p < 0.001), and depressive symptoms (BDI: 8.3 ± 4.7 vs 11.2 ± 5.5; p = 0.003), with Cohen's d = 0.57-0.74. Serum magnesium did not differ between groups at either time point (p = 0.55 and p = 0.20), and the associations persisted after multivariable adjustment and in sensitivity models including baseline serum magnesium, renal function, and medications affecting magnesium balance. Post- discharge magnesium bisglycinate use was associated with greater improvement in self-reported sleep, anxiety, and depressive symptom scores following ACS. These hypothesis-generating findings, limited by residual confounding and healthy-user bias, require confirmation in an adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

papers.title: Efficacy, Acceptability, and Tolerability of Trazodone in Insomnia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Trazodone is widely prescribed off label for insomnia symptoms, but the dose range that best balances efficacy with acceptability and tolerability remains uncertain. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis evaluated trazodone for insomnia symptoms, with emphasis on clinically relevant dose selection. We searched Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 17 November 2025, for randomized controlled trials comparing trazodone with placebo or different trazodone doses in patients with insomnia symptoms. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using a one-stage random-effects model with restricted cubic splines. The primary outcome was subjective sleep quality; secondary outcomes were all-cause dropout rate and dropout due to adverse events. Thirteen randomized controlled trials involving 1366 participants were included. Compared with placebo, trazodone moderately improved subjective sleep quality (Cohen's d = 0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.36-0.98; I2 = 80.86%; p < 0.01). The dose-response curve suggested that efficacy increased at lower doses and approached a plateau around 50 mg/day, although estimates in the higher-dose range were sparse and imprecise. The estimated 50% effective dose was 15.2 mg/day, and the 95% effective dose was 38.2 mg/day, but these estimates should be interpreted as exploratory rather than as precise dose targets. Conventional meta-analysis showed no clear difference in all-cause discontinuation or discontinuation due to adverse events, whereas dose-response analysis suggested a possible dose-related increase in adverse event-related discontinuation. Trazodone was associated with short-term improvement in subjective sleep quality among heterogeneous populations with insomnia symptoms. The most observable benefit appears to occur at relatively low doses, while dose escalation may offer limited additional benefit and reduce tolerability. However, interpretation of the findings is limited by considerable clinical heterogeneity, sparse evidence at higher doses, and insufficient data on long-term efficacy and safety. CRD420251232065.

papers.title: Parental Accommodation in Pre-school Aged Children with Specific Phobias: An Exploratory Study.
papers.abstract: Specific phobia (SP), characterised by persistent anxiety, distress, and pathological avoidance of a feared stimulus, is among the most common childhood anxiety disorders and predicts later mental health difficulties. One mechanism known to maintain child anxiety and reduce treatment response is parental accommodation (PA), yet little is known about its role in young children with phobias. This cross-sectional study explored correlates and mediators of PA across phobia subtypes in 93 phobic children aged 3-6 years. All parents engaged in some form of PA, with accommodation significantly higher in the natural-environment subtype. Greater PA was associated with greater child anxiety, functional impairment, and sleep difficulties, as well as parental depression and parenting stress. In a hierarchical regression, child functional impairment and parenting stress were uniquely associated with PA. Mediation and reverse mediation analyses indicated that while PA partially accounted for the indirect association between child anxiety and functional impairment, functional impairment also significantly accounted for the indirect association between anxiety and PA, with no definitive evidence for the direction of causality. There is a need for longitudinal research to replicate these findings to elucidate potential treatment targets.

papers.title: Epidemiology, Complications, and Management of Complications of Achondroplasia: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Achondroplasia is a rare genetic condition associated with considerable clinical burden. This study examined the clinical burden of achondroplasia, including epidemiology, condition complications and their management, and the estimated prevalence of common complications. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted (September 2025) to identify articles published from 2011. As a result of heterogeneity across studies, meta-analyses of complication prevalence were restricted to pediatric and adolescent populations. Overall, 200 studies were included. Forty-five studies reported epidemiological data; the prevalence of achondroplasia ranged from one to 67 per 100,000 births. The most common neurological complications were cervicomedullary compression/craniocervical junction stenosis (mean 34%; n = 13) and foramen magnum narrowing (FMN; mean 26%; n = 21). The top respiratory complications were sleep disordered breathing (SDB; mean 60%; n = 13) and obstructive sleep apnea (mean 48%; n = 27). Ear, nose, and throat (ENT) complications comprised ear infections (mean 40%; n = 12) and hearing impairment (mean 40%; n = 16). Common orthopedic complications included kyphosis (mean 43%; n = 22) and bowing of legs or genu varum (mean 39%; n = 7). The top complications among pediatric populations were SDB (mean 65% [95% confidence interval (CI) 36, 85]; n = 13) and FMN (mean 56% [37, 73]; n = 20). Cervicomedullary decompression (mean 11%; n = 22) was a more frequent treatment option for neurologic complications than suboccipital decompression (mean 19%; n = 3). Typical interventions included ENT procedures (mean 40%; n = 37) and surgery for orthopedic complications (mean 28%; n = 27). Twenty-six studies reported complications from limb-lengthening surgeries (mean age of treatment 6.2-16.9 years). This SLR and meta-analysis underscore the significant clinical burden related to complications and their management in individuals with achondroplasia. Prevalence estimates varied widely by geography, reflecting differences in data sources, case ascertainment, and reporting practices. The high frequency and severity of complications underscore the need for effective treatments to reduce complication burden and improve patient quality of life.

papers.title: Sleep and Memory: Consolidation, Updating, and State-Dependent Control.
papers.abstract: This review synthesizes recent evidence on the role of sleep in memory consolidation and updating, focusing on the underlying neural mechanisms and their control. Recent literature demonstrates that memory encoding is followed by a labile window during which memory traces are subject not only to consolidation but also to updating. Sleep after single-shot learning can stabilize or enhance memory, rendering it resistant to subsequent natural forgetting. In addition, sleep following multiple experiences supports further forms of memory processing, including reconsolidation, extinction, integration, and differentiation. These processes are mediated by neural circuitry dynamics coupled with electrophysiological oscillations and neuromodulatory rhythms across sleep states. Furthermore, memory processing during sleep can be experimentally controlled by manipulating these internal fluctuations or through targeted memory reactivation. Sleep-dependent processing of existing and newly acquired memories is governed by dissociable state-specific mechanisms, which are increasingly amenable to experimental control.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Physical Activity Interventions on Sleep Disturbances in Children and Adolescents With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis of Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent among children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the potential effects of physical activity (PA) interventions on sleep and explored intervention characteristics to generate hypotheses. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched 10 databases from inception to November 2025. Controlled trials evaluating PA interventions on sleep in children and adolescents with ASD were included. Random-effects models computed pooled effect sizes, and subgroup analyses examined potential moderators. Thirteen trials (579 participants) were included. Pooled analyses showed a significant effect on subjective overall sleep problems (g = - 2.200, 95% CI [- 3.425, - 0.974], p < 0.001). Objective sleep efficiency was also significant (g = 2.040, 95% CI [0.419, 3.661], p = 0.014) but not robust, becoming non-significant after exclusion of one influential study (p = 0.111). No significant effects were found for sleep-disordered breathing, sleep onset latency, actigraphy-measured sleep duration, and wake after sleep onset. Heterogeneity was high across most outcomes (I² > 90%), and funnel plot asymmetry with significant Egger's tests suggested potential publication bias for subjective outcomes. Larger estimates for mind-body or aquatic exercises (≥ 10 weeks, 3-5 sessions/week, 45-60 min/session) were exploratory. PA interventions provide preliminary evidence of improvement in selected sleep outcomes among children and adolescents with ASD, particularly subjective overall sleep problems, whereas evidence for objective sleep efficiency was not robust. Heterogeneity and potential publication bias limit certainty, and suggested intervention characteristics remain preliminary and require validation in high-quality trials.
papers.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

papers.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with outcomes in hospitalized patients with pneumonia: a retrospective analysis of the nationwide inpatient sample.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) impairs mucociliary defense, reduces ventilatory reserve, promotes systemic inflammation, and predisposes patients to lower respiratory tract infections. Despite biological plausibility, the population-level association of comorbid OSA with pneumonia hospitalization outcomes remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate associations between OSA and clinical outcomes in adults hospitalized with pneumonia using a nationally representative inpatient database. Using the 2018-2020 Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS), we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of pneumonia, stratified by OSA status. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, household income quartile, primary payer, Charlson Comorbidity Index, obesity, hospital type, hospital bed size, and geographic region. P-values were corrected for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni), and E-values were calculated to assess sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. Among 4,918,328 hospitalizations, 9.2% (n = 450,580) had coexisting OSA. Despite a greater comorbidity burden, OSA was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (3.3% vs. 4.8%; aOR 0.74; 95% CI 0.71-0.77; p < 0.0001), lower sepsis (aOR 0.89; 95% CI 0.87-0.90), and lower septic shock (2.2% vs. 2.7%; aOR 0.80; 95% CI 0.76-0.84). Conversely, OSA was associated with higher acute respiratory failure (48.1% vs. 35.8%; aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.54-1.59), noninvasive ventilation (NIV) use (14.8% vs. 5.0%; aOR 3.26; 95% CI 3.17-3.34), and acute kidney injury (AKI; 24.1% vs. 22.1%; aOR 1.13; 95% CI 1.11-1.15). Adjusted length of stay was slightly longer (β + 0.11 days; 95% CI 0.07-0.16), while adjusted hospital charges did not differ significantly. All associations except hospital charges remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons; E-values suggested that the sepsis and AKI associations could be explained by relatively weak unmeasured confounding. Among adults hospitalized with pneumonia, comorbid OSA was associated with higher rates of acute respiratory failure, NIV use, and AKI, and with lower in-hospital mortality and sepsis. Because of the retrospective administrative design and the lack of data on pneumonia severity, OSA severity, and CPAP use, residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and prospective studies are needed.

papers.title: Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Unanswered Questions.
papers.abstract: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) remains the leading cause of epilepsy-related mortality. While heterogeneous in its pathophysiology, a significant proportion of cases are likely attributable to cardiorespiratory collapse following a convulsive seizure. We synthesize recent mechanistic, biomarker, and prevention literature, moving from retrospective risk inference toward individualized action. Human and animal data support a multiple hit model, in which seizure-induced cardiorespiratory dysfunction is necessary but not necessarily sufficient for death: the environment, genetic susceptibility, sleep and circadian state, and potentially as yet unidentified factors determine which seizures prove fatal. The Mortality in Epilepsy Monitoring Units study (MORTEMUS) provided key insights into SUDEP pathophysiology, while multicenter prospective studies continue to examine SUDEP risk factors and mechanisms, and elucidate candidate biomarkers for individual risk stratification. Prevention is slowly moving beyond mainstays of nocturnal supervision and antiseizure therapies, guided by data from animal models of seizure-associated death. Emerging technologies such as seizure detection devices are being widely deployed to enhance protection, though none has been shown in a randomized trial to reduce SUDEP. Efforts toward universal SUDEP education and counseling not only address legal and moral disclosure responsibilities, but encourage patient autonomy and informed decision-making for individual risk reduction. The decade following publication of the MORTEMUS study continues to provide new insights into SUDEP pathophysiology, propose novel candidate biomarkers and offer potential intervention targets. While obstacles remain in the replication of putative clinical biomarkers and the translation of promising findings from animal models, enhancing SUDEP knowledge and effective patient counseling are critical to improving outcomes and saving lives.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and cistromic analyses reveal associations between mechanotransduction-associated transcription and clock-gene expression in pulmonary arterial hypertension and TEAD-sensitive CRY1/CLOCK responses.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves vascular remodeling in an abnormal mechanical environment, but the relationship between mechanotransduction-associated transcription and clock-gene expression remains unclear. We integrated three PAH lung transcriptomic cohorts, donor-level endothelial analyses, vascular cell-state and spatial transcriptomic data, endothelial perturbation transcriptomics, and chromatin-binding data, with validation in human pulmonary artery endothelial cells (HPAECs). In 83 PAH lung samples, restricted maximum likelihood (REML) random-effects pooling showed a positive association between mechanotransduction and clock-related scores (Spearman ρ = 0.393, 95% confidence interval 0.185-0.567; Hartung-Knapp sensitivity P = 0.0279), which weakened when restricted to genes detectable across cohorts. Endothelial pseudobulk data from GSE169471 supported a positive donor-level association (n = 8, ρ = 0.738); the six-donor GSE210248 analysis used different score pairs. Associations varied in direction across vascular cell states, while molecular programs in 217 spatial regions differed by donor and lesion context. In HUVECs, activated YAP/TAZ increased CRY1 and CLOCK expression, with partial attenuation by TEAD-binding-deficient mutants. ChIP-seq identified candidate binding sites near both genes. In HPAECs, a stiffer substrate was associated with higher nuclear YAP/TAZ and CRY1/CLOCK protein levels; construct comparisons and independent TEAD1 knockdown supported TEAD-sensitive expression induction. Beyond prior CRY1 findings, this study provides evidence for CLOCK responses in pulmonary artery endothelium and cell-state heterogeneity. The findings support a candidate regulatory link, not altered circadian function or a causal mechanism of PAH vascular remodeling.

papers.title: Transcriptomic characterization of obligate winter diapause in the emerald ash borer (Agrilus planipennis).
papers.abstract: Wood-boring insects pose serious threats to trees, and even when living inside their hosts, they remain exposed to adverse conditions such as extreme low temperatures. Diapause is a critical strategy that enables certain pests to survive such environments and sustain their populations. Characterizing the molecular changes associated with diapause may therefore improve our understanding of their overwintering biology and environmental responses. However, transcriptomic studies of diapause in wood-boring insects remain relatively limited, partly because of their long life cycles, cryptic habits, and difficulties in sampling and observation. In this study, we focused on the emerald ash borer (EAB, Agrilus planipennis), an obligate diapausing pest that causes severe damage in both its native and invaded ranges. Using a comparative transcriptomic approach, we sequenced samples from three developmental stages: pre-diapause, diapause, and post-diapause. Compared to the other developmental stages, 1,147 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified as showing diapause-stage-associated expression patterns, with up-regulated genes outnumbering down-regulated genes by approximately 1.88-fold. By integrating exploratory GO/KEGG analyses, expression profiles, and previously reported diapause-associated pathways, we identified 47 candidate diapause-associated genes. Among these, 35 were upregulated (1.24- to 807.71-fold) and 12 were downregulated (0.04- to 0.74-fold) relative to the pre- and post-diapausing stages. KEGG Mapper further indicated that several candidates were associated with the Wnt, circadian rhythm, and FOXO signaling pathways. Collectively, these results characterize diapause-associated transcriptional changes in EAB and provide candidate genes and pathways for further investigation of overwintering responses in EAB and other winter-diapausing wood-boring insects.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.abstract: Sleep science has shifted from coarse stage-based metrics toward a microstructural perspective that treats electroencephalographic biomarkers, spectral power, sleep spindles, and slow oscillations as candidate windows onto restorative brain function. This high-definition review evaluates whether acupuncture has been shown to modify these features. Direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is currently very limited: most available electrophysiological studies were conducted during quiet wakefulness, in resting daytime EEG recordings from clinical groups, or under propofol anesthesia. These studies demonstrate that acupuncture or related electrical acupoint stimulation can produce state-, region-, and frequency-dependent changes in EEG power and network organization, but they do not yet establish increased NREM spindle density, improved slow-oscillation-spindle coupling, enhanced slow-wave morphology, memory consolidation, or glymphatic clearance. We therefore distinguish directly observed findings from indirect mechanistic support and from hypotheses that require prospective testing. Plausible pathways include ascending somatosensory influences on thalamocortical excitability, autonomic and hypothalamic effects that may reduce hyperarousal, and peripheral or central neurochemical processes involving adenosine, GABA, serotonin, and BDNF; however, the causal sequence from needling to sleep microarchitecture remains unproven. Future progress requires preregistered, adequately powered, multi-night studies using validated spindle and slow-wave detectors, explicit control estimands, and multimodal measurements. Biomarker-guided and closed-loop acupuncture should presently be regarded as a research framework rather than an established treatment strategy.

papers.title: TARS-EEG: a tropical algebraic representation for EEG seizure detection.
papers.abstract: To propose an interpretable tropical algebraic signal representation, named TARS-EEG, for EEG-based seizure detection by modelling short EEG segments through max-plus and min-plus waveform-dominance profiles. Short EEG segments from the Epileptic Seizure Recognition dataset were mapped into multiscale tropical dilation, erosion, gradient, and residue profiles. A Tropical Seizure Index was introduced to quantify normalized local waveform-dominance energy. The extracted tropical features were evaluated using standard classifiers with recording-group-aware train-test analysis, recording-group-aware five-fold cross-validation, and ablation experiments. The proposed TARS-EEG representation achieved stable seizure/non-seizure classification performance across standard classifiers. Under recording-group-aware five-fold cross-validation, MLP achieved the highest mean accuracy of 97.70 %, while XGBoost achieved the highest ROC-AUC of 0.9926. Ablation analysis showed that the complete multiscale tropical representation performed better than individual neighbourhood-scale representations. TARS-EEG provides a compact and interpretable algebraic representation for EEG seizure detection. The results suggest that multiscale max-plus and min-plus waveform descriptors can capture seizure-related local waveform dominance effectively.

papers.title: RORα contributes to melatonin-mediated neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by promoting microglia/macrophage M2 polarization through the AMPK-mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (CI/R) injury is a neurological disorder in which microglia and macrophages regulate repair by switching M1/M2 phenotypes. RORα, a regulator of circadian rhythm and a mediator for melatonin effects, has an unclear role in CI/R injury and melatonin-mediated neuroprotection, particularly in microglial/macrophage polarization. An in vivo transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was established in C57BL/6J mice, and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models were developed for BV-2 and HT22 cells. In vivo, Flag-tagged RORα overexpression lentivirus were intracranially injected and melatonin (10 mg/kg) was injected intraperitoneally; in vitro, BV2 cells were exposed to 200 µM melatonin and infected with an RORα-overexpressing lentiviral vector, while HT22 cells were cultivated in conditioned medium. Western blot, immunofluorescence, TTC staining, and ELISA were used to evaluate RORα expression, neurological function, microglia/macrophage M2 polarization, inflammatory responses, and cellular apoptosis, respectively. The role of the AMPK-mTOR pathway was confirmed using the AMPK inhibitor Compound C in vitro. The viability, apoptosis, and ROS levels of HT22 cell were assessed using CCK-8 assay, TUNEL staining, and flow cytometry, respectively. In both in vivo and BV-2 cell in vitro models, RORα levels gradually decreased within 24 h, followed by a gradual recovery. Melatonin reduced neurological scores and enhanced blood-brain barrier protection, promoting M2 microglia/macrophage polarization and inhibiting subsequent inflammatory responses, with RORα overexpression further amplifying these effects. In an HT22 cell model, RORα overexpression enhanced the protection by melatonin against OGD/R-induced reductions in cell viability, as well as against increased apoptosis and elevated ROS levels. Mechanistically, RORα overexpression promoted M2 microglial polarization via activation of the AMPK-mTOR pathway, thereby amplifying the melatonin-mediated neuroprotection. RORα enhanced neuroprotection by melatonin against CI/R injury through promoting microglia/macrophage M2 polarization, suggesting a possible treatment target for CI/R injury.

papers.title: Pharmacotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD.
papers.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is trauma- and stressor-related disorder frequently associated with somatic and psychiatric comorbidities. The most frequent psychiatric comorbidities are major depressive disorder (MDD), sleep disturbances, alcohol use disorders (AUD) and psychoses. The lack of clinical improvement is frequent in PTSD, and presence of comorbidities complicates PTSD treatment. This narrative review covered pharmacotherapy of common psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD (MDD, psychosis, sleep disturbances, especially obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and insomnia and AUD. We searched for novel data in reviews, randomized clinical trials, open labeled studies in English language through June 2026, identified using PubMed/MEDLINE/Web of Sciences/Google Scholar and clinical practice guidelines from the American Psychological Association for the Treatment of PTSD in adults (2025), and the US Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense from 2023. We discussed available evidence related to pharmacotherapy of PTSD with comorbidities. The vast majority of PTSD patients have at least one psychiatric comorbidity. Pharmacological treatment represents a challenge, given that pharmacological agents used to treat PTSD mostly do not affect symptoms of other comorbid disorders. Therefore, the choice of medications is highly individual, depending on the clinical presentation, tolerability issues, physical comorbidities, and patient preference.

papers.title: Wearable electrophysiology monitoring enabled by stretchable porous composite conductors.
papers.abstract: We report a porous AgNWs/PEDOT:PSS composite electrode with uniform conductive networks and cold-welded junctions, fabricated by template-assisted assembly. The porous architecture effectively dissipates stress and accommodates strain, yielding excellent performance at 50% strain and stable performance over 5000 stretching cycles. The electrode enables reliable ECG, EOG, and EMG monitoring.

papers.title: Beyond Onset Timing: Longer Sound Envelope Duration Enhances Neural Representation of the Musical Beat.
papers.abstract: Musical rhythm is often experienced with a periodic beat, serving as a temporal reference for coordinating movement. Thus far, models of beat processing have mainly relied on representing sensory inputs as patterns of onset timing, largely overlooking other acoustic features. Here, we challenge this view by showing that the internal representation of beat is affected by other temporal features of the stimulus beyond onset timing alone. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while participants listened to rhythmic sequences designed to elicit a beat. Across conditions, we manipulated the duration of the tones conveying the rhythms, while keeping all other parameters identical, including overall intensity, speed, and rhythmic pattern structure. Beat periodicity was enhanced in the EEG responses with increased sound duration, even though it was not prominent in either the acoustic envelope or the output of a biomimetic auditory nerve model, thus pointing to higher-level processing beyond basic sensory confounds. These results demonstrate the preferential role of longer sound durations in fostering temporal scaffolding processes that integrate fast rhythmic inputs into behavior-relevant internal structures, such as the beat. More generally, our findings support a holistic processing account whereby features beyond onset timing are integrated into a neural representation of rhythm.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Transpulmonary Atrial Pacemaker Implantation in Fontan Circulation With Bilateral Glenn.
papers.abstract: Patients with Fontan circulation frequently develop atrial arrhythmias and sinus node dysfunction. Atrial pacing is challenging because conventional transvenous access is limited by complex Fontan anatomy. A 20-year-old man with dextroisomerism, bilateral Glenn anastomoses, and Fontan circulation presented with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and recurrent supraventricular tachycardia. A transpulmonary transvenous approach achieved endocardial atrial lead implantation with excellent pacing parameters. Despite optimized medical therapy, heart failure progressed, and the patient died during transplant evaluation. This case highlights the technical feasibility of transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing as an alternative to repeat epicardial surgery in selected patients with Fontan circulation. Careful procedural planning, multimodality imaging, and individualized assessment of long-term anticoagulation are important considerations. Despite arrhythmia control, optimized therapy and restoration of atrioventricular synchrony may not prevent heart failure progression, which may be irreversible. Transpulmonary endocardial atrial pacing is a feasible alternative in carefully selected Patients with Fontan circulation. Sudden cardiac death risk stratification remains limited in this study group.

papers.title: Novel Transvenous Approach for Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation in a Patient With Fontan Circulation: Trans-Left Pulmonary Artery-Left Atrium.
papers.abstract: After Fontan palliation, direct venous access to the ventricle is eliminated, complicating implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) placement. A 34-year-old status-post lateral tunnel Fontan presented with syncope. He was found to have high-grade atrioventricular block and fractured epicardial leads. He was recommended an ICD with severely depressed single right ventricle function but was not an epicardial candidate because of multiple prior sternotomies and recurrent chest wall abscesses. Despite balloon angioplasty of the transbaffle puncture, a sheath for ICD placement could not be advanced. A trans-left pulmonary artery to left atrial (LPA-LA) puncture was performed at the left pulmonary artery/Fontan conduit junction above the left atrium roof to implant the right ventricle ICD lead. Transpulmonary LPA-LA is a feasible option for ICD lead implantation in patients with Fontan who are not candidates for epicardial leads. This is the first report of transpulmonary LPA-LA puncture for ventricular lead placement in Fontan circulation.

papers.title: Spontaneous Neuronal Activity in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Insights from Human and Animal Studies.
papers.abstract: Developmental spontaneous neuronal activity (SNA) plays an instrumental role in the generation of precise brain circuits. Spontaneous activity patterns guide neuronal differentiation, synaptic refinement, and circuit formation; consequently, perturbations in these activity patterns can profoundly influence brain network organization. Growing evidence suggests that mutations in autism-associated genes lead to alterations of the SNA pattern during early brain development, thereby giving rise to the behavioral features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This review integrates findings from neuroimaging studies, which reveal widespread alterations in neuronal excitability in individuals with ASD. Regional homogeneity and functional connectivity analyses consistently demonstrate region-specific abnormalities, including hyperactivity in higher-order cortical regions, hypoactivity in sensorimotor areas, and disrupted long-range connectivity. These functional alterations are closely linked to the underlying molecular and cellular mechanisms such as excitation-inhibition (E/I) imbalance, impaired GABAergic signaling, glutamatergic dysregulation, and abnormalities in calcium-dependent signaling pathways. Identification of activity-based biomarkers, together with advanced neuroimaging techniques and computational and machine learning (ML) approaches, may facilitate early diagnosis of ASD. Understanding the origin and consequences of alterations in SNA provides a unifying framework for identifying novel targets for designing pharmacological intervention strategies.
papers.journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry

papers.title: Association of physical activity with insulin resistance in shift workers: data from NHANES.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association between shift work patterns and insulin resistance (IR) surrogates, and the potential moderating role of physical activity (PA). This cross-sectional study analysed 992 adults from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-2018. Participants were categorized into daytime and variable shift workers. Four IR surrogates were evaluated. Weighted linear regression models adjusted for demographics, anthropometrics, lifestyle, and clinical covariates assessed associations between work schedules, PA, and metabolic outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluded individuals with diabetes. Compared to daytime workers, variable shift workers had significantly higher triglycerides, lower high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C), and elevated levels of all IR surrogates. Physical activity was inversely associated with triglyceride-glucose - waist circumference (TyG-WC) and body mass index (TyG-BMI). The most pronounced combined beneficial association was observed for daytime schedules combined with sufficient PA on homeostasis model assessment of IR (HOMA‑IR) and TyG-BMI. However, when stratified, work-related PA correlated positively with these indices, while leisure-time PA exhibited stronger inverse associations; transportation PA showed no association. Variable shift work and insufficient PA are associated with adverse metabolic profiles and elevated IR. As a modifiable factor, PA may help mitigate metabolic risk in shift-working populations. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).
papers.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health

papers.title: Quantitative effects of sleep deprivation on digital pupillary dynamics and visual evoked potential metrics in healthy adults.
papers.abstract: The pupillary light reflex (PLR), pupillary sleepiness test (PST), and visual evoked potentials (VEPs) are crucial for assessing the functional integrity of the visual and autonomic nervous systems. These responses integrate retinal phototransduction with midbrain reflex pathways and cortical visual processing, all of which are influenced by physiological and clinical disorders. Their temporal dynamics lay the groundwork for using pupillary reflexes and cortical potentials as biomarkers of fatigue and the effects of psychoactive substances on them. This study aimed to identify physiological biomarkers of fatigue by evaluating the PLR and VEPs. These modalities were validated against the PST, pupillary unrest index parameters, and blink-rate analysis to assess autonomic and cortical contributions to fatigue. This study examined the effects of 48-hour sleep deprivation on pupillary behavior in 18 healthy adults under controlled conditions. Analysis of PLR dynamics revealed that the dilation-phase parameters DDil1 and DDil2, corresponding to pupil diameters at 20% and 80% recovery, respectively, were sensitive to changes in autonomic activation. These complemented the established fatigue indices, including constriction velocity, relative amplitude, time of minimum diameter, and latency. Visual evoked potentials analysis demonstrated that sustained wakefulness modulated cortical responses, with a delay and amplitude reduction in the N145 component. Biomarkers from the pupillary reflex dilation phase and N145 LAT in VEP recordings serve as reliable indicators of fatigue severity, as corroborated by the PST and Stanford Sleepiness Scale assessments. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).
papers.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization. Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Keratoconus and obstructive sleep apnea risk: a cross-sectional study using validated screening questionnaires.
papers.abstract: To compare obstructive sleep apnea screening classifications, anthropometric characteristics, and mechanical behaviors between participants with keratoconus and controls and to explore their associations with disease severity. This prospective cross-sectional study included 74 participants with keratoconus and 49 controls. The paper-based Berlin and STOP-BANG questionnaires were administered face-to-face by a researcher and scored manually. A study-specific questionnaire assessed eye rubbing and sleep position, whereas a separate structured field recorded self-reported ocular compression during sleep. Both groups underwent corneal tomography. The primary logistic regression model included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), eye rubbing, and ocular compression. Participants with keratoconus had a higher BMI (29.4±6.4 vs. 26.3±5.1 kg/m2; p=0.005), larger neck circumference (40.1±4.6 vs. 37.6±4.6 cm; p=0.004), more frequent eye rubbing (71.6% vs. 51.0%; p=0.020), and more frequent ocular compression (43.2% vs. 20.4%; p=0.009) than controls. High-risk classifications did not differ significantly between groups according to either the Berlin Questionnaire (p=0.206) or STOP-BANG (p=0.139). In exploratory models adjusted for age and sex, positive associations were observed for the Berlin Questionnaire (OR, 2.58; 95% CI, 0.91-7.28) and STOP-BANG (OR, 3.30; 95% CI, 0.83-13.05). In the primary model, younger age (OR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.83-0.93), male sex (OR, 2.91; 95% CI, 1.14-7.42), and higher BMI (OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.05-1.27) remained associated with keratoconus, whereas the estimates for behavioral factors were attenuated. No association with disease severity was detected. Participants with keratoconus had higher anthropometric measurements and more frequent mechanical behaviors; however, the prevalence of high-risk obstructive sleep apnea classifications did not differ significantly between groups. Questionnaire-based and anthropometric findings are not independent because BMI contributes to both screening instruments, whereas neck circumference contributes to the STOP-BANG score. Ocular compression was assessed using a nonvalidated self-report measure rather than objective pressure measurements. Severity analyses were underpowered, and causality cannot be inferred from the study design.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sleep deprivation in nursing technicians working in shifts.
papers.abstract: to estimate the prevalence of sleep deprivation among nursing technicians working in hospital shifts and identify the associated factors. a cross-sectional study was conducted at a municipal university hospital in Goiás, Brazil, between March and May 2022, with 198 participants. Sleep deprivation was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, defined as less than five hours of sleep per night. Multivariate analysis was used to identify factors associated with sleep deprivation. the prevalence of sleep deprivation was 43.9%. The main factors associated with sleep deprivation included prolonged daily work hours (OR=3.60/p=0.001), inadequate consumption of fruits, vegetables and greens (OR=2.25/p=0.024), coffee consumption (OR=3.14/p=0.031), high Body Mass Index (OR=1.27/p=0.001) and presence of anxiety symptoms (OR=6.58/p=0.001). intervention strategies should consider occupational and mental health factors to improve nursing technicians' sleep quality.

papers.title: Menopausal symptom burden in postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to compare menopausal symptom severity between postmenopausal women with and without fibromyalgia syndrome, and to estimate the independent association of fibromyalgia syndrome with menopausal symptom burden. Comparative cross-sectional study of 80 postmenopausal women: 40 with fibromyalgia syndrome and 40 without. The primary outcome was the Menopause Rating Scale total score; pain, fatigue and sleep disturbance were rated on 0-10 visual analog scales. The association of fibromyalgia syndrome with Menopause Rating Scale total score was estimated by multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, body mass index, education and route of menopause. Menopause Rating Scale total score was 26.2±9.7 with fibromyalgia syndrome versus 12.9±6.1 in controls (mean difference 13.3 points, 95%CI 9.6-16.9; Hedges' g=1.63; p<0.001). Severe symptoms (Menopause Rating Scale ≥17) occurred in 85.0% versus 27.5% (risk ratio 3.1; 95%CI 1.8-5.2). Fibromyalgia syndrome remained independently associated with Menopause Rating Scale total score after adjustment (β=13.13; 95%CI 9.32-16.94; p<0.001); further adjustment for pain, fatigue and sleep visual analog scales attenuated but did not abolish this association (β=10.11; 95%CI 6.07-14.16). Postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia syndrome carry a substantially greater menopausal symptom burden than women of comparable age and body mass index. This association was independent of measured demographic and reproductive characteristics, but its independence from the core features of fibromyalgia syndrome could not be established, given the overlap between the two symptom sets.

papers.title: Genetic Spectrum and molecular diagnosis of nystagmus in a spanish paediatric cohort.
papers.abstract: IntroductionNystagmus is a common presenting sign of early onset inherited retinal dystrophies. Identifying a genetic diagnosis for infantile nystagmus syndrome patients is crucial for providing appropriate treatment and genetic counselling. This study aimed to evaluate the genetic findings in paediatric patients with nystagmus assessed between 1st January 2020 and 31st December 2025.MethodsA total of 94 children presenting with nystagmus underwent a detailed ophthalmologic evaluation including electrodiagnostic tests and were referred for genetic testing during the study period. Comprehensive genomic analysis was performed to identify pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants.ResultsOf the 94 patients, 30 (32%) were found to have a pathogenic or likely pathogenic genetic variant. The most frequently implicated genes were PAX6, NDP, TYR, CNGA3, RS1 and FRMD7. These findings reflect the genetic heterogeneity of paediatric nystagmus and underscore the importance of targeted genetic evaluation in affected individuals.ConclusionA significant proportion of children with nystagmus have identifiable genetic causes, with mutations in PAX6, NDP, TYR, CNGA3, RS1 and FRMD7 being the most common in our cohort. Early genetic diagnosis can guide clinical management, inform prognosis, and enable genetic counselling.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBrain diseases pose a significant global health challenge, and their diagnosis often relies on subjective clinical assessments.ObjectiveTo this end, this study proposes an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework for single-channel Electroencephalography (EEG)-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.MethodsFirst, EEG signals are decomposed into rhythm-specific sub-bands using the Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (DWPT). Then, for each rhythm, a multi-dimensional feature matrix (MFM) is constructed by integrating Approximate Entropy (AE), Rhythm Energy Ratio (RER), C0-complexity (C0), and Zero-crossing Rate (ZCR), which comprehensively models the EEG characteristics. Six classifiers were compared under subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and Decision Tree (DT) was selected as the representative classifier. Each channel was then evaluated independently as a complete single-channel system, and representative channels were identified from the completed results.ResultsValidated on publicly available datasets for SCHIZ (schizophrenia), UNM (Parkinson's disease), and MPHCE (depression), the method achieves impressive accuracies of 84.52% (F4), 86.54% (F4), and 93.10% (Fp1), respectively, using single-channel EEG electrode.ConclusionsSuch results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains robust detection performance in each of the three disease-specific tasks. The framework is lightweight by design, using only a single EEG channel and a single simple machine-learning model for classification. It needs no multi-channel feature concatenation or decision-level fusion. This single-channel design suits hardware and data sources with limited resources, and may support the development of low-cost portable EEG systems.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

papers.title: Sublingual cyclobenzaprine for fibromyalgia: a critical evaluation of clinical development and therapeutic positioning.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia combines widespread pain, nonrestorative sleep, fatigue, cognitive symptoms, and functional impairment. Sublingual cyclobenzaprine received US approval for fibromyalgia in August 2025. This narrative review evaluates its development, rationale, pharmacokinetics, efficacy, safety, and therapeutic positioning. The search covered PubMed/MEDLINE, trial registries, regulatory sources, and reference lists through 20 August 2026, with an update on 28 September 2026; primary reports and regulatory documents were prioritized. Two of three 5.6-mg phase 3 trials met the pain endpoint; earlier 2.8-mg trials did not. Mean placebo-adjusted pain reductions were 0.4-0.66 points in positive trials. One additional participant achieved ≥30% pain reduction per 6-9 treated; pooled safety data suggested one additional oral mucosal reaction per three treated. These estimates derive from different evidence sets and are not a formal benefit-harm ratio. Frequent oral sensory reactions may cause functional unblinding. Threshold-matched indirect responder benchmarks do not establish superiority over established therapies; altered pharmacokinetics do not establish less next-day impairment than low-dose oral cyclobenzaprine. Positive studies lasted 14 weeks; responder estimates were exploratory. Controlled long-term and comparative-effectiveness data remain limited. Sponsor involvement, the negative RALLY trial, limited geriatric evidence, and absence of active-comparator trials constrain interpretation. A monitored trial may be reasonable in selected adults with persistent, sleep-prominent symptoms despite multimodal care and low treatment risk, although this phenotype is unvalidated. Continuation should require net improvement in symptoms and daytime function. Independent active-comparator trials, particularly against low-dose bedtime oral cyclobenzaprine, assessing morning alertness, tolerability, and masking would most change the assessment.

papers.title: Association between chronotype, eating behaviors, and Mediterranean diet adherence among overweight and obese women.
papers.abstract: BackgroundChronotype, which reflects individual circadian preference, has a limited evidence base regarding its relationship with eating behaviors and adherence to the Mediterranean diet among overweight and obese women.AimThis study aimed to examine the association between chronotype, eating behaviors, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet among overweight and obese women.MethodsThis cross-sectional study was conducted in Türkiye and included 181 overweight and obese women attending a nutrition outpatient clinic. Chronotype was assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), eating behaviors using the Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire (DEBQ), and Mediterranean diet adherence using the Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS).ResultsAmong the participants, 22.7% were classified as morning type, 59.1% as intermediate type, and 18.2% as evening type. Mediterranean diet adherence scores differed significantly across chronotype groups and were significantly higher in the morning chronotype group compared with the intermediate and evening groups (p = 0.001). Emotional eating scores (p = 0.037), external eating scores (p < 0.001), and total DEBQ scores (p = 0.018) were significantly higher among women with an evening chronotype. No significant difference was observed in restrained eating scores across chronotype groups (p = 0.777).ConclusionChronotype was associated with eating behaviors and Mediterranean diet adherence among overweight and obese women. Morning chronotypes demonstrated healthier eating behavior patterns and greater adherence to the Mediterranean diet, whereas evening chronotypes exhibited higher emotional and external eating tendencies. These findings suggest that chronotype may be an important factor to consider in nutritional counseling and obesity management.

papers.title: Determinants and mechanisms of fatigue in older adult patients with stroke: A structural equation modeling approach.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to explore the determinants and pathways of fatigue in older adult patients with stroke, drawing upon the theory of unpleasant symptoms, to inform clinical interventions.MethodsA convenience sampling method was used to recruit 234 older adult patients with stroke between July 2024 and January 2025. Data were collected using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Social Support Rating Scale, and Stroke Specific Quality of Life Scale. Statistical analysis was conducted using R software (version 4.4.3), and a structural equation model was constructed. The mediating effect was evaluated using the Bootstrap method.ResultsFatigue levels were significantly higher in patients with greater anxiety, depression, poorer sleep quality, and higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and in those with lower education level and poorer stroke-specific quality of life (all p < 0.05). The structural equation model demonstrated a good fit (CFI = 1.000, RMSEA = 0.000). Anxiety, depression, and sleep quality were identified as complete mediators between education level, social support, CRP levels, and fatigue. The mediating effect accounted for 70.1 of the total effect, indicating that anxiety, depression, and sleep quality collectively explain most of the association between sociodemographic, psychosocial, and inflammatory factors and fatigue in this population.ConclusionFatigue among older adult patients with stroke is influenced by multiple interrelated factors, with anxiety, depression, and sleep quality acting as key mediators. These findings support routine screening and targeted management of psychological distress and sleep problems to mitigate fatigue during stroke rehabilitation.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation

papers.title: Chronotherapy at a Crossroads: Restoring Rigor and Trust in Circadian Medicine.
[Current status and progress of electrophysiological diagnostic and treatment technology in urology and andrology].
papers.abstract: The application of electrophysiological diagnostic and treatment technology in the field of urology and andrology is becoming increasingly widespread, providing new methods for the diagnosis and treatment of various urinary system diseases. With the in-depth research on electrophysiological technology and the promotion of its clinical application, its application in fields such as prostate diseases, bladder dysfunction and male sexual dysfunction has continuously made progress, greatly improving the diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic effect of diseases. Current research indicates that electrophysiological technology can effectively assess the neurological function of the urinary system, offering a foundation for individualized treatment. However, despite the great potential for the application of electrophysiological technology in urology and andrology, challenges like a lack of standardization and limited clinical promotion still exist. This article reviews the current application status of electrophysiology in urology and andrology, discusses its progress in related diseases, and analyzes potential future research directions and clinical application prospects, with the goal of providing insights for the advancement of urology and andrology.
