papers.title: [Combined use of endocrine therapy with Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer: A retrospective real-world cohort study].
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the impact of combination of Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules on the survival outcome and quality of life of patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) on the basis of standard endocrine therapy. Methods This retrospective real-world cohort study enrolled 41 patients diagnosed with CRPC between April 2021 and December 2024, including 21 patients in the control group (standard endocrine therapy) and 20 patients in the treatment group (standard endocrine therapy combined with Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules). The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and radiological progression-free survival (rPFS). Secondary outcomes included quality of life (FACT-P Version 4 scale), TCM syndrome scores (Shenyang Xu, Xue Yu), and sleep quality (ISI scale). The Kaplan-Meier method, Cox proportional hazards model and linear mixed model were used for analysis, and the inverse probability weighting method (IPTW) was used for sensitivity analysis. Results By the end of the follow-up, a total of 23 deaths had occurred, accounting for 56.1% of the total cohort. The median overall survival (OS) was 22.0 months in the control group and 34.0 months in the treatment group, representing a 12.0-month extension in the treatment group; however, the between-group difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank χ2=2.798,P=0.094). IPTW-weighted analysis showed a trend toward reduced mortality risk in the treatment group (HR=0.540,95%CI: 0.231-1.261, P=0.155). In the subgroup of patients with Gleason score ≥9, OS was superior in the treatment group compared with the control group (P=0.039); however, the treatment effect did not reach statistical significance in the multivariate Cox regression analysis (HR=0.299, 95%CI: 0.061-1.478, P=0.139). There was no statistically significant difference in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) between the two groups (log-rank χ2=0.143, P=0.705). Regarding quality of life, FACT-P Version 4 scores increased from 73.50±11.68 at baseline to 81.50±8.45 at 12 months in the treatment group, and from 73.38±9.63 to 77.81±10.60 in the control group. The time × group interaction effect was statistically significant (P<0.05), whereas between-group differences at individual time points did not reach statistical significance after Bonferroni correction (P>0.05). The Shenyang Xu score decreased from (17.10±6.15) to (7.15±3.30) in the treatment group, and from (19.95±2.82) to (17.62±4.63) in the control group. The Xue Yu score decreased from (31.45±13.71) to (13.95±6.00) in the treatment group, and from (37.14±7.49) to (35.00±9.86) in the control group. The time × group interaction effects for both scores were statistically significant (all P<0.01). Regarding sleep quality, the ISI score decreased from (12.60±5.92) to (5.85±2.58) in the treatment group, whereas it changed from (12.29±3.39) to (12.43±4.33) in the control group. The time×group interaction effects for the Shenyang Xu, Xue Yu, and ISI scores were all statistically significant (all P<0.01). Conclusion On the basis of standard endocrine therapy, the combination of Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules was associated with an OS benefit in the CRPC subgroup with Gleason score ≥9. This combination regimen significantly improved Shenyang Xu and Xue Yu syndromes and sleep quality in patients with CRPC, while producing a more sustained trend toward improvement in quality of life.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions for Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to systematically assess the efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions (TGDs) as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of Parkinson's disease (PD) using the latest clinical evidence. Nine databases were searched from their inception to 31 August 2025 to identify eligible studies. Primary outcomes included the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Score (TCMSS) and clinical efficacy. Secondary outcomes encompassed the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), British 39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39), Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale (PDSS), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and adverse events. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to assess the quality of evidence. Thirty-four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving a total of 3049 participants were ultimately included. The results indicated that add-on therapy with TGDs significantly benefited patients with PD by reducing the UPDRS, TCMSS, PDQ-39, and HAMD scores, as well as IL-6, TNF-α and MDA levels, and by increasing clinical efficacy, the MMSE, MoCA, and PDSS scores, and SOD levels. TGDs also reduced the incidence of adverse events, including constipation, gastrointestinal reactions, and the on-off phenomenon. This meta-analysis provided up-to-date and supportive evidence for the efficacy and safety of TGDs as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of patients with PD. Given the generally low certainty of the evidence, more high-quality RCTs are recommended to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Association between bone mineral density, sleep disturbance, and sleep duration: Results from observational and mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: This study combines a nationally representative U.S. cohort with two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to examine associations of sleep disturbance and sleep duration with DXA-measured bone mineral density (BMD) at the femoral neck and lumbar spine. 6421 participants from NHANES 2007-2010 were included. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations between sleep disturbance, sleep duration, and BMD. Two-sample MR with five methods (primary: inverse variance-weighted) corroborated observational findings. Sleep disturbance was negatively associated with BMD at the femoral neck [β: -0.03; 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.04 to -0.02] and the lumbar spine (β: -0.01; 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.00), and remained significant after adjustment (femoral neck: β: -0.01; 95% CI: -0.02 to -0.01; lumbar spine: β: -0.01; 95% CI: -0.02 to 0.00). No significant associations were found between sleep duration and BMD. MR showed consistent negative trends for the effect of sleep disorder on BMD (femoral neck: β: -0.039; 95% CI: -0.142 to 0.063; lumbar spine: β: -0.041; 95% CI: -0.182 to 0.101), though not statistically significant. No causal relationship was found with sleep duration. Sleep disorders may be causally associated with a higher risk of bone loss. Extending sleep duration does not appear to compensate for sleep disorder-related bone loss.

papers.title: Who Takes Long Daytime Naps? Results of the 'German Health Update' (GEDA 2023).
papers.abstract: In the international literature, napping has been associated with positive health outcomes; however, naps lasting at least 60 minutes are linked to adverse health impacts. Until now, representative data on the frequency and duration of naps in Germany have been lacking. Using data from the representative GEDA 2023 study (n = 7,967), this fact sheet presents the prevalence of naps and extended naps (≥ 60 minutes) for women and men, stratified by age and educational groups. Almost half of the adult population in Germany takes a nap at least once a week, a quarter of whom for 60 minutes or more. Extended naps are more prevalent among women under 45 and among less educated men compared with their higher-educated peers. The results highlight the prevalence of napping in the German population, as well as the social groups that more frequently take extended naps and may therefore face higher health risks.

papers.title: Who gets enough sleep? - Sleep duration and classification based on sleep recommendations among the adult population in Germany.
papers.abstract: An insufficient or excessive sleep duration can be associated with various health risks. The National Sleep Foundation recommends seven to nine hours' sleep per night for 18 - 64-year-olds and seven to eight hours' sleep for adults aged 65 and older. The aim of this study is to describe the sleep duration in the adult population in Germany and to identify population groups that meet the sleep duration recommendations. Using data from the GEDA 2023 telephone survey, the mean sleep duration and the prevalence of adherence to sleep recommendations were calculated for weekdays, weekends and the whole week, stratified by gender, age group and educational group. In addition, bedtimes were grouped into categories and predicted probabilities of meeting the recommendations were estimated. On average, the adult population in Germany sleeps for 07:26 hours per night, with longer sleep duration at the weekend, particularly among 18 - 29-year-olds (07:20 hours vs. 08:23 hours). On average, women sleep longer than men (07:31 hours vs. 07:20 hours). Overall, 51.6 % meet the recommended sleep duration, more frequently at weekends than on weekdays (54.7 % vs. 46.7 %) and among those with higher level of education (62.5 %). Later bedtimes are associated with a lower likelihood of meeting the recommendations. Continuous monitoring of sleep behaviour should be established as part of national health monitoring. Additional sleep parameters, such as sleep quality and sleep disorders, should also be taken into account to identify at-risk groups and to target public health measures effectively.

papers.title: Disease Management Distress as a Self-Reinforcing Cascade During Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy for Breast Cancer: A Qualitative Study in Cultural Context.
papers.abstract: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer presents physical, psychological, and social challenges. How these challenges interact and amplify one another remains underexplored, particularly in cultural contexts where family role expectations and emotional restraint shape distress. This study aimed to explore how distress manifests and interacts across physical, emotional, cognitive, and social role dimensions during AET within a specific cultural context. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 17 HR+ breast cancer patients receiving AET from a tertiary hospital in China. Data were analyzed using conventional content analysis. Analysis suggested a self-reinforcing interpretive pattern derived from participant narratives, in which physical symptoms, emotional distress, cognitive difficulties, and social role pressures appeared to interact and could be interpreted as mutually reinforcing. Physical symptoms appeared to disrupt sleep and bodily control; these experiences were often interpreted by patients as signs of disease progression and could trigger fears of recurrence and body-image distress. Treatment management barriers, including rigid medication schedules and standardized education that failed to address individualized concerns, compounded emotional depletion. The loss of social roles and family dismissal of invisible symptoms deepened distress. Culturally patterned responses were evident: shame silenced genitourinary symptom reporting, family role reversal generated disproportionate distress, and repeated invalidation led to self-silencing. AET-related distress could be interpreted as a pattern in which difficulties across multiple dimensions appeared to interact and could be interpreted as mutually reinforcing. Recognizing where a patient stands within this proposed cascade and attending to the cultural norms that shape these experiences may suggest potential intervention directions, which require longitudinal research for further validation.

papers.title: The protocol for a phase 2A, multi centre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to assess the effect of 12 weeks treatment with oral PXS-4728A on microglia activation, as measured by positron emission tomography, in participants with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM-sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a well-described prodromal feature of synuclein diseases, including Parkinson's disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies and, less frequently, multiple system atrophy. Neuroinflammation has been reported in iRBD and is potentially a major contributor to synuclein accumulation and propagation. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) overexpressed by activated microglia has been used to demonstrate neuroinflammation in both iRBD and manifest PD. Although immune-modulating therapies have not shown direct benefit in PD, there are to date no reported trials in prodromal disease. This paper describes the protocol for the first immune-modulating drug trial in iRBD, which could provide evidence for an early neuroprotective intervention strategy in prodromal PD. This is a phase IIa, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial of the small molecule PXS-4728A in iRBD. Forty participants with definitive iRBD, one or more features of Parkinsonism, impaired olfaction and/or impaired colour vision will be randomised 3:1 (treatment: placebo) for a 12-week treatment period, followed by a 12-week washout. The primary outcome will assess the effect of PXS-4728A on neuroinflammation, measured by PET using the TSPO radioligand [11C]-PK11195 across nigro-striato-cortical regions in the treatment arm (within-arm) from baseline to week 12. Between-arm differences will be treated as exploratory. Drug safety and tolerability will also be assessed as a primary outcome. Secondary outcomes include further regional and whole-brain analysis of [11C]-PK11195 binding. Exploratory outcomes will assess change in clinical scales of prodromal symptoms (motor and non-motor), biological markers from blood and CSF, and digital biomarkers (actigraphy, motor and cognitive). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05904717; Identifier, NCT05904717.

papers.title: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism following cemented hemiarthroplasty for pathological femoral fracture: A case report with dual-energy CT spectral analysis.
papers.abstract: Macroscopic pulmonary fat embolism is an uncommon complication of cemented arthroplasty, and its occurrence after fixation of a pathological femoral fracture is rarely documented. We report the case of a 73-year-old woman with metastatic nonsmall cell lung cancer who developed severe hemodynamic instability during cement pressurization for hemiarthroplasty of a pathological right proximal femoral lesion, consistent with bone cement implantation syndrome but not fulfilling the criteria for fat embolism syndrome, and who recovered with supportive care. Dual-energy CT pulmonary angiography showed a 30 × 15 mm filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery and smaller left lower lobe segmental defects, with a mean attenuation of -86.6 HU within the main defect, CT numbers becoming progressively more negative at lower photon energies in contrast to a paraspinal muscle reference, and persistence of the defect on virtual noncontrast images. This case illustrates that attenuation measurement within any postoperative intraluminal filling defect is a simple and potentially decisive step, and that dual-energy spectral analysis may provide complementary support for the fatty nature of an embolus.

papers.title: A Rare Syndrome in Rapid Succession: A Case Report of Two Patients With Chorea-Hyperglycemia-Basal Ganglia (CHBG) Syndrome Within One Month.
papers.abstract: Chorea-Hyperglycemia-Basal Ganglia (CHBG) syndrome, also referred to as diabetic striatopathy, is a very rare and poorly understood cause of chorea and ballismus. Common features of CHBG syndrome include unilateral chorea or ballismus, hyperglycemia, and basal ganglia hyperintensity on neuroimaging. We present two cases of CHBG syndrome who were hospitalized at our community hospital within a 1-month period, an occurrence that is exceedingly rare. The first case presented with subacute progressive right-sided hemiballismus and the second case presented with acute monochorea of the left upper extremity. Both cases presented with uncontrolled Type II diabetes mellitus with HbA1c values ≥ 14%. Both cases experienced symptoms that persisted despite sleep, which is an atypical characteristic among those with CHBG syndrome. In both cases, the formal radiology reports were interpreted as normal. Retrospective review identified faint T1-weighted hyperintensity of the left basal ganglia in Case 1. In Case 2, the consulting neurologist questioned the presence of a very subtle T1-weighted hyperintensity of the right putamen; however, this finding was not described in the formal radiology report, could not be definitively attributed to CHBG syndrome, and its significance remains uncertain. Both cases had significant improvement in their symptoms with strict glycemic management, and both were prescribed adjunctive antichorea medications for additional symptom control. CHBG syndrome is important for physicians to know about and be able to recognize in order to arrive at a timely diagnosis and avoid unnecessary diagnostic testing.

papers.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological condition primarily caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). However, recent research suggests a functional hyperactivity phase that precedes neuronal degeneration and may hold therapeutic potential. This study was conducted as a narrative review to synthesize evidence on early-phase dopaminergic hyperactivation in PD and different interventions that could potentially delay the onset of PD. We identified various toxins and genetic mutations that increase neuronal excitability, which eventually progresses to depletion of SNc neurons. This disrupts the circuitry of the basal ganglia, resulting in compensatory hyperactivity and increased dopamine release. Preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence supports that neurodegeneration in PD is preceded by a period of neuronal hyperactivation marked by increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, revealing altered striatal connections and increased dopamine turnover. This hyperdopaminergic disorder manifests clinically as early non-motor symptoms like autonomic dysfunction, REM sleep behavior disorder, and hyposmia. Multimodal biomarkers that combine genetic, imaging, and electrophysiological data can detect this pre-degenerative stage, making early intervention possible. Calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory medications that target the NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways are examples of novel strategies for preserving neuronal integrity. Therefore, redefining PD as a disorder of reversible neuronal stress instead of permanent degeneration can lead to opportunities for both early and long-term neuroprotection.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: clinical assessment, treatable syndromes, and limits of biomarker inference.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease (AD) affect patients and caregivers, but clinical action depends on the syndrome, measurement, and outcome under consideration. This narrative review links sleep assessment to indication-based care while distinguishing symptomatic benefit, physiological target engagement, and disease modification. A purposive literature search was supplemented by targeted checks of PubMed-indexed and original publisher records through 4 October 2026. Selected studies are described by population, AD ascertainment, comparator, and measured endpoint rather than assigned formal evidence-certainty grades. Actigraphy characterizes behavioral rest-activity patterns; melatonin timing and temperature rhythms address endogenous circadian physiology under controlled conditions. Polysomnography and quantitative electroencephalography characterize respiratory events, sleep architecture, and oscillatory activity. These measurements inform different questions and do not independently assign AD etiology or cognitive-functional stage. Clinical priorities include confirmed obstructive sleep apnea, cognition-adapted insomnia care, irregular sleep timing, medication-related effects, parasomnias, limb symptoms, and excessive daytime sleepiness. Interpretation incorporates hypoxemia, treatment exposure, comorbidity, caregiver support, and competing diagnoses. Randomized sleep benefits remain distinct from observational cognitive associations or exploratory imaging and cerebrospinal fluid changes. Human and animal studies of arousal circuits, protein dynamics, inflammation, and fluid transport provide mechanistic context, with conflicting results interpreted according to the actual experimental endpoint. The review provides a clinically organized account of selected evidence, not a comprehensive treatment ranking. Sleep care and cognitive-etiologic assessment should proceed in parallel, with follow-up matched to patient function, safety, and the specific treatment goal.

papers.title: Experiences of maternal distress and early childhood development amid climate-related stress in Benue state, Nigeria: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Climate-related flooding and extreme heat affect maternal and child wellbeing in low-and middle-income countries. Although evidence suggests that climate-related events can affect mental health and child wellbeing, little is known about how these experiences are described in flood-prone settings. This study explores participants' accounts of flooding, extreme heat, and household vulnerability in Benue State and their perceived implications for maternal mental health and early childhood development. A qualitative descriptive design was used. Data were collected through six focus group discussions and six semi-structured interviews with 54 mothers, health workers, community leaders, and policymakers and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants described flooding as a recurrent threat shaped by spatial vulnerability, poor drainage, and inadequate land-use planning. Participants described flooding in relation to disrupted routines, livelihoods, food and water security, and caregiving; mothers and health workers also described extreme heat as disrupting sleep and caregiving. Participants described maternal psychological distress associated with uncertainty, household disruption, economic losses, and caregiving demands. Participants described challenges affecting children's nutrition, healthcare access, immunisation, learning, safety, and social development. Community coping strategies included collective action and social support, while participants described gaps in formal responses. The findings highlight interconnected experiences of climate-related disruption, maternal distress, caregiving, and conditions relevant to early childhood wellbeing. Responses could support continuity of health services, nutrition, early learning, safe environments, psychosocial support, and community participation.

papers.title: The FaesMYB15-FaesELF3 module regulates flowering time, floral organ number, and floral color in red flower long-homostyle common buckwheat.
papers.abstract: EARLY FLOWERING 3 (ELF3) is a core member of the Evening Complex (EC) and plays a critical role in regulating flowering through the plant circadian clock. R2R3-MYB transcription factors (TFs) control the transcriptional regulation of anthocyanin structural genes involved in anthocyanin accumulation in various plants and also play important roles involved in floral development. However, how ELF3 homologs work together with R2R3-MYB TFs to regulate flowering, floral organ development, and flower color remains unclear. In this study, R2R3-MYB TF FaesMYB15 directly binds to the FaesELF3 promoter and suppresses expression of FaesELF3 in common buckwheat. In addition, overexpression of FaesELF3 in red flower LH Fagopyrum esculentum leads to significantly earlier flowering and rapid plant growth, and results in flowers with increased tepal and stamen numbers and a lighter tepal color in transgenic plant. Moreover, total anthocyanin content in the inflorescence of the 35S::FaesELF3 line was significantly lower than that of the normal red flower LH common buckwheat. FaesELF3 overexpression markedly downregulated the expressions of two core circadian clock genes, FaesPRR5-1 and FaesPRR5-2, and two AGAMOUS-like MADS-box genes, FaesAGL18 and FaesAGL19, involved in flowering regulation in transgenic plants. Our study introduces a new regulator module of FaesMYB15-FaesELF3 involved in regulating flowering time, floral color, and floral organ number in crops, providing insights for novel breeding strategies of flowering regulation and flower color modification in common buckwheat.

papers.title: Circadian rhythmicity in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are time-critical events that exhibit circadian patterns, which influence their incidence and clinical outcomes. To determine whether circadian rhythmicity influences the time of onset of OHCA and STEMI, as well as related clinical outcomes, in patients requiring prehospital emergency care and subsequent hospitalization. A scoping review. The search process included four online databases: MEDLINE Complete, CINAHL Plus with Full Text, ScienceDirect, and ProQuest. The review included original articles published between January 2010 and December 2024. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. These revealed that the incidence of OHCA and STEMI exhibits significant circadian variability, with the highest incidence in the morning. OHCA often has a secondary afternoon/evening peak. The nighttime hours are associated with the lowest incidence. Patients with nighttime OHCA or STEMI have a lower probability of return of spontaneous circulation and worse one-month and one-year survival and neurological outcomes. This less favorable prognosis is not due to the time of day when the event occurs but rather due to limited bystander availability, lower rates of bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, and longer times to hospital intervention. Additionally, these events were more frequently recorded in winter, while weekly variations were insignificant. Circadian and seasonal factors influence the occurrence and clinical course of OHCA and STEMI, with worse outcomes for nighttime cases being more a consequence of limited availability than the time of the event itself.
papers.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)

papers.title: HEALTH AND SOCIAL IMPACT OF THE INTERNET AND SOCIAL MEDIA ON AFRICAN CHILDREN: A NARRATIVE REVIEW AND A CALL TO ACTION.
papers.abstract: Internet and social media are increasingly embedded in children's education, relationships, and leisure. For African children, this expansion is occurring alongside marked inequalities in connectivity, digital literacy, parental mediation, and online protection. To synthesise evidence on the health and social effects of internet and social media use among African children and derive practical multilevel actions. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed Central, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online were searched for literature published from January 2016 to June 2025. African studies and relevant reviews or policy reports involving persons younger than 18 years were narratively synthesised. Findings were mapped to a social ecological framework. Digital technologies support learning, access to information, social connection, and creativity. However, excessive or poorly supervised use is associated with sleep disruption, mental health symptoms, problematic internet use, sedentary behaviour, visual complaints, cyberbullying, exploitation, privacy harms, and academic disruption. Exposure and risk differ substantially by age, sex, residence, household resources, and parental support. Much of the available evidence is cross-sectional and does not establish causality. African responses should protect children without excluding them from digital opportunities. Coordinated action by families, schools, health professionals, communities, governments, and technology companies is required.

papers.title: Factors associated with the preoperative electrophysiological severity of carpal tunnel syndrome and correlation with early postoperative hand function status.
papers.abstract: To investigate factors associated with preoperative electrophysiological severity in carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) and the correlation between electrophysiological severity and early postoperative hand function status. A total of 148 patients with CTS diagnosed by clinical examination, nerve conduction studies and supplementary electromyography in the study hospital between 1 January 2024 and 1 December 2024 were retrospectively enrolled in this study. Based on preoperative electrophysiological severity, CTS patients were split into mild, moderate, and severe groups. At 3 weeks post-treatment, we collected demographic data, anthropometric measurements, and scores from the LCTQ, PRWE, and DASH questionnaires. Statistical analyses included one-way ANOVA, chi-square tests, and ordinal logistic regression. With the escalation of disease severity, disease duration (14.66 ± 5.59 vs. 27.35 ± 11.67 vs. 34.81 ± 11.22, p < 0.001) and transverse carpal diameter (36.68 ± 3.03 vs. 38.78 ± 2.76 vs. 40.92 ± 2.89, p < 0.001) increased progressively, whereas the ratio of wrist circumference to transverse carpal diameter decreased (4.24 ± 0.39 vs. 4.07 ± 0.39 vs. 3.92 ± 0.38, p < 0.001). The ordinal logistic regression showed that disease duration, transverse carpal diameter and wrist circumference/transverse carpal diameter were independent factors associated with electrophysiological severity (omnibus test: p < 0.001, Nagelkerke pseudo R 2 = 0.622). Preoperative LCTQ, PRWE and DASH scores were significantly higher in the severe group than in the mild or moderate groups (all p < 0.001). At 3 weeks postoperatively, all scores were significantly improved from baseline (all p < 0.001) but still differed across groups. Correlation analysis revealed that LCTQ (r = 0.63), PRWE (r = 0.42) and DASH (r = 0.87) results were all positively correlated with preoperative electrophysiological severity. Disease duration, transverse carpal diameter and the ratio of wrist circumference to transverse carpal diameter were associated with electrophysiological severity in patients with CTS, with longer disease durations, larger transverse carpal diameters and smaller wrist circumference-to-transverse carpal diameter ratios corresponding to greater electrophysiological severity and poorer early postoperative function statuses.

papers.title: Screen time, physical activity, and overweight/obesity among school-aged children and adolescents in Heilongjiang Province, China: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Childhood overweight and obesity are major public health concerns in China. The activity displacement hypothesis provides a plausible framework linking electronic-device use, physical activity, and weight status, but its applicability may vary across settings. This study examined overweight/obesity and explored whether physical-activity frequency formed a statistical pathway between daily electronic-device use and overweight/obesity among school-aged children and adolescents in Heilongjiang Province, China. This cross-sectional secondary analysis used data collected between October 2024 and April 2025 from participating schools in Daqing, Heihe, and Yichun/Wangkui. Of 26,535 survey records, 14,095 had nonmissing values for the outcome, exposure, age, and prespecified covariates and were retained in the original analysis. The questionnaire recorded average total daily electronic-device use, exercise frequency, nighttime sleep duration, and parental education. Multivariable logistic regression and sex- and grade-stratified models were fitted. To harmonize exposure specification, additional logistic models treated daily electronic-device use continuously, with and without adjustment for physical-activity frequency; school-clustered robust standard errors were examined as a sensitivity analysis. An exploratory bootstrap decomposition with 1,000 iterations estimated direct and indirect statistical associations through physical-activity frequency. Among 14,095 participants, the prevalence of overweight/obesity was 38.2%. Male sex showed the strongest association (OR = 2.67, 95% CI: 2.48-2.87). A higher physical-activity frequency score (OR = 0.94) and a higher approximate sleep-duration score (OR = 0.96) were inversely associated with overweight/obesity. In the added continuous-exposure analysis, each additional reported hour/day was weakly associated before adjustment for physical activity (OR = 1.019, 95% CI: 1.002-1.035, p = 0.025) but not after adjustment (OR = 1.014, 95% CI: 0.998-1.031, p = 0.085); neither estimate was statistically significant with school-clustered robust standard errors. The exploratory decomposition yielded a direct probability difference of 0.0033 and an indirect probability difference of 0.0011 through physical-activity frequency; the descriptive indirect proportion was 24.35%. The association between reported daily electronic-device use and overweight/obesity was small and sensitive to exposure specification, physical-activity adjustment, and variance estimation. The fitted models were compatible with a small indirect statistical association through physical-activity frequency, but the cross-sectional data do not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation. Longitudinal studies using validated measures are needed.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Resting-state EEG characteristics may differ between autistic and non-autistic children. Conventional band power mixes periodic and broadband activity; spectral parameterization separates periodic peaks from the aperiodic background. Auditory integration training (AIT) is used as a complementary intervention, but its immediate neurophysiological and clinical effects remain uncertain. We examined baseline EEG differences and pre-post changes around one AIT session. Twenty children with ASD and 15 typically developing (TD) children aged 6-8 years participated. Resting EEG was recorded in ASD before and immediately after a 30-min Berard AIT session. Sixteen ASD participants had usable paired recordings. Relative power was measured in five bands. Periodic and aperiodic components were parameterized with FOOOF. Sensitivity analyses varied R-squared threshold, aperiodic mode, fitting settings, channel aggregation. At baseline, ASD showed higher delta and lower theta, alpha, and beta relative power than TD. After modeling peaks, aperiodic exponent and offset did not differ between groups. Among 16 paired ASD recordings, delta decreased and beta/gamma increased post-session; paired tests of exponent and offset were nonsignificant. Five of 20 baseline and seven of 18 post-session recordings had R-squared<0.90, but sensitivity analyses did not change null aperiodic findings. This uncontrolled pilot study found immediate pre-post band-power differences around one Berard AIT session but no significant FOOOF-derived aperiodic changes. Findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot distinguish AIT-specific effects from repeated measurement, arousal, expectancy, or generic auditory stimulation. Variable fit quality and small sample limit precision; controlled longitudinal studies are needed.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.abstract: The Tibetan Buddhist tradition distinguishes between two broad categories of meditation: Sutra and Tantra, which differ in the methods and mental faculties they employ. The main neurophysiological studies of Tibetan Buddhist meditation have been conducted mostly on Sutra practices; while Tantric meditation remains less studied. This publication presents a dual comparative study, using both between-groups and within-subjects design, of the neurophysiological (EEG) correlates characterizing Sutra and Tantra meditative practices, examining both the meditative states and the meditative traits. The study was carried out within the natural environment of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in India, maintaining the socio-cultural context. Two groups of long-term practitioners (Buddhist monks of Gelug lineage), one experienced in the Tantra tradition (T-group, n = 21) and the other in the Sutra tradition (S-group, n = 20) participated in the study. A between-group cluster permutation test revealed that the groups differed in EEG alpha power during meditation, as well as in baseline resting conditions before and after meditation. Specifically, T-group demonstrated consistently lower alpha power compared to the S-group, regardless of the conditions. Thus, the observed differences are stable characteristics of the groups. The within-subjects analysis demonstrated that the conditions (meditation, and baseline resting states before and after meditation) differed only in the T-group: during meditation, an increase in individual alpha peak frequency (iAPF) was observed in the occipital leads, followed by a decrease in iAPF after meditation. We suggest that reported between-group differences represent enduring meditative traits developed through years of training in meditative techniques in the Sutra and Tantra traditions. Nevertheless, we cannot entirely exclude the possibility that these variations may also stem from certain cohort-specific characteristics unrelated to meditation. An examination of individual power spectra revealed that the absence of significant differences in EEG spectral power between conditions can be primarily attributed to the inter-individual variability in both groups. This variability, in turn, may stem from extensive expertise of highly experienced practitioners, who over years of training, develop individualized cognitive strategies for maintaining the meditative state. Our future research will focus on a more detailed quantitative analysis of inter-individual variability during meditations and on identifying additional between-group differences among practitioners in different traditions.

papers.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a mindfulness-based vitality promotion program in a lifelong learning setting: a single-arm mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract: As global aging accelerates, age-related psychophysiological conditions have emerged as major public health concerns. Promoting and sustaining vitality, an inherent human capacity, is essential for healthy aging and long-term well-being. The Mindfulness-based Vitality Promotion (MVP) program is a mindfulness-based behavioral intervention designed to enhance physical and psychological vitality and support sustainable well-being. This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of the MVP program and explored preliminary pre-post changes in health-related outcomes among community-dwelling individuals in a lifelong learning setting. This study employed a single-arm mixed-methods design. A total of 35 participants were recruited for this study. The MVP program was delivered over 8 weeks, with each session lasting 90 min. Quantitative data were collected through self-report questionnaires, and qualitative data were obtained via semi-structured interviews. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed based on program retention, session attendance, and participant satisfaction. Quantitative analysis revealed significant pre-post increases in integrative vitality and well-being, along with significant reductions in depression, fatigue, and anxiety. No statistically significant changes were observed in pain, sleep disturbance, digestive symptoms, anger, or mindfulness. Of the 35 enrolled participants, 31 completed the program (88.6%), with a mean attendance of 6.37 of eight sessions. Among the 30 satisfaction survey respondents, 28 (93.3%) indicated willingness to participate again and 30 (100%) indicated willingness to recommend the program to others. The qualitative analysis identified four major themes: (i) diverse life challenges and self-care needs, (ii) learning through experience, connection, and application, (iii) regaining balance and agency in life, and (iv) sustaining practice requires continued support. Mixed-methods findings provide preliminary information regarding the feasibility and acceptability of the MVP program and indicate favorable pre-post changes in several self-reported health-related outcomes. The MVP program may represent a practical lifelong learning intervention with potential relevance for public health promotion. Further controlled studies are warranted to establish its efficacy. The trial was first submitted to the Clinical Research Information Service, Republic of Korea (KCT0009961, https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=28524&search_page=L), on October 8, 2024, before participant enrollment began, and registration was finalized on November 28, 2024.

papers.title: Blood pressure changes across pregnancy and postpartum: from physiological adaptations to pathological deviations.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy represents a unique physiological period characterized by dynamic cardiovascular adaptations and changes in blood pressure (BP) throughout gestation and the postpartum period. Deviations from these expected patterns may represent a risk to maternal health and be associated with the development of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Personalized and continuous monitoring, including BP measurements and the assessment of longitudinal and circadian BP patterns, can contribute to the earlier identification of women at risk. Accurate BP assessment remains central to the diagnosis and management of HDP. In this context, out-of-office BP assessment, particularly 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, may provide additional information and identify abnormalities that remain undetected by conventional office measurements. HDP are among the most frequent complications of pregnancy and are associated with increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Their management extends beyond delivery, as postpartum hypertension remains underrecognized, and adequate follow-up and timely, targeted antihypertensive treatment are essential. Emerging strategies, including home BP monitoring, telemedicine-based programs, and multidisciplinary postpartum hypertension clinics, may improve continuity of care. This review examines physiological and pathological BP changes across pregnancy and the postpartum period, with particular emphasis on longitudinal BP trajectories and circadian patterns, beyond absolute BP values alone, as potential early indicators of HDP, while integrating current evidence and guideline recommendations on their diagnosis, monitoring, and management.

papers.title: Effect of multi-pin atmospheric pressure DBD cold plasma treatment on the anti-nutritional, optical, functional, morphological, and pasting properties of finger millet (Eleusine coracana) grain.
papers.abstract: This study explores the effect of cold plasma treatment on finger millets (Eleusine coracana) to reduce anti-nutritional factors and improve its nutritional value. The study utilized a Box-Behnken experimental design to assess the effect of process parameters-voltage, treatment time, and electrode distance-on the anti-nutritional factors in finger millet grains. Results revealed that under optimized condition (20 kV, 18-min treatment time, and 10 cm electrode distance), there is a significant reduction in phytic acid (30%) and tannin content (24.4%). Additional analyses showed improvements in water absorption (9.52%), oil absorption (0.154 ± 0.09 g/g to 0.904 ± 0.002 g/g), water solubility index (13.24%), emulsifying (28.1%), and foaming capacity (8.01-10.49%) of treated samples, enhancing their functional and pasting properties. The FTIR spectral analysis indicates similar patterns, showing alterations in the concentration of functional groups. Meanwhile, SEM images reveal cracks in the surface morphology following treatment. The study concludes that cold plasma is an innovative technology for minimizing antinutrients and enhancing nutritional quality of finger millet, making it more suitable for consumption.
papers.journal: Journal of food science and technology

papers.title: Prevalence of nocturnal and isolated nocturnal hypertension in population-based studies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Nocturnal hypertension (NH) and isolated nocturnal hypertension (INH) require nighttime blood pressure assessment, but published prevalence estimates differ in sampling, treatment eligibility, and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) protocols. This study aimed to summarize NH and study-defined INH proportions in population/community samples. Four databases were searched through 17 March 2026. Logit random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the nine-item Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) 2017 checklist. Clinical/occupational and circadian-pattern reports were described individually rather than pooled. Nine NH estimates from four sources included 8,282 participants and 3,331 cases. Pooled prevalence was 42.5% (95% CI, 33.2%-52.3%; approximate 95% prediction interval, 17.2%-72.3%; I2 = 97.6%). Four INH estimates included 3,659 participants and 657 cases; the descriptive pooled proportion was 17.3% (95% CI, 10.4%-27.5%; prediction interval, 3.6%-54.0%; I2 = 91.5%). INH denominators differed by treatment eligibility; a sensitivity analysis using reported non-treated denominators yielded 19.6% (95% CI, 11.4%-31.6%). Certainty was judged very low. A sensitivity requiring both original nighttime recording-quality criteria could not be estimated from the published aggregate data. NH and INH were common in the population-based and community samples studied. These findings provide reference estimates for planning population-based studies and evaluating targeted detection strategies using ABPM. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251233166, identifier PROSPERO CRD420251233166.

papers.title: Current strategies of cerebral oxygenation monitoring in general intensive care units: a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Cerebral hypoxia represents the final metabolic consequence of sustained intracranial pressure and impaired autoregulation. Continuous cerebral oxygen monitoring is essential to prevent secondary ischemic injury in neurocritical care particularly in severe traumatic brain injury, malignant infarction, and aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. It also guides management of systemic disturbances such as shock, sepsis, and respiratory failure and is increasingly used perioperatively in high-risk cardiac, carotid, and neurosurgical procedures. To synthesize physiological principles, monitoring modalities, and clinical applications of cerebral oxygenation across neurocritical care and perioperative settings, emphasizing bedside interpretation and integration within multimodal neuromonitoring. PubMed and Scopus were searched (January 2010-January 2025) using MeSH terms and keywords including "cerebral oxygenation," "brain tissue oxygen tension," "jugular bulb saturation," and "near-infrared spectroscopy." Fifty-eight English-language studies (randomized controlled trials, observational studies, reviews, and editorials) were included. Non-English publications, animal studies, conference abstracts, unavailable full texts, and non-peer-reviewed articles were excluded. Brain tissue oxygen tension, jugular bulb oximetry, and near-infrared spectroscopy provide complementary insights. Brain tissue oxygen tension is invasive and region-specific (<25 mmHg indicates high risk), jugular bulb oximetry reflects global cerebral oxygen extraction, and near-infrared spectroscopy enables noninvasive regional trend monitoring. Multimodal neuromonitoring integrating these with intracranial pressure, transcranial Doppler, and electroencephalography improves detection and management of secondary ischemia. In neurocritical care, invasive monitoring supports targeted interventions, whereas in ICU and perioperative settings, multimodal strategies balance diagnostic yield and feasibility. Cerebral oxygen monitoring should be routinely implemented in high-risk patients. Multimodal neuromonitoring should be prioritized to detect hypoxia early and guide individualized cerebral perfusion strategies. Near-infrared spectroscopy should be used for continuous monitoring, while invasive modalities should be reserved for high-risk neurocritical patients. Standardized thresholds and protocolized approaches should be established through prospective, outcome-driven research.
papers.journal: Journal of critical care medicine (Universitatea de Medicina si Farmacie din Targu-Mures)

papers.title: Latent profiles of day-7 cognitive performance and associated ecological factors in older adults after elective surgery: an observational study.
papers.abstract: To identify latent profiles of postoperative day-7 cognitive performance among older adults after elective surgery and to explore demographic, behavioral, clinical, and social factors associated with profile membership. This prospective observational study included 308 consecutively recruited patients aged ≥65 years who underwent elective surgery under general anesthesia. Cognition was assessed with the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and latent profile analysis used five study-defined postoperative domain scores. Candidate correlates were organized with the health ecological model and examined using univariate tests and posterior-probability-weighted exploratory multinomial regression. Three severity-ordered profiles were identified: low (n=83, 26.9%), intermediate (n=72, 23.4%), and high postoperative cognitive performance (n=153, 49.7%). Older age and lower education were associated with both lower-performance profiles. Greater activities-of-daily-living dependence, lower income, and living alone were associated with the low-performance profile, whereas poorer sleep was associated with the intermediate-performance profile. Day-7 MMSE performance formed a severity gradient across three data-driven profiles. These cross-sectional profiles do not demonstrate postoperative decline, a clinical diagnosis, or an effect attributable specifically to general anesthesia. Longitudinal studies with retained baseline scores, appropriate comparison groups, and broader neuropsychological assessment are required before profile-specific interventions can be recommended.

papers.title: Advancing experimental fish welfare: insights from the Swiss fish welfare meeting 2026.
papers.abstract: Fish are widely used in research and aquaculture, yet many aspects of their welfare remain poorly understood. Recent years have seen a shift from health and disease prevention as cornerstones of wellbeing toward concepts of welfare that include behavior, affective states, cumulative lifetime experiences, and positive welfare. Current challenges relate to the taxonomic diversity of fishes, the dominance of zebrafish as model species, and the translation of welfare concepts across experimental, applied, and industrial settings. Knowledge gaps remain regarding welfare assessment, environmental enrichment, euthanasia, pain management, and the implementation of evidence-based refinement measures. Here we summarize the outcomes of the Swiss Fish Welfare Symposium 2026, which brought together researchers, caretakers, veterinarians, regulators, and industry. Participants identified drivers of change such as a Culture of Care, improved knowledge exchange, and incentive structures to reward refinement. Presentations emphasized the need for welfare research under realistic husbandry conditions, the development of cumulative and species-specific welfare assessment tools, and the generation of evidence for housing, enrichment, analgesia, euthanasia, and rehoming practices. Speakers stressed that recommendations developed under idealized conditions often fail to reflect the practical realities of research facilities and aquaculture systems. The symposium revealed a research field in transition from compliance-based approaches toward a vision of welfare that encompasses both animal and human well-being. Participants identified collaboration, systematic use of existing welfare data, and research beyond zebrafish as critical priorities. More broadly, discussions highlighted the need to bridge gaps between fundamental research, regulation, husbandry practice, and industry to achieve evidence-based and implementable improvements in fish welfare.

papers.title: Regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences exceed longitudinal changes across an approximately 34-h protocol: a prospective quality-controlled proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
papers.abstract: Regional organization, acquisition sequence, and measurement quality can obscure the interpretation of longitudinal proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) changes. We compared anterior vs. posterior cingulate metabolite-ratio differences with changes across an approximately 34-h protocol and tested whether findings depended on sequence, quality-control rules, respiratory burden, comorbidity, or polysomnographic sleep measures. In this prospective single-center observational study, 138 university-affiliated and advertisement-recruited participants underwent baseline evening spectroscopy of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) on day 1, full-night polysomnography from day 2 into day 3, and post-PSG morning spectroscopy on day 3 using MEGA-PRESS and SVS-PRESS. Among 116 participants with complete paired timestamps, the median interval between scan starts was 34.01 h (IQR, 33.86-34.10 h). Primary metabolite-to-creatine ratios were analyzed using age-, sex-, and body mass index-adjusted generalized estimating equations. Sensitivity analyses evaluated effect magnitude, sequence dependence, spectral-quality selection, follow-up availability, exclusion of participants with apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/h, exclusion of hypertension or diabetes, and associations between metabolite change and seven polysomnographic measures. A total of 137 participants contributed to adjusted primary models. PCC showed higher NAA/Cr in both sequences and higher SVS GlxT/Cr, whereas ACC showed higher Cho/Cr in both sequences and higher MEGA Glu/Cr (all q < 0.001); PCC also showed higher MEGA GABA/Cr (q = 0.020). Cr2 denotes the vendor-fitted second creatine/phosphocreatine resonance, and GlxT denotes the sum of six vendor-fitted glutamate/glutamine components. Follow-up reductions that survived false-discovery-rate correction were confined to SVS Cr2/Cr and GlxT/Cr. Across 11 outcomes, the median absolute paired standardized effect size was 0.571 for region and 0.125 for longitudinal change; the former was 4.6 times the latter, a ratio of median standardized effect magnitudes rather than a biological fold difference. Excluding AHI ≥ 15 events/h preserved the direction of all 12 primary FDR-significant effects, with 11 remaining q < 0.05. None of 77 polysomnographic dose-response tests survived global correction. In this heterogeneous cohort, regional differences in cingulate metabolite ratios were larger and more robust than longitudinal changes. Because the approximately 34-h contrast combined elapsed time, circadian phase, an intervening monitored night, repositioning, and other uncontrolled influences, it should not be interpreted as a sleep-specific effect. The ratio-based findings should not be interpreted as regional concentration differences.

papers.title: Trajectories of perinatal depression, anxiety, perceived stress, sleep quality, and psychological flexibility from pregnancy to six months postpartum and their relationship with the number of abortions and deliveries.
papers.abstract: Perinatal psychological distress is common and longitudinally heterogeneous, yet little is known about how obstetric history shapes symptom trajectories. We identified trajectories of depressive symptoms, perceived stress, sleep quality, psychological flexibility, and anxiety from early pregnancy to 24 weeks postpartum and examined their associations with the number of previous abortions and deliveries. In this prospective longitudinal cohort study, 254 pregnant women were recruited at 13 weeks of gestation from a tertiary hospital in China and assessed eight times through 24 weeks postpartum using the EPDS, CPSS, PSQI, CompACT, and GAD-7. Group-based trajectory modeling identified latent trajectory classes. Logistic regression examined associations with obstetric history, adjusting for sociodemographic covariates. Three trajectories emerged for depressive symptoms (low-stable, 38.98%; mild-stable, 47.24%; moderate-increasing, 13.78%), perceived stress (low-stable, 31.89%; moderate-increasing, 16.54%; high-stable, 51.57%), and sleep quality (good-stable, 50.00%; mild-worsening, 38.58%; persistent poor, 11.42%); two emerged for psychological flexibility (continuously declining vs high-stable) and anxiety (low-stable, 93.70%; moderate, 6.30%). Compared with women without abortion history, those with two or more abortions had higher odds of mild-stable (OR = 5.14) and moderate-increasing depression (OR = 19.12), mild-worsening (OR = 3.06) and persistent poor sleep (OR = 5.51), and declining psychological flexibility (OR = 2.61); one abortion was associated with increased stress (OR = 2.54 and 2.16) and moderate anxiety (OR = 4.18). Number of deliveries was not associated with any trajectory. Previous abortions predict adverse perinatal psychological trajectories in a dose-dependent manner. Routine assessment of abortion history at the first prenatal visit could help target early screening and tailored interventions.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.abstract: Magnetic seizure therapy (MST) is an emerging convulsive treatment for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) with efficacy comparable to electroconvulsive therapy and superior cognitive safety. However, its neurophysiological mechanisms-particularly those underlying conflict monitoring and response inhibition-remain unclear. Frontal midline theta-band activity indexes anterior cingulate-prefrontal cognitive-control activity and may reflect inefficient neural processing in depression. In this open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with TRD (16 female; mean age 20.89 ± 8.16 years; 10 of the 19 participants were minors) received 6-12 MST sessions using 100-Hz double-cone coil stimulation targeting bilateral F3/F4 frontal regions. Clinical assessments, including the 24-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-24), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), and 64-channel Go/Nogo task-based electroencephalography (EEG), were performed before and after treatment. EEG outcome measures included event-related potentials (N2/P3), time-frequency power (theta/beta), microstate dynamics, and theta-beta cross-frequency coupling. Following MST, patients showed significant reductions in depressive symptoms (HAMD: 40.53 ± 10.25 to 22.53 ± 11.21; MADRS: 35.68 ± 8.84 to 20.68 ± 11.12). Response rates ranged from 42.1% to 57.9%. Behavioral data could not be formally analyzed due to incomplete data storage. At an uncorrected threshold, total Nogo-related theta-band activity (4-7 Hz) at Fz and FCz was lower after treatment; however, these effects did not survive FDR correction. ERP amplitudes did not change significantly. Exploratory microstate analysis showed nominal changes in Map4 AUC during Go processing and Map2 duration during Nogo processing; none survived FDR correction. These parameters should not be interpreted as reflecting changes in neural activation or inhibitory preparation. No significant changes were observed in theta-beta cross-frequency coupling or Go-condition theta power. These preliminary findings suggest that MST was associated with short-term symptom improvement and lower total Nogo-related theta-band activity at an uncorrected threshold. Because no control group, complete behavioral data, normative comparison, Time × Condition interaction, or EEG-clinical association was available, these findings cannot establish causal mechanisms, condition specificity, improved neural efficiency, or biomarker utility. Replication in adequately powered controlled studies with complete behavioral and longitudinal clinical measures is required.

papers.title: Physical activity and sleep quality among college students: the sequential indirect associations of negative attentional bias and bedtime procrastination.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality is fundamental to college students' physical and psychological health and academic functioning. Amid increasing digitalization and stress, sleep problems remain prevalent among college students. Previous research has shown that physical activity, cognitive processing styles, and behavioral regulation patterns are associated with sleep outcomes, but these variables have often been examined separately, with limited attention to their integrated association structure. Based on cross-sectional survey data, this study used latent-variable structural equation modeling to examine the sequential indirect association pattern among physical activity, negative attentional bias, bedtime procrastination, and sleep quality. Using cluster sampling, data were collected from 921 college students from four universities in East China (439 males, 482 females; M_age = 20.34, SD = 1.59). Measures included the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS-3), Negative Attentional Bias Scale, Bedtime Procrastination Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Structural equation modeling and bootstrap methods examined indirect associations. Results indicated that physical activity was significantly associated with lower PSQI scores, indicating better sleep quality (B_total = -0.072, β_total = -0.440, p < 0.001). Negative attentional bias and bedtime procrastination both showed significant partial indirect associations. The simple indirect associations through negative attentional bias and bedtime procrastination accounted for 20.8 and 15.3% of the total association, respectively. The sequential indirect association "physical activity → negative attentional bias → bedtime procrastination → sleep quality" was also significant, although its proportion was relatively small (4.2%). Overall, the total indirect association accounted for 40.3% of the total association. Multi-group structural analysis indicated that the association structure was broadly comparable across gender groups, although associations involving bedtime procrastination appeared stronger among female students. By integrating cognitive processing and behavioral regulation perspectives, this study provides a more integrative view of the association between physical activity and sleep quality. The findings suggest that college students' sleep problems may be embedded within a broader system of health behaviors and psychological processes. Given the cross-sectional design, future longitudinal or experimental studies should examine the dynamic associations among these variables.

papers.title: Food craving in a cultural context: behavioral and electrophysiological evidence from Indian and Western food sets.
papers.abstract: Food craving is a ubiquitous experience, often shaped by cultural familiarity. Although craving may be considered a culture-bound construct, its neural and behavioral underpinnings across food cultures remain limited. Here, we examined the effects of multisensory food exposure on craving in an Indian population, comparing Indian and Western foods across sweet and savory categories. In Experiment 1 (Indian Food Craving; IFC), participants viewed Indian sweet and savory food images before and after multisensory exposure, reporting desire and willingness-to-pay (bid) ratings along with Food Craving Questionnaire-State (FCQ-S) scores. EEG was recorded using a 64-channel system. In Experiment 2 (Western Food Craving; WFC), participants completed a similar paradigm using Western food items. Multisensory exposure significantly increased FCQ-S scores in both experiments, indicating successful craving induction. Behaviorally, desire and bid ratings increased for both sweet and savory Indian foods, whereas for Western foods, increases were observed only for sweet items. ERP analyses revealed increased P200 and N200 amplitudes following exposure to Indian sweet foods, while LPP amplitudes increased for savory foods across both Indian and Western food categories. Complementary MVPA revealed enhanced pre- vs. post-exposure classification for sweet foods during the early (0-300 ms) window for both Indian and Western foods, whereas both sweet and savory foods showed significant classification during the later(300-600 ms) window. Together, these findings suggest that multisensory exposure modulates food-cue processing in a stimulus- and time-dependent manner, with possible contributions from attentional processes. Overall, the findings highlight the influence of food type and cultural context on craving-related neural and behavioral responses.

papers.title: Effects of acceptance and commitment therapy on psychological and health-related outcomes in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of disability worldwide and is frequently accompanied by psychological and functional impairments. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a third-wave behavioral intervention focusing on psychological flexibility, has been increasingly applied in stroke rehabilitation. Although previous reviews have suggested beneficial effects of ACT in stroke patients, whether these benefits persist in the short term after the intervention ends, and the certainty of the evidence, remain unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261325108). Randomized controlled trials evaluating ACT in stroke patients were included. Pooled effects were calculated using random-effects models, with separate analyses for post-intervention and follow-up outcomes. Sources of heterogeneity were explored using subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Twenty-two RCTs involving 1,975 participants were included. ACT may be associated with reductions in depressive symptoms (post-intervention: SMD = -1.32, 95% CI: -1.80 to -0.84; follow-up: SMD = -0.76, 95% CI: -1.07 to -0.45) and anxiety symptoms (post-intervention: SMD = -1.36, 95% CI: -1.90 to -0.82; follow-up: SMD = -0.51, 95% CI: -1.42 to 0.40, not significant); depressive symptoms remained statistically significant at follow-up. Heterogeneity was considerable for both outcomes at post-intervention (I2 = 93.68% for depression and 93.60% for anxiety), so the pooled estimates represent average effects across studies. ACT may also be associated with improvements in psychological flexibility, quality of life, and sleep quality; however, these outcomes were based on a limited number of studies and showed considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.68 to 92.26%), so they should be interpreted cautiously. However, no statistically significant effects were observed for activities of daily living, neurological function, or hope. ACT did not appear to increase dropout rates in the available studies (K = 16; RR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.58-1.69). Meta-regression analyses indicated that intervention duration may not be a significant moderator of treatment effects. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, mainly due to risk of bias and inconsistency. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy may be a useful adjunctive intervention for improving psychological outcomes in people with stroke. However, evidence for functional recovery remains insufficient. Future high-quality RCTs with standardized protocols, larger samples, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm the long-term effectiveness of ACT. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifer CRD420261325108.

papers.title: Decomposition of gender disparities in abnormal sleep duration among Chinese older adults: evidence from a national survey.
papers.abstract: Sleep duration is an important component of healthy aging, yet gender differences in short and long sleep among older adults remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine gender differences in sleep duration among Chinese older adults and quantify the contributions of socioeconomic, behavioral, functional, and health-related factors to these differences. Data were obtained from 9,590 adults aged ≥65 years who participated in the 2018 wave of the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Sleep duration was self-reported and categorized as short (<6 h), normal (6-8 h), or long (>8 h). Multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with short and long sleep, with weighted analyses and Poisson regression performed as sensitivity analyses. Separate Fairlie decomposition analyses were conducted for short and long sleep to quantify the contributions of observed characteristics to gender differences. Overall, 44.95% of participants had abnormal sleep duration, with a higher prevalence among women than men (46.87% vs. 42.66%, p < 0.001). Compared with men, women had a higher relative risk of short sleep (RRR = 1.399, 95% CI: 1.204-1.625) but a lower relative risk of long sleep (RRR = 0.856, 95% CI: 0.754-0.972). The association with short sleep remained significant in the weighted analysis (RRR = 1.530, 95% CI: 1.210-1.935), whereas the gender difference in long sleep was attenuated (RRR = 0.821, 95% CI: 0.661-1.021). For short sleep, observed characteristics explained 21.65% of the gender disparity. Education (22.75%), depressive symptoms (11.07%), IADL limitation (6.02%), and self-assessed health (4.82%) contributed positively to the disparity, whereas smoking status (-22.57%), drinking status (-12.45%), and exercise (-4.87%) partially offset it. The gender difference in long sleep was negligible, with substantial offsetting contributions across factors. Gender differences in sleep duration among Chinese older adults were primarily concentrated in short sleep, with women experiencing a higher risk. Socioeconomic, behavioral, psychological, and functional characteristics contributed to this disparity, although most of the short-sleep difference remained unexplained. Gender-sensitive interventions addressing educational disadvantage, depressive symptoms, functional limitations, and health behaviors may help reduce inequalities in sleep duration among older adults.

papers.title: Incremental predictive value of multimodal over unimodal assessment for upper limb motor recovery after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Clinical scales predict post-stroke motor recovery but are insensitive to neural substrates. Neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers capture corticospinal integrity, yet their incremental value over clinical assessment remains unquantified. To quantify the pooled incremental predictive value (ΔAUC) of adding biomarkers to clinical models for upper limb motor recovery at 3-6 months post-stroke. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from inception to January 31, 2026, for prospective cohort studies evaluating ≥2 assessment modalities. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled ΔAUC between multimodal and clinical-only models. Sensitivity analyses used alternative between-study variance estimators and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Meta-regression examined sources of heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Twenty-three studies (N = 1,341) were included. Multimodal assessment significantly improved prognostic accuracy over clinical models alone (pooled ΔAUC = +0.112, 95% CI 0.061 to 0.163, p < 0.001). MEP status showed the largest incremental gain (ΔAUC = +0.150, 95% CI 0.023 to 0.277; I 2 = 71.0%). Ipsilesional CST FA was reported in one study (ΔAUC = +0.220, 95% CI 0.110 to 0.330). Other DTI-derived metrics did not reach statistical significance (ΔAUC = +0.074, 95% CI -0.006 to 0.155). Task-based fMRI showed promise in one study (ΔAUC = +0.190, 95% CI 0.088 to 0.292). EEG, kinematic parameters, and resting-state fMRI could not be pooled. Stroke phase was a significant moderator (β = -0.127, 95% CI -0.247 to -0.007, p = 0.039), with larger gains in subacute versus acute assessments. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, adding selected biomarkers to clinical assessment was associated with improved discrimination for upper limb motor recovery after stroke. MEP status showed the largest incremental gain. Stroke phase significantly moderated the incremental value, with larger gains in the subacute phase. However, given the small number of studies and the prediction interval crossing zero, these findings should be considered statistically promising but not yet robust enough to guide routine clinical practice. Further validation in larger prospective cohorts is needed before MEP-guided stratification can be applied clinically. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261288506, Identifier: CRD420261288506.

papers.title: Source-resolved electroencephalogram microstates reveal opposing prefrontal-posterior dynamics and a candidate temporal-to-precuneus pathway in disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Objective and circuit-level biomarkers of consciousness are urgently needed for disorders of consciousness. We recorded high-density electroencephalography from 33 patients with disorders of consciousness (17 vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, 16 minimally conscious state) and 19 healthy controls during rest and auditory stimulation, and combined source-localized microstate analysis with hypothesis-generating Granger causality analysis. Source microstate 3 (right prefrontal) and microstate 4 (parieto-occipital-temporal) showed diametrically opposite dynamics: microstate 3 was enhanced in the vegetative state whereas microstate 4 coverage and occurrence were higher in the minimally conscious state, revealing a fronto-posterior opponent imbalance. In repeated internal cross-validation within this cohort, microstate 4 occurrence discriminated the two patient groups (area under the curve = 0.812, 95% confidence interval 0.647-0.945). Hypothesis-generating connectivity analysis nominally implicated stronger right middle temporal-to-precuneus information flow in the minimally conscious state, a signal that did not survive network-level multiplicity correction. Source-resolved microstates thus reveal opposing cortical dynamics associated with consciousness level.

papers.title: Sleep duration and systemic inflammation assessed using the systemic inflammation response index: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020 and 2021-2023.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the association between usual weekday/workday sleep duration and the systemic inflammation response index among adults reporting at least 7 h of sleep while assessing the influence of questionnaire coding and complex survey design.MethodsThis cross-sectional secondary analysis included 10,971 participants aged ≥18 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey January 2017 to March 2020 and August 2021 to August 2023 cycles. The systemic inflammation response index was calculated as monocyte count × neutrophil count/lymphocyte count. Unweighted pooled linear models were retained as exploratory analyses after correcting smoking skip-pattern and special-response coding; the fully adjusted sample comprised 9051 participants. Survey-weighted regressions were fitted separately by period using the appropriate examination or phlebotomy weight, strata, and primary sampling units. An existing smooth curve was retained for descriptive purposes, not threshold inference.ResultsIn the corrected pooled fully adjusted model, each additional reported hour was associated with a 0.0371 higher systemic inflammation response index (95% confidence interval: 0.0198-0.0544; p < 0.001). The corresponding period-specific survey-weighted estimates were 0.0246 (95% confidence interval: -0.0108, 0.0601; p = 0.165) before the pandemic and 0.0529 (95% confidence interval: 0.0126-0.0933; p = 0.014) in 2021-2023. Fully adjusted log-Systemic inflammation response index analyses did not reach statistical significance (p < 0.05) in either period. The visual downturn near 11 h was not a formally estimated threshold; only 195 participants reported ≥12 h of sleep.ConclusionsLonger reported sleep within the ≥7 h range was positively associated with the systemic inflammation response index in exploratory pooled analyses; however, period-specific and outcome-scale checks did not provide uniformly significant evidence. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality, an optimal sleep duration, or an anti-inflammatory benefit of prolonged sleep duration.
